name: Ziggs
rationale:
Passive bonus damage ratio now flat; maximum damage to structures increased.
Bumping up this bombing bud to better bonk down buildings and, more importantly, to bring an artillery mage into the meta.

lines.raw: AP ratio increased to 50% AP at all levels from 30 to 50% AP.
Bonus damage against structures increased to 150% from 100%.

name: Nimbus Cloak
rationale: Nimbus Cloak has become the go-to for both jungle and AD as a consistent offensive and defensive tool. We’re lowering some of its overall strength, specifically in consideration of Smite and Hexflash, so that it’s not as ubiquitous of a choice.

lines.raw: Bonus movement speed reduced to 10 / 20 / 30% from 15 / 25 / 35%.

lines.attribute: Siege minion: Red side siege minion attack range
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Red side siege minion attack range increased to 300 from 280.

name: Aatrox
rationale:
R Bonus damage ratio increased later.
Aatrox is on the fringes of pro play, hanging on for dear life. Since he’s restrained in that MMR, he has room for us to push him into a much better state for all players.

lines.raw: Bonus attack damage increased to 20 to 40% AD from 20 to 30% AD.

name: Caitlyn
rationale:
Base movement speed decreased.
Caitlyn's 10.15 buffs put her in a bit too domineering of a place for both professional and regular play.

lines.raw: Base movement speed reduced to 325 from 330.

name: Evelynn
rationale:
Q dart and spike base damage decreased.
Our changes last patch gave her a lot of new power in the jungle, so we’re reeling back some of the damage that we gave her earlier in 10.8.

lines.raw: Dart base damage reduced to 25 to 45 from 30 to 50.
Spike base damage reduced to 25 to 45 from 30 to 50.

name: Gragas
rationale:
Base armor increased.
Gragas has been getting thrown around by the jungle, so we’re hoping this change lets him slam right back. With more defense, it should also help out his early game exchanges in the top lane.

lines.raw: Base armor increased to 38 from 35.

name: Hecarim
rationale:
E bonus movement speed maximum reduced.
Trotting back some of the changes from 10.16, which overshot our expectations, especially with Hecarim players picking up on his synergy with Phase Rush.

lines.raw: Bonus movement speed reduced to 25 to 85% from 25 to 100%.

name: Kai'Sa
rationale:
Base AD growth increased. E bonus AS increased later.
Kai’Sa is struggling at all levels of play. Giving her a little bit of a supercharge to help her reach her late game potential.

lines.raw: Attack damage growth increased to 2 from 1.7.
Bonus attack speed increased to 40 to 80% from 40 to 60%.

name: Lux
rationale:
W shield decreased; mana cost no longer static and increased; fixed a bug where W would apply three times.
Lux support, especially with an early shield max, has gained a lot of traction as of late. To curb the oppressive playstyle of just spamming her shield in lane, we’re targeting its power when maxed first, while avoiding hurting her more damage-oriented builds. Also, bugfix for a shieldfix!

lines.raw: Base shield reduced to 45 to 125 from 50 to 150.
AP ratio increased to 35% AP from 30% AP.
Mana cost increased to 60 to 80 from 60 at all ranks.

lines.attribute: No longer grants bonus shielding at the edge.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: No longer grants bonus shielding at the edge.

name: Qiyana
rationale:
W bonus AD ratio decreased. E base damage decreased later.
Qiyana has been riding a high wave in elite play, and although we’ve been able to avoid nerfing her due to her lack of presence in pro, the tide’s turned this time.

lines.raw: Bonus AD ratio reduced to 10% bonus AD from 20%.
Base damage reduced to 60 to 180 from 60 to 200.

name: Sona
rationale:
Base health and mana decreased. Q damage ratio decreased. W heal ratio decreased. E self and aura bonus movement speed decreased.
Sona’s power has reached a crescendo as a support and bot lane carry across skilled, elite, and average levels of play. We can’t keep babying our baby girl any longer—we’re toning down her power by bringing down her scaling.

lines.raw: Base health reduced to 480 from 482.36.
Base mana reduced to 340 from 340.6.
Active AP ratio reduced to 40% AP from 50% AP.
Heal AP ratio reduced to 20% AP from 25% AP.

lines.attribute: Self bonus movement speed AP ratio
lines.raw: Self bonus movement speed AP ratio reduced to 2% per 100 AP from 3% per 100 AP.

lines.attribute: Ally bonus movement speed AP ratio
lines.raw: Ally bonus movement speed AP ratio reduced to 2% per 100 AP from 3% per 100 AP.

name: Varus
rationale:
Base AS growth increased.
Our last wave of changes in 10.14 knocked Varus completely out of the meta. He’s in a weak spot at all levels of play, so we’re cautiously giving him a helping hand.

lines.raw: Attack speed growth increased to 4% from 3%.

lines.attribute: Bonus attack speed ratio on champion takedown
lines.old: 30% bonus attack speed from non-growth sources at all levels
lines.raw: Bonus attack speed ratio on champion takedown increased to 30 to 35.1% bonus attack speed from 30% bonus attack speed from non-growth sources at all levels.

lines.attribute: Bonus attack speed ratio on non-champion kill
lines.old: 15% bonus attack speed from non-growth sources at all levels
lines.raw: Bonus attack speed ratio on non-champion kill increased to 15 to 17.55% bonus attack speed from 15% bonus attack speed from non-growth sources at all levels.

name: Xayah
rationale:
Base AD growth increased.
Xayah has been struggling to keep up with her counterparts, so we’re fluffing up her feathers and giving her a little more swish as the game progresses.

lines.raw: Attack damage growth increased to 3.5 from 2.9.

name: Yone
rationale:
Q base damage decreased later. R no longer applies life steal.
While not currently overpowered, we expect Yone isn’t long-term balanced and will continue to grow from where he is—and where he is the strongest.

lines.raw: Base damage reduced to 20 to 100 from 20 to 120.
Removed: No longer benefits from lifesteal.

name: Ahri
rationale:
Passive replaced with Q passive, where now any spell can heal. W now grants movement speed, deals 200% damage to low-health minions, and better targets low-health minions.
Ahri's identity and gameplay have become a little muddled over time, and she isn’t as charming as we’d like her to be. We’re making some kit changes, especially to her W, to reinforce an identity of a flighty mage who can weave in and out of fights as she looks for the perfect moment to strike. In addition, we’re also shifting her Essence thievery from her Q to her passive to open up more opportunities for her to reap its healing rewards when trading with enemy champions. Altogether, she should feel equipped to (spirit) rush into more combos and outplays.

lines.raw: Base health regeneration reduced to 5.5 from 6.5.

lines.raw: Renamed Essence Theft from Vastayan Grace.

name: Ashe
rationale:
Base attack damage decreased.
Ashe has remained one of the primary marksmen in Pro play, so we’re icing some of her power.

lines.raw: Base attack damage reduced to 59 from 61.

lines.attribute: Runaan's Hurricane Wind's Fury's damage now properly takes under consideration the future levels of Ranger's Focus.

We’re heating things up by giving Rumble a jump start that’ll hopefully park him as another good early game Pro pick option.

name: Sett
rationale:
Passive right punch changed to scale with bonus attack damage. Q bonus damage ratio of target’s maximum health now fixed; bonus damage ratio per 100 total attack damage now scales.
Sett’s continued to muscle his way through Pro levels of play, especially with low-economy tank and utility builds. Since our previous nerf to his base values wasn't sufficient, we're taking a larger swing at him. To do this, we’re adjusting how he scales with damage and gold to incentivize players to swap to damage-oriented builds instead. Expect another check in after Worlds to make sure he’s… well, all set.

name: Shyvana
rationale:
E dragon form explosion radius increased; dragon form visuals and cast indicator now accurately represents the ability’s hit radius; dragon form ground zone damage tick rate decreased.
In fixing a minor Shyvana clarity bug, we uncovered other levers to polish up. The result is a major clarity fix and thus a minor balance change. Previously, dragon Shyvana's radius on her E scaled with her Flame Breath rank-ups, but this effect was not accurately represented in her visuals or the tooltip. We’ve decided to remove it, as the reliability of an important spell should not change dramatically throughout the game. Overall, we expect these changes to be a small nerf to AP Shyvana, a small buff to AD Shyvana, and a large increase to Flame Breath's clarity.

Q base damage and AD ratio decreased.

name: Azir
rationale:
W bonus AS decreased.
Azir has (a)risen to the upper tier of mages in Pro play, and has become the de facto option for scaling compositions. Since pro players are able to get more 3-soldier autos off than in lower MMR (thus proccing doubled bonus attack speed), we’re bringing down the ratio.

rationale:
Base AD and AS growth decreased.
Caitlyn has been dominating and we're not confident that even with our previous nerfs there'd be a level playing field. It feels bad to put extra cuffs on the sheriff, but it seems it's prudent in order to open up bottom lane diversity for our most important tournament.

name: Senna
rationale:
Mist Wraith drop chance on minion kills decreased.
Senna has been stepping into the limelight, both as a bot lane carry and as a utility-first marksman in the Pro meta. We’re reducing her scaling via Mist Wraiths to grant more leeway to other traditional hypercarries.

lines.attribute: Mist Wraith spawn rate on minion and lesser monster kills
lines.raw: Mist Wraith spawn rate on minion and lesser monster kills reduced to 4.166% from 8.33%.

name: Sivir
rationale:
Passive bonus MS increased.
Sivir’s fallen off the radar, so we’re increasing her ability to hunt down enemies in the hopes that she boomerangs back into power.

lines.raw: Bonus movement speed increased to 35 to 55 from 30 to 50.

name: Sylas
rationale:
R cooldown decreased later.
Sylas has been shackled in Pro play due to having a weaker laning phase and stronger counterpicks. This will allow us now to amplify his real niche of snatching an ultimate here and an ultimate there, which means...he's getting Hijacked up.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 100 to 40 seconds from 100 to 60.

lines.attribute: Pool Party Syndra: Force of Will: Range indicator is no longer missing.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Range indicator is no longer missing.

name: Twisted Fate
rationale:
Base MS reduced.
Twisted Fate remains a meta-driving force in Pro play as a safe roamer, so we’re paring down some of that.

lines.raw: Base movement speed reduced to 330 from 335.

name: Udyr
rationale:
R cone damage increased.
Tiger Stance tends to be the go-to for Udyr players, so we’re giving a bit more bite (and burn) to his Phoenix Stance and its AoE damage playstyle.

lines.raw: Cone base damage increased to 60 to 310 from 50 to 275.
AP ratio increased to 70% AP from 60% AP.

name: Vayne
rationale:
R bonus AD increased.
Vayne has been in the shadows as of late and hasn’t been succeeding in places she traditionally has, so we’re heightening Vayne's window of power by letting her excel in the moments you pick her for.

lines.raw: Bonus attack damage increased to 35 to 65 from 25 to 55.

lines.attribute: Allied party indicator no longer displays green when on cooldown.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Allied party indicator no longer displays green when on cooldown.

lines.attribute: Cooldown tooltip now properly updates when using Cosmic Insight.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Cooldown tooltip now properly updates when using Cosmic Insight.

name: Aatrox
rationale:
R self-healing increased later.
Aatrox wants to step into his full potential as the unkillable DPS monster, so we’re helping him harness his darkin power by curbing some of his mid- to late-game falloff. Hopefully now this warrior demon won’t fall flat in late game teamfights.

lines.raw: Healing amplification increased to 50 to 100% from 50 to 70%.

name: Braum
rationale:
Q base damage increased; cost decreased.
We’re giving Braum a little more agency in solo queue with some extra damage and lower mana costs.

lines.raw: Base damage increased to 75 to 275 from 60 to 260.
Mana cost reduced to 45 to 65 from 55 to 75.

lines.attribute: Corrected the cooldown tooltip from 2 seconds to 1.5 seconds.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Corrected the cooldown tooltip from 2 seconds to 1.5 seconds.

name: Illaoi
rationale:
Passive tentacle spawn cooldown decreased.
Illaoi has been flailing around top lane, so we’re giving her tentacles more oomph, especially post laning phase. We’re also smoothing out her passive scaling so that she gets some benefit every level instead of every two.

lines.ability: Passive - Prophet of an Elder God
lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 20 to 7.25 seconds from 20 to 12.

lines.attribute: No longer destroys enemies' spell shields and now always deals full damage to the targeted enemy.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: No longer destroys enemies' spell shields and now always deals full damage to the targeted enemy.

lines.attribute: Lulu team can no longer get permanent vision of an area if she is cloned by Test of Spirit and dies while Help, Pix! is activated on Lulu.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Lulu team can no longer get permanent vision of an area if she is cloned by Test of Spirit and dies while Help, Pix! is activated on Lulu.

name: Karthus
rationale:
Base armor decreased.
We're continuing to tweak Karthus to get him into a comfortable place since he’s been a bit overwhelming across the map, especially in bot lane. Aiming to bring down his defenses against ADCs.

lines.raw: Base armor reduced to 18 from 20.88.

name: Kassadin
rationale:
Q shield decreased early.
Kassadin players in Skilled/Elite are too often able to stonewall lanes and scale with their early defensive tools. Many have started maxing E first, so we're pushing Kassadin to have to invest more for a safer laning phase.

lines.raw: Base shield strength reduced to 40 to 160 from 60 to 160.

name: Katarina
rationale:
Dagger retrieval damage ratio decreased.
Katarina has risen in the ranks in Skilled and Elite games as a swift assassin who can secure snowball advantages with early roams, so we’re targeting her AD ratios to lower some of her early threat.

lines.raw: Bonus AD ratio reduced to 75% bonus AD from 100%.

lines.attribute: Odyssey Kayn: Fixed a bug where he would expand and shrink when an enemy player highlighted him.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where he would expand and shrink when an enemy player highlighted him.

name: Kled
rationale:
Base magic resistance decreased.
Kled has been a strong force in both mid and top lane at all levels of play, so we want to open up more avenues to knock this yordle off his high horse lizard.

lines.raw: Base magic resistance reduced to 28 from 32.1.

name: Lulu
rationale:
W bonus attack speed decreased.
Lulu has seen wild growth in the bot lane by helping carries out a pinch too much. Since she’s both a strong offensive and defensive support, we're toning down her combative scaling on Whimsy in the late game.

lines.raw: Bonus attack speed reduced to 20 to 35% from 25 to 45%.

lines.attribute: Her team can no longer get permanent vision of an area if she is cloned by Test of Spirit and dies while Help, Pix! is activated on her.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Her team can no longer get permanent vision of an area if she is cloned by Test of Spirit and dies while Help, Pix! is activated on her.

lines.attribute: Can no longer slow her enemies for a longer period than intended when she reactivates it mid-air.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Can no longer slow her enemies for a longer period than intended when she reactivates it mid-air.

name: Maokai
rationale:
Q base damage decreased later.
We’re cutting down some of Maokai’s brawling power to give his top lane peers some space to come out of the woods.

lines.raw: Base damage reduced to 70 to 230 from 70 to 250.

name: Nunu
rationale:
Base armor decreased.
Nunu's skirmishing power is a little too strong when coupled with his top-tier gank presence and objective control. Weakening some of that strength so he rolls over junglers a little less.

lines.raw: Base armor reduced to 29 from 32.

lines.attribute: Winter Wonder Orianna: Command: Shockwave: Sparkles VFX no longer render over structures.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Sparkles VFX no longer render over structures.

name: Ryze
rationale:
Q base damage increased.
Since he’s recently escaped from his Worlds rune prison, we're ready to overload Ryze in preparation for the offseason.

lines.raw: Base damage increased to 75 to 175 from 65 to 165.

name: Sion
rationale:
Q damage ratio to monsters increased.
Sion could use a little help in the jungle, so we’re charging up his Q. A fun bonus: now he can slay baby Raptors more efficiently with his Q+W combo.

lines.attribute: Now deals 50% bonus damage against monsters.
lines.raw: New Effect: Now deals 50% bonus damage against monsters.

lines.attribute: No longer loses all of his mana after stealing Dragon's Descent.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: No longer loses all of his mana after stealing Dragon's Descent.

name: Urgot
rationale:
Passive damage to monsters increased early. W modified damage now affects both minions and monsters.
The jungle could juggle a few more juggernauts, and Urgot has what it takes to be a viable pick. We’re beefing up this beefy man’s damage against monsters.

lines.raw: Damage cap against monsters increased to 100 to 360 from 60 to 360.

lines.attribute: Now deals a minimum of 50 damage against monsters.
lines.raw: New Effect: Now deals a minimum of 50 damage against monsters.

name: Varus
rationale:
E base damage increased. R cooldown decreased.
After a long time spreading corruption at the highest tiers of play, Varus has fallen and once again has room for buffs.

lines.raw: Base damage increased to 60 to 220 from 50 to to.
Cooldown reduced to 120 to 60 seconds from 130 to 70.

lines.attribute: The sound that plays when she enters stealth no longer cuts off from the enemy perspective.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: The sound that plays when she enters stealth no longer cuts off from the enemy perspective.

lines.attribute: PROJECT Vayne: When hit by an enemy, she will now make metallic sounds instead of the normal blood/flesh sounds.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: When hit by an enemy, she will now make metallic sounds instead of the normal blood/flesh sounds.

lines.attribute: Corrected the tooltip to include information about his healing reduction versus minions.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Corrected the tooltip to include information about his healing reduction versus minions.

lines.attribute: Arcanist Zoe and Prestige Arcanist Zoe: Sleepy Trouble Bubble: AoE VFX now properly match the full duration of the ability.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: AoE VFX now properly match the full duration of the ability.

lines.attribute: Certain empowered basic attacks no longer grant double Conqueror stacks when the champion in question has Dead Man's Plate.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Certain empowered basic attacks no longer grant double Conqueror stacks when the champion in question has Dead Man's Plate.

name: Relentless Hunter
rationale: Relentless Hunter is massively outperforming other runes, especially in Skilled mid lanes. We’re bringing down its reliability and reducing some of its base power.

lines.raw: Bonus movement speed reduced to 5 from 10.
Bonus movement speed per stack reduced to 8 from 9.
Maximum bonus movement speed reduced to 45 from 55.

lines.attribute: Certain empowered basic attacks no longer grant double Conqueror stacks when the champion in question has Dead Man's Plate.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Certain empowered basic attacks no longer grant double Conqueror stacks when the champion in question has Dead Man's Plate.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where it would not apply through AoE damage abilities.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where it would not apply through AoE damage abilities.

name: Aphelios
rationale:
Passive lethality increased. R Calibrum additional mark damage increased; Severum heal increased, Gravitum root duration increased, Infernum splash damage ratio increased, Crescendum additional chakrams returned increased.
We aren’t seeing Aphelios on the Worlds stage, so it’s time for us to take a moonshot at propping him back up for all other levels of play. We’re giving him extra oomph on the ranking of his Lethality and sharpening the strengths of his various ultimates.

lines.ability: Passive - The Hitman and the Seer
lines.raw: Lethality increased to 3 to 18 from 2 to 12.
Calibrum mark damage increased to 40 to 100 from 20 to 70.
Severum heal increased to 250 to 500 from 200 to 400.

lines.attribute: Now increases Binding Eclipse root duration to 1.25 seconds if slowed while empowered by Gravitum.
lines.raw: New Effect: Now increases Binding Eclipse root duration to 1.25 seconds if slowed while empowered by Gravitum.
Infernum splash damage increased to 85% from 75%.
Bonus Crescendum chakrams increased to 4 from 3.

name: Camille
rationale:
E bonus attack speed decreased later.
Camille is one of the strongest and most prevalent top laners in Elite play, so we're pulling some power out of her split-pushing and sustained-dueling potential.

lines.raw: Bonus attack speed reduced to 40 to 60% from 40 to 80%.

name: Corki
rationale:
Q bonus damage ratio increased.
Corki's early game makes it hard for him to stand up to other mid laners. Giving him a small boost to help him take off a little faster.

lines.raw: Bonus AD ratio increased to 70% bonus AD from 50%.

name: Graves
rationale:
E bonus armor decreased.
Graves' combination of clear speed and durability have made him a prominent Elite jungle pick. Reducing some of his innate tankiness so that Graves is more punishable when he missteps.

lines.raw: Bonus armor per stack reduced to 6 to 18 from 8 to 20.
Maximum bonus armor reduced to 6*8 to 18*8 from 8*8 to 20*8.

name: Hecarim
rationale:
E base damage decreased.
Bringing down some burst from this speeding stallion.

lines.raw: Minimum base damage reduced to 35 to 155 from 45 to 165.
Maximum base damage reduced to 70 to 310 from 90 to 330.

name: Karma
rationale:
Mantra cooldown refund for abilities increased later; Mantra cooldown refund for basic attacks now flat. R cooldown decreased.
A new mantra for Karma: to channel her Mantra more often. We’re increasing the payoff for dishing out damage so Karma can optimize access to her Mantra.

lines.raw: Mantra cooldown reduction from spells increased to 2 to 5 seconds from 2 to 4.

lines.attribute: Mantra cooldown reduction from basic attacks
lines.raw: Mantra cooldown reduction from basic attacks reduced to 1 second at all levels from 1 to 2.
Cooldown reduced to 40 to 34 seconds from 45 to 36.

name: Lee Sin
rationale:
Base attack damage growth increased.
The monk could use more reliable damage to see games through.

lines.raw: Attack damage growth increased to 3.7 from 3.2.

lines.attribute: Corrected the AP ratio in the tooltip from 150% AP to 50% AP.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Corrected the AP ratio in the tooltip from 150% AP to 50% AP.

name: Nidalee
rationale:
Base attack damage decreased.
Bringing down the jungle cat’s early clear and dueling. This should be especially impactful in Elite play, where autos and attack range are utilized more effectively.

lines.raw: Base attack damage reduced to 58 from 61.

name: Pantheon
rationale:
Q damage and critical damage decreased; damage and critical damage ratios increased; Mortal Will bonus damage ratio increased.
Support Pantheon has spiked in popularity as a shield-swinging strongman who provides solid CC and durability. To balance his resilience, we’re moving some power from his base damage to his AD ratios over time. This should weaken the early kill threat from low-income supports while padding the blow for solo-lane Pantheons who have quicker access to items.

lines.raw: Base damage reduced to 70 to 190 from 75 to 215.
Bonus AD ratio increased to 115% bonus AD from 100%.
Increased base damage reduced to 155 to 455 from 155 to 475.
Increased bonus AD ratio increased to 230% bonus AD from 200%.
Mortal Will bonus AD ratio increased to 115% bonus AD from 100%.

name: Samira
rationale:
E cooldown increased; attack speed decreased.
Samira is at a place where her early game safety and mobility is a touch too reliable, so we’re bumping up her cooldown in a way so that she has to play more conservatively in the first stages of the game. We’re also trimming some of her damage so that her all ins are a little less potent.

lines.raw: Cooldown increased to 20 to 12 seconds from 15 to 11.
Bonus attack speed reduced to 20 to 40% from 30 to 50%.

lines.attribute: PsyOps Sona: Crescendo: Now correctly plays her transformation animation even when moving while leveling up Crescendo.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Now correctly plays her transformation animation even when moving while leveling up Crescendo.

name: Trundle
rationale:
Passive heal from nearby enemy death increased and now smoothly scales across levels. W cooldown now reduces with rank.
Smoothing out this pillar-punching prince’s passive so he doesn’t hit arbitrary power spikes at various levels, and throwing in a small buff at every level to help him bash down enemies. In combination with an increase in his steroid uptime, we’re hoping this will tip the scales in favor for macho Trundles to really win fights.

lines.raw: Healing increased to 2 to 7% of enemies maximum health from 2 to 6%.
Cooldown reduced to 15 to 11 seconds from 15 at all ranks.

name: Udyr
rationale:
R aura total damage increased.
Bird Udyr is still performing worse than Cat Udyr, so we’re firing up Phoenix Stance’s AoE damage to sharpen the difference in style between the two stances (Phoenix’s waveclear vs. Tiger’s dueling potential), and encourage more folks to birdy up.

lines.raw: Aura base damage increased to 50 to 300 from 40 to 240.

lines.attribute: Added a yellow ring under targets affected by the passive to match similar passive indicators on Jarvan IV, Ekko, and Shaco.
lines.raw: Added a yellow ring under targets affected by the passive to match similar passive indicators on Jarvan IV, Ekko, and Shaco.

name: Nimbus Cloak
rationale: Nimbus Cloak’s popularity has begun to stifle rune choices, especially in the jungle. We’re weakening its power overall, with a specific target on its synergy with Smite.

lines.raw: Bonus movement speed changed to 5 / 20 / 35% from 10 / 20 / 30%.
Duration reduced to 2 seconds from 2.5.

lines.attribute: Recast will no longer fizzle if she tries to reactivate it too quickly after marking her Twilight Shroud.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Recast will no longer fizzle if she tries to reactivate it too quickly after marking her Twilight Shroud.

name: Amumu
rationale:
R now stuns enemies.
Improving clarity on Amumu’s ult, which should also lead to a minor bump up in his mojo.

lines.ability: R - Curse of the Sad Mummy
lines.raw: New Effect: Now stuns enemies for 2 seconds.

lines.ability: R - Curse of the Sad Mummy
lines.attribute: No longer disarms and roots enemies for 2 seconds.
lines.raw: Removed: No longer disarms and roots enemies for 2 seconds.

name: Annie
rationale:
E now provides a shield instead of damage reduction; shield can now be cast on target ally champions; shield animation updated; cost and range increased; shield always applies to Tibbers when he's summoned
We’re giving Annie more ways to use her shield while keeping it a simple and intuitive defense when Annie just wants to play on her own.

lines.raw: Mana cost increased to 40 from 20.

lines.attribute: New Active: Annie grants herself or an ally within 800 units, and Tibbers a shield for 40 to 240 (+ 40% AP) for 3 seconds and 30 to 60% bonus movement speed that decays over 1.5 seconds. While the shield is active, enemies who basic attack it take 20 to 60 (+ 20% AP) magic damage.
lines.raw: New Active: Annie grants herself or an ally within 800 units, and Tibbers a shield for 40 to 240 (+ 40% AP) for 3 seconds and 30 to 60% bonus movement speed that decays over 1.5 seconds. While the shield is active, enemies who basic attack it take 20 to 60 (+ 20% AP) magic damage.

lines.raw: Casts on ally if targeted or if very close to targeting them (within a range of 225); otherwise self casts.

Enemies that damage Annie or Tibbers with basic attacks during this time are dealt 20 to 60 (+ 20% AP) magic damage.
lines.raw: Old Active: Annie wraps herself and Tibbers in a fiery aura, gaining 30 to 60% bonus movement speed that decays over 1.5 seconds, and reducing damage taken by 13 to 29% for 3 seconds. Enemies that damage Annie or Tibbers with basic attacks during this time are dealt 20 to 60 (+ 20% AP) magic damage.

lines.attribute: New range indicator for Tibbers that snap back when exceeding its range. The indicator is centered around Tibbers and only appears when he is within 500 range of the teleport leash.
lines.raw: New Effect: New range indicator for Tibbers that snap back when exceeding its range. The indicator is centered around Tibbers and only appears when he is within 500 range of the teleport leash.

lines.attribute: Sentries are no longer pushed towards Sion when he casts Roar of the Slayer.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Sentries are no longer pushed towards Sion when he casts Roar of the Slayer.

name: Ashe
rationale:
W arrows now increase per rank-up.
Adding more satisfaction and experiential variety to her main skill to get more bang for your buck rank ups.

lines.raw: Number of arrows changed to 7 to 11 from 9 at all ranks.

name: Brand
rationale:
Passive explosion damage decreased. E blaze spread now always spreads to nearby enemies; blaze spread radius increased; indicator now displays blaze spread radius. R fireball can now bounce back to Brand; bounce priority updated.
Once upon a time, Brand was a mid laner—but in recent history, he’s found a comfortable home as a support. To give him some steam, we’re firing up his offense to promote a more aggressive playstyle. In addition, we tapped down the percentage damage that support Brands typically rely on in order to even out his overall power. Altogether, this should help Brand feel equipped to blaze back into mid without overstepping his current strength as a support.

lines.raw: Explosion base damage reduced to 10 to 14% maximum health from 12 to 16%.
Explosion AP ratio increased to 2% per 100 AP from 1.5% per 100 AP.

lines.attribute: Conflagration now always spreads to nearby targets.
lines.raw: New Effect: Conflagration now always spreads to nearby targets.
Spread radius reduced to 300 units from 375.

lines.attribute: Blaze now increases Conflagration's spread radius to 600 units.
lines.raw: New Effect: Blaze now increases Conflagration's spread radius to 600 units.

lines.attribute: Now displays a brief indicator for the spread range.
lines.raw: New Effect: Now displays a brief indicator for the spread range.

lines.attribute: Can now bounce back to Brand. Bounces off Brand "sticks" to him slightly longer to temper 0-distance instant bursts.
lines.raw: New Effect: Can now bounce back to Brand. Bounces off Brand "sticks" to him slightly longer to temper 0-distance instant bursts.

lines.attribute: Bounce priority is now enemy champions, then Brand, then any valid bounce target.
lines.raw: Bounce priority is now enemy champions, then Brand, then any valid bounce target.

lines.attribute: SFX are no longer audible in Fog of War.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: SFX are no longer audible in Fog of War.

name: Galio
rationale:
E now has a minimum dash distance.
A consistency change to ensure players don’t accidentally zero-cast their dash, while also giving Galio’s enemies more opportunities to dodge it.

lines.attribute: Now has a minimum 250 dash distance (starting from E origination, not the dashback).
lines.raw: New Effect: Now has a minimum 250 dash distance (starting from E origination, not the dashback).

name: Jinx
rationale:
E now deals all damage upfront.
This clarity tweak on Jinx’s Chompers should provide more visible and appreciable damage.

lines.attribute: Now deals its damage instantly instead of over 1.5 seconds.
lines.raw: New Effect: Now deals its damage instantly instead of over 1.5 seconds.

lines.attribute: Pinging her abilities when they're evolved will note it in chat.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Pinging her abilities when they're evolved will note it in chat.

name: Karthus
rationale:
Q base damage reduced.
Karthus is too reliable of a jungle, mid, and bot pick because he can permashove waves and permaclear camps with little to no cost. We’re lowering his ability to deal sustained damage and gain massive leads so that his opponents have a chance to fight back.

lines.raw: Base damage reduced to 45 to 125 from 50 to 130.

lines.attribute: PsyOps Kayle: Divine Judgment: No longer triggers a series of flashes across the screen when activated.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: No longer triggers a series of flashes across the screen when activated.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where successfully hunted champions could be marked again without a 4 minute timer.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where successfully hunted champions could be marked again without a 4 minute timer.

name: LeBlanc
rationale:
E cost decreased; E base damage increased; E delayed damage increased.
Smoke and mirrors aside, LeBlanc has been in a weak spot across all levels of play. We’re giving her another trick up her sleeve by jazzing up one of her more underwhelming and underappreciated abilities. This should encourage players to rely more on her E, which is often left at rank one until late in the game.

lines.raw: Mana cost reduced to 50 from 70.
Initial base damage increased to 50 to 130 from 40 to 120.
Delayed base damage increased to 80 to 240 from 70 to 230.
Bug Fix: Fixed some ability queueing issues.

name: Lulu
rationale:
Q base damage decreased later.
Top Lulu has been doing too well in Skilled play, and all that glitters is not gold. We’re reducing her scaling damage to mitigate her ability to consistently harass opponents and waveclear.

lines.raw: Base damage reduced to 80 to 220 from 80 to 260.

name: Nasus
rationale:
R bonus resistances increased; bonus resistances per second removed.
One more clarity check, this time to make Nasus’ ultimate feel more intuitive. We also don’t think he’d be able to resist the overall buff.

lines.raw: Initial resistances increased to 40 to 70 from 15 to 55.

lines.attribute: No longer gains 1 to 3 resistances each second.
lines.raw: Removed: No longer gains 1 to 3 resistances each second.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug with the warning SFX and his growl SFX when near targets.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug with the warning SFX and his growl SFX when near targets.

name: Samira
rationale:
Base attack damage and armor reduced.
Samira has quickly made her mark as a powerhouse ADC who can effortlessly slash, bash, and dash into a snowbally lead. We’re pulling out some of her early brawling power to reduce her reliability.

lines.raw: Base attack damage reduced to 57 from 59.
Base armor reduced 26 from 28.

name: Sejuani
rationale:
R base and max damage increased.
The jungle meta has turned a cold shoulder to Sejuani. It's finally time to give our favorite boar some love and release Sejuani and Bristle from their cages glacial prison.

lines.raw: Base damage increased to 125 to 175 from 100 to 150.
Empowered and explosion base damage increased to 200 to 400 from 150 to 350.

name: Seraphine
rationale:
The Starry-Eyed Songstress
Runeterra's premier idol takes the stage in 10.22!
High-res versions of Seraphine's splashes are available on League Displays!

name: Aegis of the Legion
rationale:
Epic items are the tier below Legendary: They're the mid-tier components of Legendary and Mythic items that build out of basic items. We're ensuring they serve their role as valuable building blocks, offering incremental stats and effects that smooth your progression toward bigger purchases. Like the Legendaries, we're providing blank-slate presentations of these Epics to give you a clean read on when you'll want to pick them up. New and updated have been mixed together since there aren't as many.
Like Legendaries, some Epics are getting simple tuning passes, based on how we want you to build into the new and updated Legendary and Mythic items.

rationale:
Now grants on-hit damage based on critical strike chance, but you can't crit. No longer grants stacking attack speed. No longer grants attack damage, ability power, or penetration.
On-hit builds didn't have many build options since so much of the attack-focused portion of the shop is focused on the crit system. Rather than continue to have on-hit and crit continue fighting for item niches, Guinsoo's Rageblade now acts as a bridge between the crit and on-hit ecosystems, allowing Kog'Maws to access effects like Phantom Dancer or Runaan's Hurricane without wasting stats.

Like the Legendaries, we're providing blank-slate presentations of these Epics to give you a clean read on when you'll want to pick them up. rationale: Marksman champions suffer from awkward early-game components that leave them missing either attack damage or attack speed, both of which are critical for them to feel powerful. So, we created Noonquiver-an Epic that specifically builds into marksman Mythics and features both stats. Noonquiver also amplifies marksman PvE capabilities to provide the early lane management marksman champions crave without sending their PvP power over the top. Lastly, by giving it a smooth build path of smaller parts, it avoids the lane snowballing issue B.F. Sword had if you were forced to back before saving up 1300 gold.

name: Quicksilver Sash
rationale:
Epic items are the tier below Legendary: They're the mid-tier components of Legendary and Mythic items that build out of basic items. We're ensuring they serve their role as valuable building blocks, offering incremental stats and effects that smooth your progression toward bigger purchases. Like the Legendaries, we're providing blank-slate presentations of these Epics to give you a clean read on when you'll want to pick them up. New and updated have been mixed together since there aren't as many.
Like Legendaries, some Epics are getting simple tuning passes, based on how we want you to build into the new and updated Legendary and Mythic items.

name: Varus
rationale:
Q Blight detonation cooldown reduction removed; damage from Blight effects detonated with Q are now increased by the amount of time Varus charges it for, up to 50%; Q now shows crit text when fully charged. W bonus damage reduced; detonating a Blight stack on enemy champions and Epic Monsters now reduces all basic cooldowns by 12% of the max cooldown per stack. R now snaps Varus to face the target direction on start of cast; missile speed reduced.
As a consistent high-priority pick in Pro play, Varus’ tuning has often left players feeling unsatisfied. To bring him back with vengeance, we’re shifting power away from elements that are typically strong in Pro play—such as reliable CC and lane bullying—and back into Varus’ unique playstyle of charged arrows and spellweaving.

name: Pantheon
rationale:
Realigning Pantheon to better support the various roles he's been taking on the Rift.
Pantheon's last overhaul was aimed at bringing new life to an old top lane mainstay. With time and professional play, his rework shifted gears to mid, and then to support. While we love seeing players innovate and journey with the champion, we can't ignore the growing sentiment of folks missing the old champion they love, and we think it's worthwhile to bring Pantheon back to his original home. With that being said, the intent of these changes isn't to destroy support Pantheon, but rather to adjust that role's power, while also giving a boost to the tools that'll finally let old-school Pantheon fans successfully play him in top, and even mid lane, as promised years ago. TL;DR, we're shifting more power into a bruiser-y playstyle by giving him a higher uptime on his Q and equipping him with more selfish outputs like armor penetration at the cost of utility (i.e. strong invulnerability), slows, and most importantly, a massive movement speed boost for when he crashes onto the scene.

rationale:
W healing from monsters increased; now deals bonus damage to monsters.
Big cat and the following champs (forgive us for the non-alphabetized order here) came out of the preseason changes sorely missing the old Tiamat, so we're making adjustments for them. Rengar in particular took a massive clear speed hit, so we're bringing that back up.

Passive updated to extend Knock Up duration on already knocked up enemies. Q and R life steal effectiveness decreased. Q crit bugfix.
Samira's win rate isn't over the line, but her ban rate certainly is, which indicates an issue with game health. Cutting a frustrating knock up mechanic and the hard synergy she gained with new items.

rationale:
Base health growth increased. W self-shield increased.
Seraphine is currently feeling a lot of weakness against more aggressive opponents (i.e. Zed, Fizz, Akali) in the midlane. So much so that it's driving players away from playing her there. We're giving her a little more durability so that she can survive longer and more successfully in 1v1s.

name: Talon
rationale:
W return damage increased later.
Talon's ability to roam is contingent on his ability to clear waves. And his ability to clear waves was too reliant on Tiamat. While his lethality build suffered a lot, he's starting to move out of assassin items into Goredrinker and Ravenous, so we're only giving him a small buff for now.

lines.raw: Return base damage increased to 45 to 145 from 45 to 125.

name: Twitch
rationale:
Q attack speed increased. W slow increased. R bonus damage increased.
Both AP and AD Twitch are significantly underperforming. Our goals are for both to be viable ways to play him, but to stay true to his original gameplay design, we don't necessarily want his AP gameplay to be stronger than AD. For now, we're going to be buffing him in both styles of play, but it is possible that we will need further tuning adjustments as players get used to AP Twitch.

rationale:

rationale:

Elise has crept to the top of the jungle echelons despite some previous nerfs (see 11.2). We're squashing her down a bit to even out the playing field.

name: Ezreal
rationale:
Q damage ratio increased.
Ezreal hasn't been faring so well with the new item system. To give him more of a (mystic) shot, we're buffing his Q ratio to better synergize with Muramana, while also giving him more value when building heavy AD items like Hydra.

name: Ivern
rationale:
Base health growth decreased. E shield decreased later.
While it's great to see Ivern wunder-ing around outside of his usual home, he's still too effective meandering around the jungle. We can't beat around the bush any longer-we're pulling back some of his safety and shielding power.

lines.raw: Health growth reduced to 85 from 95.
Base shield reduced to 80 to 200 from 80 to 220.

name: Jinx
rationale:
Base health decreased. Q bonus range increased; Fishbones bonus attack speed penalty decreased. E cost increased; arm time decreased; max range cast adjusted.
The new item changes have not been kind to Jinx. We wanted to make some priority adjustments to the items in general first before tackling her, and now it's finally time. Additionally, since she's been primarily out of pro play for a while now, we're shifting some of her kit's power from raw stats to her abilities to create more room for skill expression.

name: Mordekaiser
rationale:
E cooldown decreased.
Morde isn't grasping the new season well, so we're giving him more grasp. We're hoping this along with other system changes (Riftmaker giving more health, AD bruiser items getting nerfed) will help him navigate this strange new world.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 22 to 10 seconds from 24 to 12.

rationale:
Base health decreased. Passive bonus attack speed decreased; now displays amount of attack speed on passive icon.

name: Rammus
rationale:
E cooldown flattened.
Rammus rolled comfortably into preseason and has gained more momentum with the cheaper tank Mythic items. We're reducing some of his taunt power now that his engages have become more consistent.

W1 and W2 damage ratio increased. E damage ratio increased; unbind cooldown decreased; cooldown bug fixed; long distance pathing bug fixed. R damage ratio increased.

name: Riven
rationale:
E cooldown decreased.
The new season put Riven in a weak spot, and with high cooldowns on her E, she's lost her mojo. Since both of her hardbound items (Goredrinker/Ravenous Hydra) are getting substantial nerfs this patch, we're looking to reforge her spirit.

name: Seraphine
rationale:

Seraphine is often front and center, and with her strong stage presence in mid lane (and other roles), she's in need of some tuning down.

While AD Shyvana has been tearing up the Rift with both fighter and tank builds, AP Shyv has been dragging (dragon?) behind in the new season. We want to buff AP Shyvana in ways that aren't centered around her just spamming fireballs. These changes should help her clear speed, which is weaker with the new items.

rationale:

Udyr is another dominant jungler at the moment, especially with a Phoenix max. His items are already getting hit, so this nerf is aimed to be lighter than what he would normally merit.

We’ve noticed that players really enjoy playing on-hit builds with these champions, and even if they’re not on-meta, we believe they should be viable. Prior to the Kraken changes, a significant number of Katarina’s and Urgot’s builds were on-hit, but they also had significantly lower win rates in comparison to their traditional build. These changes should bring those builds up to roughly where they were before.

name: Samira
rationale:
Passive bonus damage ratio decreased early and now scales. Q damage ratio decreased early and now scales. W duration decreased. E targeting adjusted; dash speed decreased.
As it stands, our desert rose has consistently been warming the ban bench. Even when technically close to balanced, we believe she has several frustrating attributes that contribute to her high ban rate. We’re tackling this problem by giving her some balance tweaks so that both Samira players and her opponents feel more comfortable having her back in the ring.
To do this, we’re reducing the power of her defensive tools and giving opponents more opportunities to play against her in lane. We’re also reducing her all-in potential early game. In exchange, we’re improving her kill potential mid to late game, so that when she does go in, she slays.

name: Akali
rationale:
Base health decreased and health growth increased. Passive energy restore removed. Q cost increased early and decreased later; bonus damage removed. W now increases Akali’s maximum energy. E total damage increased; first hit damage ratio decreased; second hit damage ratio increased. R first dash now deals magic damage and has increased later scaling with AP.
From the start of most games, Akali is able to wield her durability to help her coast through even the most difficult early lane phases. We’re reducing her early game tankiness so that her laning success isn't always guaranteed, but in return, we’re giving her an overall net buff with later dueling payoff, so that when she strikes, it’s deadly. In addition, we're also making her energy management more intuitive so that if you’re just now picking her up, it doesn’t take so much… energy?

Since she entered the ring, Lillia has managed to prance her way out of any nerfs while still remaining a staple in professional play. The change to Urgot in patch 11.4 was meant to make squishier Kraken Slayer off-builds more viable, but he’s veered off course, scuttling over to rush Titanic Hydra instead. There have been reports of bears, horses, and deer running amok in the jungle, but after thorough investigation, Volibear has been deemed innocent of all jungle gap wrongdoing. If anything, he's been the victim. We're waking him out of his jungle hibernation to enjoy the new season.

name: Xin Zhao
rationale:
We're shipping two sets of changes to Xin at once: One focused on his core AD fighter build and one to open up an AP off-build. This is a long one, so to make it less of a Xin ow, we’ve broken his patch notes up accordingly. First, the AD Xin we all know and love: a Demacian warrior with a strong spirit and an even stronger spear. As a brawler who uniquely excels at skirmishes, we’re sharpening his distinctive strengths by giving him tools to extend combos and initiate duels. With new, creative ways to get to his enemies, he’ll feel more empowered or, dare we say, audacious, to dive into teamfights and skirmishes.
But wait, what if Xin wants to change things up a bit? Put down the spear and don a wizard hat instead? Before his rework, AP Xin Zhao occasionally made the rounds as a fun off-build with a distinctly different playstyle from his AD counterpart. These changes are geared towards bringing AP Xin back into play, but we still expect his AD-focused builds to come out on top.

name: Teemo
rationale:
Passive bonus attack speed duration increased. E on-hit base damage increased.
Small shroom aficionado gets a sizable buff to remind us what true terror feels like.

lines.raw: Bonus attack speed duration increased to 5 seconds from 3.
On-hit base damage increased to 11 to 55 from 10 to 50.

name: Thresh
rationale:
W base shield decreased later.
Instead of space tunes, Thresh has been belting his sweet tones of misery across Pro and Elite levels of play. Players have been finding the most success around builds that max his lantern second, so we're cranking that down a notch.

lines.raw: Base shield reduced to 60 to 180 from 60 to 220.

name: Tristana
rationale:
Base attack damage decreased.
Tristana has rocket jumped to the top of Pro levels of play. We're taking a shot at her early game damage.

lines.raw: Base attack damage reduced to 59 from 61.

name: Udyr
rationale:
Base attack damage decreased.
Equipped with strong early clearing, dueling, and four eternal spirits, Udyr's been running the jungle. We're curbing the damage output across his builds to give peers the chance to start off on the right foot.

lines.raw: Base attack damage reduced to 64 from 66.

name: Varus
rationale:
Base attack damage growth increased.
If you ordered another underperforming marksman in distress, you're in luck—we've got Varus. Giving him some much-needed power that should help him feel more like a full combo rather than a sad side of fries.

lines.raw: Attack damage growth increased to 3.4 from 3.

lines.attribute: Can no longer be cast while grounded.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Can no longer be cast while grounded.

name: Yasuo
rationale:
Base attack damage growth increased.
We left Yasuo feeling winded from our nerfs to Immortal Shieldbow in 11.6, so we're partially walking back our adjustment to help him catch his breath.

lines.raw: Attack damage growth increased to 3 from 2.2.

lines.attribute: Battle Academia Yone: Yone's icon on the in-game scoreboard no longer uses the skin's portrait.
lines.raw: Undocumented/Bug Fix: Yone's icon on the in-game scoreboard no longer uses the skin's portrait.

name: Yorick
rationale:
Marked enemy champions and large monsters now Awaken nearby graves. Mist Walkers now deal damage when they leap to enemies. E cast paradigm updated.
Yorick is usually able to crush his way through average play, but recently, he's fallen behind. In addition to his absence from higher-tier games, he has room for a buff to help him across levels of play, so we're taking a first pass by making his E more satisfying and effective. Coupled with some QoL adjustments, this should help our shepherd feel less wretched, while also evening out his performance in higher levels of play.

name: Essence Reaver
rationale: Essence Reaver is overperforming amongst peers in its class, and then some. Essence should still feel like an appropriate buy, but rushing it shouldn't be as efficient as it currently is.

rationale: Since the changes in 11.4, Everfrost has been ever-present on the Rift. It's cool that players have found interesting ways to utilize all three Mythics, but Everfrost's damage was a little too high for its lockdown power, so we're bringing that down.

rationale: Lord Dominik's Regard has quickly caught on as the go-to second purchase for marksfolk. We're adjusting it so it's no longer a catch-all item, but rather something to be picked up specifically for facing tanky terrors.

rationale: Trinity Force went a bit too heavy on attack speed, which cut it off from a larger audience. In turn, we're forcing a new hand of stats (and Mythic passive!) that should make it feel like a real contender for more users.

rationale: Turbo Chemtank quickly broke speed limits and our expectations, so we're shifting some power from its zoom to its sloom.

rationale:
W cost increased early.
Lately, Annie’s been blazing down her foes. By increasing the cost on her W, she’ll have to be more careful when deciding whether to burn up minions or enemy champions.

lines.raw: Mana cost increased to 90 to 110 from 70 to 110.

name: Aphelios
rationale:
Passive lethality increased. R main weapon effects strengthened.
Aphelios has been looking pale ever since we nerfed his interaction with Kraken Slayer in 11.2. Given how he’s fallen behind other scaling marksmen, we're putting more punch into his lethality rank-ups (which have been historically lackluster), along with his weapon effects during his ultimate, to let him reach for the moon.

rationale:
E cost now scales down.
Cass has been coiled up tight with Tear of the Goddess, as she relies on its mana in mid and late game teamfights. This dependence has caused her to suffer both in power and freedom in item diversity, so we’re scaling down her need for it.

rationale: We’re bringing some fringe junglers and popular champions up to actually viable levels in the jungle. name: Dr. Mundo
rationale:
Passive max health regen increased.
At present, jungle Mundo’s been smashing, and top lane Mundo’s been crashing. We’re tackling this by pulling back on his clear speeds, which should slow his roll without stopping our purple friend from cleaving through the jungle. We’re then doctoring up Lane-do by tossing him more regen to make him the meaty meatball of his dreams.

LeBlanc is a master trickster known for her ability to bop in, burst down, and bop back out— but as of late, her burst has felt more deceitful than fatal.

We’re giving Lee Sin more clear to help him keep an eye on other top junglers.

rationale:
E bonus resistances decreased early.
Our lady of clockwork has become the staple mid lane mage in Pro play. Armed with both safe early game laning and strong mid-to-late game teamfight power, she’s a reliable source of utility and damage without much of a tradeoff. To even things out, we’re tapping down her early durability in the early phases of the game.

Q base damage decreased later. W now lasts longer with basic attacks. E taunt duration decreased. R updated so that Rammus now soars, slams, slows, and shocks. Ability VFX and SFX updated.
In conjunction with his release in Wild Rift, we’re celebrating Rammus with a mini visual update! Along with new sound and visual effects, we’re armoring this ‘dillo with a new ult that rewards him for going fast and vaulting into enemies to create the perfect impact.

name: Rumble
rationale:
Base magic resist and magic resist growth decreased. Passive Overheating bonus damage decreased; now scales with target’s maximum health; now grants attack speed. E now reduces the target’s magic resistance.
Although mid Rumble’s been doing well, he’s been feeling rather tepid up in top lane. We like supporting both sides of the yordle, so we’re finding a middle ground in power for both roles by making top Rumble better at beating down tankier targets, while making mid Rumble more vulnerable, particularly when laning against mages.

name: Vladimir
rationale:
Q cooldown decreased later.
As a champ who used to rush item components for CDR, but can no longer do so with the new Mythic item structure, Vlad has been thrown for a loop. To compensate, we’re pumping down his cooldown.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 9 to 4 seconds from 9 to 5.

lines.attribute: Now properly triggers and grants charges for Manaflow Band, Muramana, Ravenous Hydra and Tear of the Goddess.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Now properly triggers and grants charges for Manaflow Band, Muramana, Ravenous Hydra and Tear of the Goddess.

name: Yorick
rationale:
Mist Walkers damage decreased. E initial leap damage decreased; now deals increased damage over 8 attacks. Turrets now prioritize minions over the Maiden.
Well, we did it. We woke Yorick up and brought him back to life… and right over the balance line. To mitigate, we’re following up his patch 11.6 buffs by walking back some of his damage—but we don’t want to leave him back in the dirt. So we’re also adding the second part of his intended changes to help his Maiden stay alive. Instead of constantly trying to keep her out of harm’s way, our premier split pusher can now focus on destroying turrets with his minions of the Mist.

lines.raw: Mist Walker AD ratio reduced to 25% AD from 30% AD.

lines.attribute: Turrets now retaliate against the offending Mist Walker instead of Yorick if they damage an enemy champion.
lines.raw: New Effect: Turrets now retaliate against the offending Mist Walker instead of Yorick if they damage an enemy champion.

lines.attribute: Tooltip now notes the proper amount of health Mist Walkers are summoned with.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Tooltip now notes the proper amount of health Mist Walkers are summoned with.

lines.raw: Removed: Mist Walkers no longer deal 100% bonus damage on their attack after leaping to champions and large monsters.

lines.raw: New Effect: Marked enemies now take 40% bonus damage for 8 attacks from Mist Walkers for the duration of the debuff.

lines.attribute: Turrets now retaliate against the Maiden of the Mist instead of Yorick if they damage an enemy champion.
lines.raw: New Effect: Turrets now retaliate against the Maiden of the Mist instead of Yorick if they damage an enemy champion.

lines.attribute: Turrets now prioritize minions over the Maiden of the Mist.
lines.raw: New Effect: Turrets now prioritize minions over the Maiden of the Mist.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Can no longer activate Moonstone Renewer when casting the second cast repeatedly on an out-of-range ally that is in combat.

name: Zac
rationale:
W damage increased.
Between last season’s changes to jungle camp health and Bami’s Cinder, Zac lost a lot of his mid-game clear speed. We’re putting the glob back on the job by slinging him more damage, along with a buff for AP bruiser builds.

lines.raw: Base damage increased to 35 to 95 from 25 to 85.
AP ratio increased to 4% per 100 AP from 2% per 100 AP.

name: Zed
rationale: We’re bringing some fringe junglers and popular champions up to actually viable levels in the jungle. While we've done passes on a number of these champions before, we're more confident that these changes will give them safe and competitive clears that should be fun for those itching for a test run.

lines.attribute: No longer has a cooldown against minions and monsters.
lines.raw: Removed: No longer has a cooldown against minions and monsters.
Monster damage reduced to 100% from 200%.

lines.raw: New Effect: Damage cap now only affects epic monsters rather than all jungle monsters.
Epic monster damage cap changed to 300 at all levels from 200 to 500.

lines.raw: New Effect: Is now called out in chat to notify when the item is purchased.

name: Chemtech Putrifier
rationale: We set out to make Chemtech Putrifier a more sought after choice for supports by substantially broadening its use cases. First and foremost, we’re making it so you have to target an ally to receive the benefits yourself (much like Ardent Censer and Staff of Flowing Water). The ability to apply it to oneself didn't seem to have significant power implications, but it did have odd interactions (like with Ravenous Hunter) that were not intended. In addition, we’re giving the item a slight buff because it's still a bit niche and underperforms compared to other options.

lines.raw: Ability power increased to 55 from 50.

lines.attribute: The user no longer gains the buff when healing or shielding themselves.
lines.raw: Removed: The user no longer gains the buff when healing or shielding themselves.

name: Frozen Heart
rationale: Frozen Heart’s been getting looked over in the tank item department. Have some heart (and more armor, while you’re at it).

lines.raw: Armor increased to 80 from 70.
Bug Fix: Now blocked by spell shield.

name: Hextech Rocketbelt
rationale: Night Harvester tends to be purchased more and performs better than Rocketbelt, even by one of the item’s intended audiences—champions who aim to assassinate single targets. We’re bringing it back into style by sharpening the differences between the two items.

lines.raw: New Effect: Now grants 6 magic penetration.
Health reduced to 250 from 350.

lines.attribute: Upgraded Aeropack now grants 10 magic penetration.
lines.raw: New Effect: Upgraded Aeropack now grants 10 magic penetration.
Upgraded Aeropack health reduced to 350 from 450.

name: Ionian Boots of Lucidity
rationale: These kicks have become very popular in Pro play, crowding out other footwear options in the jungle. We’re slapping on a higher price tag since their cost is a contributor to an unsustainable jungle meta centered around fast clears and fast ganks at low costs.

lines.raw: Total cost increased to 950 gold from 900 gold.
Combine cost increased to 650 gold from 600 gold.
Bug Fix: Now blocked by spell shield.

lines.attribute: Sacrifice now properly redirects damage from allied Pledged champions to the user even when they're untargetable.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Sacrifice now properly redirects damage from allied Pledged champions to the user even when they're untargetable.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: When Kayle uses Starfire Spellblade as a third attack, she will now properly deal true damage.

lines.attribute: Jayce now properly deals true damage on his third attack with Mercury Cannon in all instances, not just when he crits.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Jayce now properly deals true damage on his third attack with Mercury Cannon in all instances, not just when he crits.

name: Moonstone Renewer
rationale: With Moonstone Renewer as the only Mythic that truly fulfilled enchanter’s dreams, they haven’t had much of a selection to choose from. To expand their horizons and inventories, we’re adjusting the following items to be picked up based on the situation at hand: Moonstone for more heals and shields, and Shurelya’s for more nimble feet and aggressive plays. We don’t want to overload the game with movement speed, so we’re also pivoting Staff of Flowing Water to focus from fast zooms to AP booms.

lines.attribute: Unique Passive - Starlit Grace: When affecting champions with attacks or abilities in combat, heal the nearby allied champion (excluding yourself) with the most missing health for 60 (2 second cooldown). Each second spent in combat with champions increases heal and shield power by 4%, stacking up to 5 times for a maximum of 20%.
lines.raw: New Effect: When affecting champions with attacks or abilities in combat, heal the nearby allied champion (excluding yourself) with the most missing health for 60 (2 second cooldown). Each second spent in combat with champions increases this heal by 12.5%, stacking up to 4 times for maximum of 50%.

rationale: With Moonstone Renewer as the only Mythic that truly fulfilled enchanter’s dreams, they haven’t had much of a selection to choose from. To expand their horizons and inventories, we’re adjusting the following items to be picked up based on the situation at hand: Moonstone for more heals and shields, and Shurelya’s for more nimble feet and aggressive plays. We don’t want to overload the game with movement speed, so we’re also pivoting Staff of Flowing Water to focus from fast zooms to AP booms.

lines.attribute: No longer empowers allies to deal 35 to 55 bonus magic damage on the next 3 basic attacks or instances of ability damage against champions within 3 seconds.
lines.raw: Removed: No longer empowers allies to deal 35 to 55 bonus magic damage on the next 3 basic attacks or instances of ability damage against champions within 3 seconds.

Mythic passive changed to 5 ability haste from 2.5% bonus movement speed.

name: Staff of Flowing Water
rationale: With Moonstone Renewer as the only Mythic that truly fulfilled enchanter’s dreams, they haven’t had much of a selection to choose from. To expand their horizons and inventories, we’re adjusting the following items to be picked up based on the situation at hand: Moonstone for more heals and shields, and Shurelya’s for more nimble feet and aggressive plays. We don’t want to overload the game with movement speed, so we’re also pivoting Staff of Flowing Water to focus from fast zooms to AP booms.

lines.raw: New Effect: Is now called out in chat to notify when the item is purchased.

name: Titanic Hydra
rationale: Shifting its power away from early game and low-health builds.

lines.raw: Colossus bonus attack damage changed to 2% bonus health from 1% maximum health.
Updated visual effects.

name: Diana
rationale:
Base armor growth and health regen reduced. Passive bonus attack speed reduced early.
Our buffs to Diana's passive in 11.8 helped her rise up the ranks in mid and jungle. Players are enjoying the spice she brings to the jungle, so we're gently pulling back on her clear speeds and in lane durability.

lines.raw: Armor growth reduced to 3.1 from 3.6.
Base health regeneration reduced to 6.5 from 7.5.
Bonus attack speed reduced to 15 to 40% from 20 to 40%.
Maximum bonus attack speed reduced to 45 to 120% from 60 to 120%.

name: Dr. Mundo
rationale:
Base armor and AD growths decreased.
Our 11.8 buffs to top Mundo brought him back into the spotlight and then some. Once he hits late game, he reaches an oppressive state where it feels impossible to get through his purple hide. We’re following up by taking out some of his tankiness and threat potential to let his opponents take bigger chunks out of his meaty exterior.

lines.raw: Attack damage growth reduced to 3 from 3.5.
Armor growth reduced to 3 from 3.5.

name: Garen
rationale:
W bonus resistances decreased; units kill cap increased.
With efficient stacking on his W without requiring much in return, Garen’s been able to have his beef and eat it too. We’re pushing down his spike in his tankiness so that his power curves more smoothly after picking up a Mythic item.

lines.raw: Maximum stacks increased to 150 from 120.
Bonus resistances per stack reduced to 0.2 from 0.25.
Maximum bonus resistances unchanged.

name: Gragas
rationale:
E base damage decreased later.
Gragas is currently a triple threat in Pro levels of play, guzzling casks in jungle, support, and top lane. Nudging down one of his more vital spells in lane.

lines.raw: Base damage reduced to 80 to 260 from 80 to 280.

name: Hecarim
rationale:
Base armor decreased; armor growth increased. Q damage amp per stack decreased and now scales with bonus AD. W now heals from damage dealt and scales with AD. E damage decreased.
Hecarim is still at a wild gallop in the meta, more often meeting the ban hammer than his foes. Then once he’s able to make it into a game, he’s typically confined to a full-tank build. In order to fix this two-part problem, we’re trotting down some of his upfront burst and early durability. We’re also giving more incentive for damage-oriented builds for a powerful pony rather than the same old beefy bronco.

lines.raw: Base armor reduced to 32 from 36.
Armor growth increased to 4.25 from 4.
Damage amplification per stack reduced to 2% from 5%.

lines.attribute: Damage amplification per stack now scales with 3% per 100 bonus AD.
lines.raw: New Effect: Damage amplification per stack now scales with 3% per 100 bonus AD.

lines.attribute: Healing now scales with 2.5% per 100 bonus AD.
lines.raw: New Effect: Healing now scales with 2.5% per 100 bonus AD.
Healing from ally damage reduced to 15% from 30%.

lines.attribute: Healing from ally damage now scales with 1.25% per 100 bonus AD.
lines.raw: New Effect: Healing from ally damage now scales with 1.25% per 100 bonus AD.
Minimum base damage reduced to 30 to 110 from 35 to 155.
Maximum base damage reduced to 60 to 220 from 70 to 310.

name: Heimerdinger
rationale:
W initial rocket damage decreased later.
Heimerdinger is overperforming in top, mid, and bot lane at high levels of play. Giving him a ding down.

lines.raw: Initial rocket base damage reduced to 50 to 150 from 50 to 170.
Subsequent rocket base damage reduced to 10 to 30 from 10 to 34.

lines.attribute: Maximum base damage: 50+10*4 to 150+30*4 from 50+10*4 to 170+34*4.
lines.raw: Maximum base damage: 50+10*4 to 150+30*4 from 50+10*4 to 170+34*4.

lines.attribute: Fixed bug where it would not update his attack speed correctly.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed bug where it would not update his attack speed correctly.

name: Jinx
rationale:
Q crit strike bugfix.
Jinx was doing way more splash damage than she was supposed to with Fishbones. It’s fixed now, but it’s a big enough drop in damage that we’re noting it here.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Rocket splash critical strike damage reduced to 175% from 200%.

lines.attribute: Now properly has voice lines for eating Honeyfruit and killing enemies with Void Seeker.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Now properly has voice lines for eating Honeyfruit and killing enemies with Void Seeker.

lines.attribute: Riftmaker and Trinity Force now grant her the appropriate amount of stats for her Evolutions.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Riftmaker and Trinity Force now grant her the appropriate amount of stats for her Evolutions.

name: Kayn
rationale:
Q Darkin damage modifier increased.
Shadow Assassin Kayn has been overshadowing his Darkin counterpart, so we’re bringing that part of Kayn… out of the dark.

lines.raw: Darkin AD ratio increased to 65% AD from 55% AD.

name: Kindred
rationale:
Q cooldown decreased; base damage increased later.
Kindred is continuing to struggle in the jungle, so we’re giving them a stronger mid-game power spike.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 8 seconds from 9.
Base damage increased to 60 to 160 from 60 to 140.

name: Kog'Maw
rationale:
Q resistances reduction increased. E cost decreased.
Kog'Maw has been in a cocoon more than he’s been in the bot lane, so we’re giving him more ooze to get back in the groove. In addition, we're helping him burn through more enemies that dare stand in his way... or in his spit.

lines.attribute: VO has been restored and is playing once again on all skins.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: VO has been restored and is playing once again on all skins.
Resistance reduction increased to 25 to 33% from 20 to 28%.
Mana cost reduced to 60 to 100 from 80 to 120.

name: Lulu
rationale:
W cooldown decreased; ally cast bonus attack speed increased early.
We're buffing Whimsy to give Lulu a pinch more power earlier in the game.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 15 to 11 seconds from 16 to 12.
Bonus attack speed increased to 25 to 35% from 20 to 35%.

name: Morgana
rationale:
W damage against non-epic monsters decreased.
Although we still think she’s a great new addition to the jungle, our 11.8 buff to Morgana was stronger than intended, so we're partially walking it back.

lines.raw: Damage against non-epic monsters reduced to 185% from 200%.

name: Rumble
rationale:
Passive Overheated bonus on-hit damage decreased.
Rumble is heating up in the mid lane, specifically against squishier melee targets, so we’re hitting an all-too-reliable source of his damage so his enemies have a chance to cool down.

lines.raw: Overheat on-hit base damage reduced to 5 to 40 from 10 to 50.
Overheat on-hit AP ratio reduced to 25% AP from 30% AP.

name: Sett
rationale:
W damage ratio increased. R damage ratio increased.
Our damage-binding adjustments to Sett in 10.18 reduced the effectiveness of his full-tank builds, which made him less of a menace in mid, jungle, and support. With a reduced threat of him flexing across different positions, we can now let him flex more damage.

lines.raw: Bonus AD ratio increased to 20% per 100 bonus AD from 10%.
Bonus AD ratio increased to 120% bonus AD from 100%.

name: Shen
rationale:
R shield decreased; now scales with bonus health.
With only base values and a token AP ratio, Shen’s ult feels more like a bubble than a shield, making it too unreliable for protecting squishy allies when they get caught out late game. We’re adding another ratio to make his scaling considerably better and to help him feel more empowered to protect his friends late game.

lines.raw: Minimum base shield reduced to 140 to 500 from 175 to 525.
Maximum base shield reduced to 224 to 800 from 280 to 840.

lines.attribute: Shield now scales with 17.5% bonus health, increased up to 28% based on target's missing health.
lines.raw: New Effect: Shield now scales with 17.5% bonus health, increased up to 28% based on target's missing health.

name: Taric
rationale:
Q cost decreased later. Updated tether interaction with Master Yi.
Taking some of the mana burden off of our knight in shining crystal.

lines.raw: Mana cost reduced to 70 to 90 from 70 to 110.

lines.attribute: Bound allies no longer mimic abilities if they are vanished via Alpha Strike, Hallucinate, Rappel, or Void Rush. Mimicked abilities will be removed if the ally becomes vanished via those abilities as well.
lines.raw: Removed: Bound allies no longer mimic abilities if they are vanished via Alpha Strike, Hallucinate, Rappel, or Void Rush. Mimicked abilities will be removed if the ally becomes vanished via those abilities as well.

name: Trundle
rationale:
E slow increased early.
The 8.18 nerf to Trundle’s pillar’s slow put the brakes on his ganking and ability to find picks, and our follow-up in 10.2 just didn’t cut it. With more slow from the get go, we’re making it easier for Trundle to be the zoning troll on a roll.

lines.raw: Slow increased to 32 to 60% from 20 to 60%.

lines.attribute: Fixed bugs where he would not properly copy Kindred and Shyvana stacking passives.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed bugs where he would not properly copy Kindred and Shyvana stacking passives.

lines.attribute: Fixed bug where, on possessing Kled, he would sometimes become mounted Kled with unmounted Kled abilities.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed bug where, on possessing Kled, he would sometimes become mounted Kled with unmounted Kled abilities.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where, after possessing Kindred, he would occasionally keep the Wolf's VFX for the rest of the game.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where, after possessing Kindred, he would occasionally keep the Wolf's VFX for the rest of the game.

name: Vladimir
rationale:
Q cooldown increased later.
Our last buff brought Vlad back into the role of a scaling powerhouse—maybe a little too much so. We’re partially pulling back on his 11.8 adjustment to find a sweeter middle ground.

lines.raw: Cooldown increased to 9 to 4.6 seconds from 9 to 4.

lines.attribute: Full Machine Viktor: Updated visual effects.
lines.raw: Updated visual effects.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where he would not knock-up enemies who entered the ability radius while untargetable even after their untargetability ends.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where he would not knock-up enemies who entered the ability radius while untargetable even after their untargetability ends.

name: Xerath
rationale:
Q damage increased. W base and enhanced base damage increased later.
Our resident laser-sniper has been in a confusing state, having more of a blast as a support than as a mid laner. By re-tuning his scaling to favor level and gold scaling, this should help energize mid Xerath.

lines.raw: Base damage reduced to 70 to 230 from 80 to 240.
AP ratio increased to 85% AP from 75% AP.
Base damage increased to 60 to 200 from 60 to 180.
Maximum base damage increased to 60*1.667 to 200*1.667 from 60*1.667 to 180*1.667.

lines.attribute: No longer unintentionally mutually exclusive with Lifeline items such as Sterak's Gage or Immortal Shieldbow.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: No longer unintentionally mutually exclusive with Lifeline items such as Sterak's Gage or Immortal Shieldbow.

lines.attribute: No longer builds into Wit's End.
lines.raw: No longer builds into Wit's End.

lines.attribute: Stat panel no longer shows the omnivamp as stacking.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Stat panel no longer shows the omnivamp as stacking.

name: Dead Man's Plate
rationale: Dead Man’s Plate is dominating as a second item choice for a wide range of champions, including tanks, fighters, and juggernauts. We're reducing its raw defensive stats to highlight its unique mobility passive.

lines.raw: Health reduced to 300 from 400.

name: Death's Dance
rationale: Death’s Dance has been a step behind its peers, so we’re bumping up its raw efficiency to bring it back in full swing.

lines.raw: Attack damage increased to 55 from 50.
Armor increased to 45 from 40.
Now builds into Wit's End.

name: Moonstone Renewer
rationale: Our adjustments to Moonstone in 11.8 left the item weaker than other options for supports, so we’re returning some power back to its base healing, which should feel even more satisfying when combined with its heal and shield power.

lines.raw: Starlit Grace base heal increased to 70 from 60.

name: Prowler's Claw
rationale: We’re adjusting the way Prowler’s Claw’s active targeting works to make it more user-friendly and forgiving, as it’s been more challenging to use in some kits than intended. We’re not increasing the item’s actual range, but now if you misclick slightly while trying to cast it in the middle of your combo, Prowler’s will hit the target you probably meant to click on instead of doing nothing.

lines.attribute: Sandswipe targeting changed: New: Looks for a target in the following order: Nearest champion within 50 units of the cursor.
lines.raw: Nearest champion within 50 units of the cursor.

lines.raw: Old: Targets enemy exactly at the cursor.
