lines.raw: Bug Fix: Now grants Kai'Sa the appropriate amount of stats for her Evolutions.

lines.attribute: Stat panel now correctly shows the omnivamp from the Mythic passive.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Stat panel now correctly shows the omnivamp from the Mythic passive.

lines.attribute: No longer unintentionally mutually exclusive with Lifeline items such as Sterak's Gage or Immortal Shieldbow.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: No longer unintentionally mutually exclusive with Lifeline items such as Sterak's Gage or Immortal Shieldbow.

lines.attribute: Inspire passive no longer counts allied champions twice for its "Allies Motivated" counter in its tooltip.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Inspire passive no longer counts allied champions twice for its "Allies Motivated" counter in its tooltip.

name: Sunfire Aegis
rationale: In the olden times, there was a sunnier era, or dare we say, a Sunfirey era. That was until the Chemtanks crushed all who would dare oppose them. We’re bringing back the fire by helping Aegis melt down its enemies once more.

lines.raw: Bonus monster damage increased to 150% from 100%.

lines.attribute: Now grants Kai'Sa the appropriate amount of stats for her Evolutions.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Now grants Kai'Sa the appropriate amount of stats for her Evolutions.

name: Turbo Chemtank
rationale: With Turbo in tow, junglers are able to consistently engage and gank as they gallop in from across the map, so we’re putting it on a tighter leash.

lines.raw: Supercharged bonus movement speed reduced to 40% from 60%.

name: Wit's End
rationale: For such a niche item, Wit's End lacks oomph, even when picked up in the right scenario. Adjusting the build path and adding more damage should make it feel more powerful all around and appeal to more champions.

lines.attribute: New Recipe: Hearthbound Axe + Negatron Cloak + Long Sword + 750 gold = 3100 gold.
lines.raw: New Recipe: Hearthbound Axe + Negatron Cloak + Long Sword + 750 gold = 3100 gold.

lines.raw: Old Recipe: Hearthbound Axe + Negatron Cloak + Dagger + 800 gold = 3100 gold.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Stat panel now correctly shows the omnivamp.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where she would deal double damage if her target was very close to a wall.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where she would deal double damage if her target was very close to a wall.

lines.attribute: Stun is no longer delayed by up to 0.25 seconds.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Stun is no longer delayed by up to 0.25 seconds.

lines.attribute: Knock-up is no longer delayed by up to 0.25 seconds.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Knock-up is no longer delayed by up to 0.25 seconds.

name: Bard
rationale:
Passive base damage decreased.
Bard's been overperforming at higher tiers of play due to his roaming capabilities. Obviously, it's Bard. Bard roams. So to preserve his unique strength as a roaming support, we're toning down his early lane damage instead.

lines.raw: Base damage reduced to 30 from 40.

name: Darius
rationale:
E cooldown increased.
Darius has been chopping up his foes left, right, and across levels of play. With high win rates in Elite and high ban rates in Average tiers, we're looking to make Apprehend less oppressive by giving his opponents more opportunities to farm or mount a counter-attack.

lines.raw: Cooldown increased to 26 to 18 seconds from 24 to 12.

lines.attribute: Muramana Shock now triggers on secondary targets properly.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Muramana Shock now triggers on secondary targets properly.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where effigies would not be usable for the rest of the game if the user sold their Poro-Snax at the shop in ARAM.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where effigies would not be usable for the rest of the game if the user sold their Poro-Snax at the shop in ARAM.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where he was unable to gain Tear of the Goddess stacks when killing minions.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where he was unable to gain Tear of the Goddess stacks when killing minions.

name: Galio
rationale:

rationale:

While tank Senna can be fun, it currently overshadows other item options and writes off her primary weakness as a squishy carry. To mitigate, we’re bringing more power back to support builds where she’s historically had success (lethality and AP), and tapping down Frostfire. We’re also taking this opportunity to slow down some of her range growth, which has been scaling a lot faster with the buff to her Mist in 11.2. Altogether, these changes should empower Senna to build items that better fit her identity as a powerful glass cannon.

name: Bramble Vest
rationale:
We want players to feel empowered to make meaningful item choices each game. Right now, there are two trends that are limiting early game decision-making for tanks in top lane: purchasing Thornmail as a second item, and purchasing Bramble Vest without completing Thornmail. This routine highlights the problem of Bramble Vest and Thornmail being used as generalist items, rather than their intended purpose of being picked up to face high-healing enemies. These changes are intended to give these items more clearly defined roles in the power they provide for top lane tanks. One more thing: You may notice that we gave Frozen Heart a less generic stat line than other tank items. This is intentional, since it has other unique outputs. We’re also giving it a larger base value on Rock Solid than other items since it has less innate max health scaling. Altogether, it remains a source of high ability haste and mana, and is now clearly an anti-attacker item.
We’re reshaping the Wardstone line to fit more as a capstone support item, similar to Rabadon's Deathcap, Infinity Edge, and Gargoyle Stoneplate (all of which are stronger after you pick up a few other items). We’re also streamlining the purchase path to be a one-stop-shop like Manamune and Archangel's Staff, instead of having to repeatedly upgrade it.

rationale:
We want players to feel empowered to make meaningful item choices each game. Right now, there are two trends that are limiting early game decision-making for tanks in top lane: purchasing Thornmail as a second item, and purchasing Bramble Vest without completing Thornmail. This routine highlights the problem of Bramble Vest and Thornmail being used as generalist items, rather than their intended purpose of being picked up to face high-healing enemies. These changes are intended to give these items more clearly defined roles in the power they provide for top lane tanks. One more thing: You may notice that we gave Frozen Heart a less generic stat line than other tank items. This is intentional, since it has other unique outputs. We’re also giving it a larger base value on Rock Solid than other items since it has less innate max health scaling. Altogether, it remains a source of high ability haste and mana, and is now clearly an anti-attacker item.
We’re reshaping the Wardstone line to fit more as a capstone support item, similar to Rabadon's Deathcap, Infinity Edge, and Gargoyle Stoneplate (all of which are stronger after you pick up a few other items). We’re also streamlining the purchase path to be a one-stop-shop like Manamune and Archangel's Staff, instead of having to repeatedly upgrade it.

name: Aphelios
rationale:
Base magic resist and AD growth increased. Severum’s maximum number of attacks decreased; on-hit damage increased; healing from basic attacks decreased; healing from abilities increased. Crescendum’s mini Chakram damage decreased; sentry damage increased.
Aphelios’ changelist is a whole lot of numbers, so we’ll try and break it down. First and foremost: yes, it’s an Aphelios buff! He’s been in a slump in terms of win rate and Pro presence, and could use a helping hand to get back on his feet. To do this, we’re buffing his base stats and weapon combinations that have fallen out of favor, while pulling power from the combos that have emerged as clear favorites. By upping the reward he gets from using Infernum and Severum as off-hand weapons, he should feel more well-rounded and prepared to take down his enemies, no matter what’s in his immediate arsenal.

name: Draven
rationale:
Q bonus damage increased.
With less early game AD from his core build than in previous seasons, Draven’s been less able to… well, Draven. Sharpening up his blades so he can keep up with his adoring fans.

lines.raw: Base damage increased to 40 to 60 from 35 to 55.
Bonus AD ratio increased to 70 to 110% bonus AD from 65 to 105%.
Bug Fix: Now properly stacks Manamune.

name: Gnar
rationale:
Base attack damage decreased.
Baby beast is still throwing temper tantrums, and his threat and harass potential can be too much to handle. We’re pulling back some of his early lane power to give his enemies a chance to catch their breath (and maybe even Gnar’s boomerang).

name: Hecarim
rationale:
Base armor increased. Q damage ratio increased.
We weren’t kidding—Hecarim needed help last patch, and he still does now. We’re doubling down on the buff to his Q and reverting part of his 11.9 nerf. Time to run free, horsey.

lines.raw: Base armor increased to 35 from 32.
Damage bonus AD ratio increased to 85% bonus AD from 75%.

name: Illaoi
rationale:
Base mana growth increased.
With a smaller mana pool than other fighters, Illaoi often runs low on mana in later phases of the game. This leaves her between a rock and a hard place, where she has to carefully balance when to use mana to push faster and when she’s ready to take on challengers. To solve this, we’re increasing her mana scaling.

lines.raw: Mana growth increased to 50 from 40.

name: Jarvan IV
rationale:
W cooldown decreased.
Jarvan tends to lose steam early on in a fight, so we’re giving him more incentives to stay in the battle and continue protecting the faithful.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 9 seconds from 12.

name: Kai'Sa
rationale:
Q cooldown increased early.
This fearless predator has been making Pro play her prey. We’re looking to draw back some of her early game power by curbing her ability to control waves and giving her opponents more opportunities to punish her when her Q is down.

lines.raw: Cooldown increased to 10 to 6 seconds from 8 to 6.
Updated visual effects.

name: Malphite
rationale:
W on-hit damage increased.
Malphite’s been feeling more rock-soft than solid. Combined with Bramble Vest’s nerf in patch 11.11, he’s hit rock bottom. To buff up his trading in lane, we’re amping up the thunder in his claps so that he can hit like the ton of bricks he is.

lines.raw: Cleave base damage increased to 15 to 55 from 10 to 50.
Cleave armor ratio increased to 15% armor from 10% armor.

name: Nasus
rationale:
Passive life steal decreased.
With the patch 11.11 buff to Divine Sunderer, Nasus has been a top dog (literally) in Average play, where he’s able to stay in lane and farm until the cows come home. We’re targeting this by reducing the amount of life steal he can get when he has easier access to minions.

name: Rammus
rationale:
W base bonus armor increased. R cooldown decreased.
Everyone knows Rammus and Bramble Vest are best friends, so it should come as no surprise that he’s been feeling prickly after Bramble’s 11.11 nerf. To mend fences, we’re putting more armor in the armordillo and letting him slam down more often, so that he can continue running rings around his competition.

Cooldown reduced to 110 to 80 seconds from 130 to 90.

rationale:
Q non-champion healing reduced.
This croc has been up and down the block in Pro play. With resourceless sustain and waveclear, he’s able to wade into lane and neutralize most matchups, then force fights by jumping on a victim with his point-and-click CC. To address this, we’re scaling back his healing.

We’re giving him another tap down by shifting power away from the initial part of his W and slightly lowering its overall scaling. To balance also giving a small boost to the second half of Rake, which is easier to dodge.

name: Tahm Kench
rationale:
Devour and R swapped and reworked. Passive bonus damage decreased. Q now heals, applies his passive, and scales with his size. E shield duration increased; healing over time increased but takes longer to come into effect. And new VFX all around!
The Kench is shinier and slimier than ever with a pretty big update this patch! Historically, our favorite catfish has been limited by his power because his kit is so strong in professional play, forcing him to remain weak for the vast majority of players. To resolve this, we’re making a few major adjustments, so buckle up. First, we’re moving power from Devour—which is heavily used in coordinated play to completely negate allies’ weaknesses and enemies’ actions—into other abilities that reward him for proactive play. Previously, Tahm’s main contributions revolved around standing by to unconditionally save an ally with Devour. With this rework, he will need to take greater risks with his new Abyssal Dive and capitalize on licks and cool tricks (tongue healing, anyone?). Second, we’re making Devour easier to use with allies. They will now see a clear indicator when Devour is available so they know when to run to him for safety. Third, we’re adjusting Abyssal Voyage from being entirely about coordinating with an ally for a cross-map play (a strength heavily restricted to Pro play environments) into being an ability that works on its own. Last but not least, he’s getting new VFX so that the Kench can get a lick leg up on his competition, in style.

name: Black Cleaver
rationale: As mentioned back in May, we're doing an overall pass at movement speed within items and runes. We've adjusted items that have either passively crept up in movement speed (Lich Bane and Trinity Force) or have effects that weaken player expectations of what’s considered a safe range or escape route (Shurelya's and Nimbus Cloak). Most of these changes are expected to be power neutral, but we also threw in tweaks based on whether the item was over- or underperforming. A special note for Stridebreaker… While Stridebreaker's active is an exciting output for many fighters, it heavily weakened the Juggernaut class's primary weakness: mobility. Juggernauts excel once they begin combat on their terms, so an item that allows a Juggernaut to close gaps makes it inherently very powerful, not to mention its damage and ability to be reused. To address this, we’re altering its active to better suit Juggernauts’ needs and boosting it’s stats to amp up their strengths, rather than covering up their weaknesses.

name: Prowler's Claw
rationale: As mentioned back in May, we're doing an overall pass at movement speed within items and runes. We've adjusted items that have either passively crept up in movement speed (Lich Bane and Trinity Force) or have effects that weaken player expectations of what’s considered a safe range or escape route (Shurelya's and Nimbus Cloak). Most of these changes are expected to be power neutral, but we also threw in tweaks based on whether the item was over- or underperforming. A special note for Stridebreaker… While Stridebreaker's active is an exciting output for many fighters, it heavily weakened the Juggernaut class's primary weakness: mobility. Juggernauts excel once they begin combat on their terms, so an item that allows a Juggernaut to close gaps makes it inherently very powerful, not to mention its damage and ability to be reused. To address this, we’re altering its active to better suit Juggernauts’ needs and boosting it’s stats to amp up their strengths, rather than covering up their weaknesses.

rationale:

With more movement speed, she’ll be more able to dodge skillshots, close gaps, and be in the right place at the right time. name: Lillia
rationale:
Base health regen decreased; armor increased. Passive damage increased and now heals. Q cost increased; max stacks decreased; bonus movement speed per stack decreased and lasts longer; cooldown now scales; base damage increased. W damage increased. E cooldown increased; slow is now flat; damage increased. R damage ratio increased; sleep duration decreased; slow decreased and no longer increases over the duration.
You know there’s a lot coming up when the summary line is a paragraph, so here’s the TL;DR—we’re buffing Lillia so that she’s less bashful when bonking down enemies in solo combat. How? We’re shifting some of her power out of her fast clear and coordination-dependent CC, which are often leveraged in higher levels of play into duel-focused strengths. This means that we’re bringing down her early game clear and movement speed, but helping her quickly recoup the losses once she gets her hooves on some AP and reaches mid-to-late game. With the addition of innate sustain, she’ll be able to stay healthy in extended fights and when she isn’t able to perfectly clear camps.

One of Nocturne’s key strengths is his ability to sit in lane and sustain off of waves, shrugging off most harass that comes his way. Similar to the reasoning behind Viego’s nerf last patch, Nocturne is relying on an unhealthy pattern of resourceless sustain. He should be earning his keep instead of relying on his passive, and opponents should feel like they can make a dent in his shadows.

name: Stridebreaker
rationale: Stridebreaker landed strong after its change last patch. One of our goals for the item was to give fighters a way to stick to a target for a period of time, but they don’t need to bring their unlucky foe to a complete standstill to do that. So we’re toning down how much it can slow, but keeping its slow over time. Also, we did an oopsie—the changes also caused Stridebreaker to lose 5 AD on completion. That’s fixed now.

name: Annie
rationale:
Q damage ratio decreased.
The small pyromaniac and her bear are taking over Skilled play! Annie does well versus short-range characters, which are her more common match-ups, so we’re lowering her upfront burst damage and lane harass.

lines.raw: AP ratio reduced to 75% AP from 80% AP.

name: Aurelion Sol
rationale:
Q cooldown increased.
Aurelion Sol is toeing the line in Elite play, and he’s finally put his claw right over it. Slowing him down accordingly.

lines.raw: Cooldown increased to 12 to 8 seconds from 11 to 7.

name: Blitzcrank
rationale:
Base armor and Q damage increased.
Blitz has been cranking out pretty low lethality in the early/mid game. Considering he’s got a flashy fist, it should feel more rewarding when it actually hits. To polish him off, we’re also giving him a thicker metal skin.

lines.raw: Base armor increased to 40 from 37.
Base damage increased to 90 to 290 from 70 to 270.
AP ratio increased to 120% AP from 100% AP.

name: Caitlyn
rationale:
Q damage ratio increased later.
The Sheriff of Piltover could use some encouragement getting on over to the current marksman meta. She’s been finding success with Q-max builds, so we’re adding more incentive by boosting its scaling.

lines.raw: AD ratio increased to 130 to 190% AD from 130 to 170% AD.

name: Cassiopeia
rationale:
E base empowered damage increased.
Cassiopeia used to be a lane bully, but over the years, her gameplay has become farming patiently through the early game until she scales up to a point where she’s able to dish out the damage. With this change, she’ll be more able to press an advantage when she lands her Q in the early laning phase.

lines.raw: Bonus base damage increased to 20 to 100 from 10 to 90.

name: Gwen
rationale:
E bonus attack speed decreased early.
Equipped with raw stat power and a big ol’ pair of scissors, it’s a little too easy for Gwen to snip back at even the toughest of opponents. We’re looking to sharpen her intended weakness by tapping down the speed of her slashes from level 1.

lines.raw: Bonus attack speed reduced to 20 to 80% from 40 to 80%.

lines.attribute: Animation no longer locks if she inputs another command right after casting the ability.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Animation no longer locks if she inputs another command right after casting the ability.

name: Irelia
rationale:
W damage ratio decreased; damage reduction decreased later.
After a good visit in 11.14’s patch notes, Irelia’s ended up on the strong side but in a much better position to balance moving forward. We’ll be watching to see where she lands longterm, but for now, we’re limiting the power on her W.

lines.raw: Minimum AD ratio reduced to 40% AD from 50% AD.
Maximum AD ratio reduced to 120% AD from 150% AD.
Base physical damage reduction reduced to 40 to 70% from 40 to 80%.
Base magic damage reduction reduced to 20 to 35% from 20 to 40%.

name: Kayle
rationale:
Base magic resist decreased.
In mid lane, Kayle’s a safe pick who can reliably stand fly her ground until she hits her power spike. Reducing her magic resist from the get-go should give opponents more opportunities to punish her vulnerable early game.

lines.raw: Base magic resistance reduced to 26 from 30.

name: Kennen
rationale:
Q damage increased.
Struggling across the board, Kennen’s been out of sight for a while now. We’re upping his main ability to feel more like a strike from a storm rather than a sting.

lines.raw: Base damage increased to 85 to 265 from 75 to 235.
AP ratio increased to 80% AP from 75% AP.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where the movement speed did not scale off of AP from runes.

name: Mordekaiser
rationale:
W cooldown decreased; stored post-mitigation damage from damage dealt increased.
The Iron Revenant’s been having trouble standing up to the current fighters in top lane, so we’re passing him more durability to help him hold his own in lane and overall throughout the game.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 12 to 8 seconds from 14 to 10.
Damage dealt stored increased to 45% from 35%.
Damage dealt stored to non-champions increased to 11.25% from 8.75%.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Recall sound effects now play correctly.

name: Nidalee
rationale:
Base health and health growth increased.
Nidalee is known for being fierce, but as of late, her performance across all levels of play has been anything but. With more health, she should be less afraid to bring out the cougar against her prey, and should also help her feel more accessible to players who are just picking her up.

lines.raw: Base health increased to 570 from 545.
Health growth increased to 95 from 85.

lines.attribute: Now correctly heals for the full amount against pets.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Now correctly heals for the full amount against pets.

name: Rell
rationale:
W cooldown decreased.
Rell is a champion who brings disruption and fury to her foes, especially when she’s able to pull out her full combo in extended fights, but she’s been weak across all levels of play. We’re reverting her 11.5 nerf so that she’ll be able to crash down on her opponents, tough out the fight, and mount up—and be able to do it all over again.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 11 seconds from 13.
Cooldown reduced to 11 seconds from 13.

name: Rumble
rationale:
Various Rumble heat system bugfixes and other QoL adjustments!
We’re addressing some frustrating bugs around Rumble’s Overheated system that were left from our changes in patch 11.13. These fixes should even out some abnormalities and help players feel more in control of Tristy.

lines.attribute: Bug Fix: Heat is now checked more consistently: Delay until Heat decays is now much more consistent.
lines.raw: Delay until Heat decays is now much more consistent.

lines.attribute: Bug Fix: Heat is now checked more consistently: Overheated duration is now consistently 5.25 seconds from only averaging this value.
lines.raw: Overheated duration is now consistently 5.25 seconds from only averaging this value.

lines.attribute: Heat no longer gets returned to a previous value when using the Undo function in the shop, which allowed generating high values of heat at the start of the game easily.
lines.raw: Heat no longer gets returned to a previous value when using the Undo function in the shop, which allowed generating high values of heat at the start of the game easily.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: When targeting very far away, no longer tries to walk "in range", overriding Rumble's orders.

lines.attribute: (This was already fixed in V11.14, but documented in this patch instead).
lines.raw: (This was already fixed in V11.14, but documented in this patch instead).

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Unique skin voice lines have been restored.

lines.attribute: Orange smoke VFX now correctly appears from the enemy's point of view when cast through fog of war.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Orange smoke VFX now correctly appears from the enemy's point of view when cast through fog of war.

name: Shyvana
rationale:
Q cooldown decreased early; damage ratios increased.
Shyvana could use more oomph in her one point wonder, so we're buffing her Q to help her clear speeds and let her really dig her teeth into her enemies. We're also adding in some AP compensation so that both her builds can benefit equally.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 7 to 5 seconds from 9 to 5.
First attack AP ratio increased to 35% AP from 25% AP.
Second attack AP ratio increased to 25% AP from 15% AP.

name: Sylas
rationale:
Q detonation damage increased. W heal decreased.
Sylas is a versatile dueler who does what he does a little too well—healing his way through fights, often swinging the battle to his advantage, often catching his opponents off guard. Although sustain is an important part of his kit, enemies should be able to find some kink in his armor. We’re moving some of his sustain power over to his chains so that he doesn’t swing fights as hard, but can still find success when he lands his less-reliable abilities.

lines.raw: Detonation base damage increased to 70 to 290 from 60 to 280.
Detonation AP ratio increased to 90% AP from 80% AP.
Base heal reduced to 25 to 125 from 30 to 150.
Maximum base heal reduced to 50 to 250 from 60 to 300.
Heal AP ratio reduced to 40% AP from 45% AP.
Maximum heal AP ratio reduced to 80% AP from 90% AP.

name: Syndra
rationale:
Q cost decreased early.
Syndra’s 10.13 mana nerf was intended to bring her down in Pro play, but it was only somewhat effective, while also causing painful detriment to her early game. Now that she’s much less present in Pro, we’re reverting the change and will find another tactic if she poses a problem in the future.

lines.raw: Mana cost reduced to 40 to 80 from 60 to 80.

name: Thresh
rationale:
E cooldown increased.
With all his tools to keep his friends alive, Thresh is one of the best at peeling enemies off of otherwise vulnerable allies. Recently, he’s been dominating Pro play, so we’re curbing his power by targeting his E’s uptime.

lines.raw: Cooldown increased to 13 to 10 seconds from 11 to 9.

name: Viego
rationale:
Q base damage decreased; bonus damage against monsters increased; healing from damage against marked minions decreased.
Despite his last visit to the patch notes in 11.13, Viego’s continued to be a popular pick in all his roles. We’re taking another pass by targeting his solo lane power and compensating with additional monster damage in the hopes he’ll end up in a more balanced state long-term.

lines.attribute: Now responds to Shadow Isles voice interactions rather than Demacian.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Now responds to Shadow Isles voice interactions rather than Demacian.

lines.attribute: Now gains the bonus range from R.
lines.raw: Undocumented/Bug Fix: Now gains the bonus range from R.

lines.ability: Q - Blade of the Ruined King
lines.raw: Base damage reduced to 15 to 75 from 25 to 85.

lines.ability: Q - Blade of the Ruined King
lines.raw: Bonus monster damage increased to 20 from 10.

lines.ability: Q - Blade of the Ruined King
lines.raw: Healing against minions reduced to 10% from 50%.

name: Wukong
rationale:
Base health regen decreased.
Wukong’s able to stay healthy in lane, even after taking a beating. We’re lowering his sustain so that while he remains a strong duelist, he’ll need more time to lick his wounds.

lines.raw: Base health regeneration reduced to 2.5 from 4.

name: Xayah
rationale:
R cooldown decreased.
Xayah’s been dragging behind the rest of the flock. Some spice should really let her feathers fly.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 140 to 100 seconds from 160 to 130.

lines.attribute: Taunt voice lines for Ezreal and Lux have been restored.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Taunt voice lines for Ezreal and Lux have been restored.

name: Hullbreaker
rationale: Hullbreaker could use some help as the game reaches later phases of the game. We’re giving more durability for anyone who’s hunting alone.

lines.raw: Boarding Party bonus resistances increased to 20 to 60 from 20 to 45.
Boarding Party minion bonus resistances increased to 20*3 to 60*3 from 20*3 to 45*3.

lines.attribute: All summoner spells (excluding Flash) and item actives are now disabled while the hook is attached or in flight.
lines.raw: Undocumented/New Effect: All summoner spells (excluding Flash) and item actives are now disabled while the hook is attached or in flight.

lines.attribute: Using the active for Stopwatch / Zhonya's Hourglass now ends the swing prematurely.
lines.raw: Undocumented/New Effect: Using the active for Stopwatch / Zhonya's Hourglass now ends the swing prematurely.

name: Diana
rationale:
Passive damage to non-epic monsters decreased.
Since our 11.8 changes, Diana’s become a popular jungle pick, and a powerful one at that, especially in competitive play. Although we’re happy that Diana’s found a second home, she’s a little too strong. To nudge down her jungle strength, we’re nerfing her jungle clear.

lines.raw: Damage against monsters reduced to 250% from 300%.

name: Fiora
rationale:
E cooldown increased later.
Fiora's been on the strong side for a while, especially in higher levels of play. We're bringing down her split pushing and tower whacking power in mid to late phases of the game.

lines.raw: Cooldown increased to 11 to 7 seconds from 11 to 5.

lines.attribute: Old God Ivern: Renamed to Old God Ivern from Elderwood Ivern.
lines.raw: Renamed to Old God Ivern from Elderwood Ivern.

name: Jarvan IV
rationale:
Passive damage increased. R bonus damage ratio increased.
The Exemplar of Demacia hasn’t been excelling in any level of play. We’re amping up Cataclysm to help him make a bigger impact while also buffing his dueling and clearing potential.

lines.raw: Health ratio increased to 10% of the target's current health from 8%.
Bonus AD ratio increased to 180% bonus AD from 150%.

name: Jhin
rationale:
W damage increased. R minimum damage ratio increased.
Jhin has been feeling rather lackluster, and he hasn’t been making the cut into most games. With a deadlier flourish and an even deadlier finale, he’ll have a better shot at picking off enemies when playing off of allies and in key fights.

lines.raw: Base damage increased to 60 to 200 from 50 to 190.
Non-champion base damage increased to 45 to 150 from 37.5 to 142.5.
Minimum AD ratio increased to 25% AD from 20% AD.
Maximum AD ratio increased to 100% AD from 80% AD.

name: Karma
rationale:
Passive on-hit cooldown reduction removed; cooldown reduction from abilities now flat. Q base damage decreased early; cooldown increased early and decreased later; cost decreased. Q2 initial damage increased. E base shield increased later; bonus movement speed now flat; Defiance now only grants allies bonus movement speed.
Karma’s been much stronger in coordinated Pro play than in solo queue for a while. Rather than continuing to make minor changes, we're attempting to make bigger ones to help Karma succeed in the hands of all players. To do so, we’re targeting her consistent early game pressure and waveclear, along with her R-E shield-and-speed buff for her full team. In return, we’re rewarding her with more Mantras when she lands abilities on champions, which will also be helped by her Q’s lower cooldown and cost. We’re also strengthening her R-Q so that she’s still able to obliterate her foes when she’s on her own.

lines.attribute: Basic attacks against enemy champions no longer reduce Mantra cooldown by 1 second.
lines.raw: Removed: Basic attacks against enemy champions no longer reduce Mantra cooldown by 1 second.
Mantra cooldown reduction from spells increased to 5 seconds at all levels from 2 to 5.
Cooldown changed to 9 to 5 seconds from 8 to 6.
Mana cost reduced to 45 from 55.
Base damage reduced to 70 to 270 from 90 to 270.
Inner Flame bonus base damage increased to 40 to 220 from 25 to 175.
Base shield increased to 80 to 260 from 80 to 240.
Bonus movement speed reduced to 40% at all ranks from 40 to 60%.

lines.attribute: Secondary targets now only receive 12% bonus movement speed instead of the same amount as Inspire (40%).
lines.raw: New Effect: Secondary targets now only receive 12% bonus movement speed instead of the same amount as Inspire (40%).

name: Lee Sin
rationale:
W omnivamp decreased.
Lee Sin came out of our 11.13 nerfs kicking, making his way from dominating lanes straight into dominating the jungle. This time, we’re laying down a straightforward nerf that should curb his early- to mid-game dueling power.

lines.raw: Life steal and spell vamp reduced to 5 to 25% from 10 to 30%.

name: Lulu
rationale:
W cooldown increased. R cooldown increased early.
While Lulu’s power in Average play is balanced, she’s strong in Skilled and even stronger in Elite. Back in patch 11.9, we purposefully buffed Lulu, targeting these skill brackets by reducing the cooldown on her W and increasing its bonus attack speed. The increased uptime on reliable peel made her a highly frustrating champion to play against, which has been reflected in her high ban rates. To get her back in action, we’re reverting the buff on her Skilled-skewed mechanic of instant CC and increasing her R cooldown.

lines.raw: Cooldown increased to 16 to 12 seconds from 15 to 11.
Cooldown increased to 120 to 80 seconds from 110 to 80.

name: Maokai
rationale:
Passive heal increased. E detonation damage decreased.
Top Maokai has been struggling to stay in lane even with his tank builds, so we’re increasing his sustain. On the other hand, Support Mao and his saplings have been causing a commotion in the bot lane, where AP builds offer powerful scaling. Maokai will still have strong poke, but we’re toning it down. One more thing: Maokai's original passive values were bugged. He was healing for less of his maximum health (5-13% instead of 6-13%) and it wasn’t scaling properly (it was scaling linearly at every level instead of its intended breakpoints of level 1/6/9…). so the previous values of his passive’s heal reflect the bugged, in-game values. Now, the scaling has been corrected, and the heal from his maximum health has an even bigger bump than his tooltip would have you believe.

lines.raw: Heal health ratio increased to 7 / 8.5 / 10 to 15% maximum health from 6 / 7.5 / 9 to 13%.

name: Amumu
rationale:
Q now has 2 charges. W damage increased early; decreased late. R stun duration no longer scales. Health and armor growth decreased.
Our sad little mummy's been left out of high level play for ages. While there's an easy joke here about Amumu having no friends, we wanted to address this long-standing problem and ensure he can find his way in the world of modern League. In particular, we wanted to up his engage threat in the early game where high MMR players prioritize securing small leads that can snowball into victory. One subtle benefit of 2-charge Q, beyond the obvious stuff: It reduces the pressure to spam Q on cooldown, since you aren't "wasting" uptime by holding onto your first charge as long as the second is recharging. This creates a new avenue for skill expression: When should Amumu use both charges, and when should he hold one? All this said, Amumu's late game has never really been his problem. We tossed in a few nerfs to his later scaling to even out his newly-increased potential to get ahead early. From a raw stats perspective, he'll be innately weaker at higher levels, but now he'll get there faster and have more items when he does.
As a reminder, W ticks twice per second, so each tick deals half the listed damage below!

As a result, we've had to limit his scaling in a way that's been unsatisfying for Gangplank players, given that late game power has traditionally been core to his identity. We're walking back on that plank by lowering his early advantages and bringing them back ashore in late game with extra crit-skewed spice. More barrels!

AP Lucian is also getting some compensation buffs since we know it's a fun (although weak) build that gets affected by these AD-encouraging changes. rationale: Divine Sunderer has been the go-to choice for fighters all across the spectrum, and even some marksmen. We're looking to nerf its generic power to let its more aggressive item competitors outshine it when they're supposed to.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where it was not displaying the actual number of champions rooted and slowed by the item's active in the inventory tooltip.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where it was not displaying the actual number of champions rooted and slowed by the item's active in the inventory tooltip.

name: Hullbreaker
rationale: While Hullbreaker is a strong early rush on a few champions, its opportunity cost is too large to be a great choice compared to other Legendary fighter items that have more generic value. We're giving it a bit of beef so that players feel a bit more inclined to go on a raiding party.

lines.raw: Health increased to 400 from 300.

lines.attribute: No longer builds into Youmuu's Ghostblade.
lines.raw: No longer builds into Youmuu's Ghostblade.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where the Cloth Armor and Refillable Potion starting bundle would display "+1 More" text even though it does not grant a third item.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where the Cloth Armor and Refillable Potion starting bundle would display "+1 More" text even though it does not grant a third item.

name: Serpent's Fang
rationale: Rather than being a situational item against shield-heavy enemies, Serpent's Fang has become a staple in the second item slot for physical assassins. We want to preserve its low gold cost so that it's still an accessible situational pickup, but with stats that are more proportional.

lines.raw: Lethality reduced to 12 from 18.

name: Wit's End
rationale: Wit's End has become a powerful early rush item for a variety of attack speed champions. While it's good to offer early attack speed options, Wit's End often becomes the best choice regardless of how much magic damage the enemy team has. We're reshaping its damage scaling so that it's just as powerful late but isn't only being picked up for its early damage value.

lines.raw: Fray damage changed to 15 / 25 / 35 / 45 / 55 / 65 / 75 / 76.25 / 77.5 / 78.75 / 80 from 15 to 80. Formula changed.

name: Youmuu's Ghostblade
rationale: Youmuu's went from being a beloved aggressive pick to an underutilized niche item. We nerfed its generic power last season to give room for other situational items, but we're seeing now that we went a little too far. AD assassins have been yearning for a good general item rather than defaulting to counter pick-ups like Serpent's Fang. So, *drumroll please*... we're reverting the patch 10.23 changes and welcoming back 2020’s Youmuu's Ghostblade!

lines.attribute: New Recipe: Serrated Dirk + Caulfield's Warhammer + 700 gold = 2900 gold.: Old Recipe: Serrated Dirk + Pickaxe + 1025 gold = 3000 gold.
lines.raw: Old Recipe: Serrated Dirk + Pickaxe + 1025 gold = 3000 gold.
Ability haste increased to 15 from 0.
Attack damage reduced to 55 from 60.

name: Fleet Footwork
rationale: Fleet Footwork just hasn't been a very good pick for marksmen. Rather than a straight buff to make it more viable, we're increasing healing against champions for everyone and reducing healing against minions depending on attack type to avoid too much power in lane sustain. Healing against minions for melee is getting reduced more than ranged because melee champions have already been using it very effectively for that very reason, making this an overall buff for ranged and closer to neutral for melee.

lines.raw: Healing against minions reduced to 20% (melee) / 10% (ranged) from 100% (melee) / 20% (ranged).
Base heal increased to 10 to 100 from 3 to 60.
Bonus AD ratio increased to 40% bonus AD from 30%.
AP ratio increased to 30% AP from 20% AP.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where it was healing against wards. Its tooltip now also correctly displays the total amount of healing done.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where it was healing against wards. Its tooltip now also correctly displays the total amount of healing done.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where breaking a spell shield on him would interrupt the ability.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where breaking a spell shield on him would interrupt the ability.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where he was unable to cancel the ability while being silenced.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where he was unable to cancel the ability while being silenced.

name: Aphelios
rationale:
Base attack damage decreased.
Aphelios' early game is very consistent right now, which explains his elevated presence in Pro play recently. We're nerfing his laning phase to make it harder for him to get to his first item and scale. Uh, something something moonstones.

lines.raw: Base attack damage reduced to 55 from 57.

name: Ashe
rationale:
W cooldown increased early.
Ashe's lane control early game goes a bit too far and wide. We're giving her opponents more space to play back without getting pierced by cones and cones of crystalline arrows.

lines.raw: Cooldown increased to 18 to 4 seconds from 14 to 4.

name: Camille
rationale:
Passive cooldown increased early.
Camille's steel-like resilience is a bit too high for her scaling power, so we're nerfing her shield early to make her more vulnerable in lane.

lines.raw: Cooldown increased to 20 to 10 seconds from 16 to 10.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where it would get cancelled upon using any consumables.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where it would get cancelled upon using any consumables.

lines.attribute: Crime City Nightmare Darius: Heavier sound effects for Hemorrhage and Noxian Guillotine.
lines.raw: Heavier sound effects for Hemorrhage and Noxian Guillotine.

name: Dr. Mundo
rationale:
Q maximum damage to monsters increased. R grants extra base HP on-cast instead of healing for missing health; healing over time decreased late.
While it's true that Grievous Wounds is the standard against healing champs, it's left Dr. Mundo rather sickly at higher levels of play. Anti-healing items tend to undermine champions like him and Soraka whose entire identities are designed around big beefy heals. The immediate base health gained from his ult will now ignore Grievous Wounds, but the healing over time will still be affected by it. This should make the anti-heal effect less sharp of a counter but still enough of a jab to hurt Mundo good. We're also juicing up his jungle potential to make him more appealing as a Pro flex pick.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where he would ignore all subsequent CC from a dragon or Rift Herald after it broke his Goes Where He Pleases spell shield once.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where he would ignore all subsequent CC from a dragon or Rift Herald after it broke his Goes Where He Pleases spell shield once.
Damage cap against monsters increased to 350 to 650 from 300 to 500.

lines.attribute: On cast, now grants him 15 to 25% missing health as base health for the duration of the ability.
lines.raw: New Effect: On cast, now grants him 15 to 25% missing health as base health for the duration of the ability.

lines.attribute: No longer heals for 20% missing health on cast.
lines.raw: Removed: No longer heals for 20% missing health on cast.
Health regeneration reduced to 20 to 60% maximum health from 20 to 70%.

name: Draven
rationale:
R now executes based on Adoration stacks.
We're giving the Glorious Executioner something he's wanted for a long time—an execute—but putting it on the ability in his kit with the most counterplay. Rather than just staying away from him the entire game, opponents will now be more incentivized to kill Draven than ever before. Let the games begin.

lines.attribute: Adoration stack count updates will now be displayed in All chat, not just Team chat.
lines.raw: Adoration stack count updates will now be displayed in All chat, not just Team chat.

lines.attribute: Now executes enemy champions with health that is less than or is left below the current number of League of Draven stacks.
lines.raw: New Effect: Now executes enemy champions with health that is less than or is left below the current number of League of Draven stacks.

lines.attribute: Updated the tooltip to include the additional damage dealt against jungle monsters.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Updated the tooltip to include the additional damage dealt against jungle monsters.

name: Fizz
rationale:
Passive damage reduction increased against basic attacks. W base damage increased. R damage reduced.
A lot of Fizz's power is in his ult, which is inconsistent in skilled play since more players at that level know to either dodge or Zhonya's it. His R will still pack a punch, but we're borrowing some of its bite and putting it into his early game threat with W as well as giving him a thicker skin against basic attacks to help his survivability in lane.

lines.attribute: Damage reduction against champion basic attack is increased to 8 (+ 2% AP).
lines.raw: New Effect: Damage reduction against champion basic attack is increased to 8 (+ 2% AP).
On-hit base damage increased to 20 to 40 from 10 to 30.
Guppy base damage reduced to 150 to 300 from 150 to 350.
Chomper base damage reduced to 200 to 350 from 225 to 425.
Gigalodon base damage reduced to 250 to 400 from 300 to 500.
Guppy AP ratio reduced to 70% AP from 80% AP.
Chomper AP ratio reduced to 85% AP from 100% AP.
Gigalodon AP ratio reduced to 100% AP from 120% AP.

name: Gangplank
rationale:
Base health and health growth increased.
Last patch, we changed Gangplank's Q so that it would count as a ranged instead of melee attack. He's lost a lot of durability now that he doesn't benefit as much from Grasp of the Undying (and thus the rest of the Resolve tree) anymore. Giving this pirate some of his burliness back to help him survive the choppy waters of early top lane.

lines.raw: Base health increased to 570 from 540.
Health growth increased to 90 from 82.

name: Jayce
rationale:
Passive duration decreased.
Jayce is an all-around power slam in highly skilled hands. Rather than reduce his wattage damage output, we're turning down his ability to outrun ganks and quickly traverse the map, both of which are particularly useful for the Pro scene.

lines.attribute: Bonus movement speed and ghosting duration
lines.raw: Bonus movement speed and ghosting duration reduced to 0.75 seconds from 1.25.

name: Jinx
rationale:
Q mana cost reduced early for Fishbones.
We're boosting Jinx's lane push power to make her a more viable pick and increase her early game overall. Katchoo!

lines.raw: Fishbones mana cost reduced to 16 to 20 from 20 at all ranks.

name: Kai'Sa
rationale:
E cooldown reduced late.
Kai'Sa represents a hypercarry style that we haven't seen much of in this meta's bully-focused bot lane. Since she's known for her scaling capability, we're buffing exactly that while keeping both her lane vulnerability and Q burst damage intact.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 16 to 10 seconds from 16 to 12.

name: Kalista
rationale:
R knockup duration decreased early.
Kalista's ult with a melee support is almost guaranteed to kill with chain CC, especially in Pro-level high coordination gank setups. We’re giving her opponents a slightly bigger window to escape her wrath.

lines.raw: Knock up duration reduced to 1 to 2 seconds from 1.5 to 2.

name: Karma
rationale:
Base armor increased. E base shield increased.
Karma's changes in 11.16 were effective at reducing her dominance in Pro play while avoiding major nerfs to her everywhere else. Since she's been on the weaker side overall, we're upping her winrate across the board with some generic buffs. She really does always catch up, huh?

lines.raw: Base armor increased to 28 from 26.
Base shield increased to 90 to 270 from 80 to 260.

name: Kog'Maw
rationale:
E AP scaling increased.
AD Kog is in a healthy spot now, but AP Kog has all but shriveled up. While our very hungry caterpillar should be weaker than other champions early in the game, he simply hasn't been a viable pick mid. We're buffing his waveclear to more reasonable levels to help him become the beautiful butterfly he really is.

lines.raw: AP ratio increased to 70% AP from 50% AP.

name: Lee Sin
rationale:
Base attack damage decreased.
Despite all his previous nerfs, Lee Sin has still been a super duper high priority Pro pick in jungle. (The blind monk was so popular, he got either picked or banned in 100% of LCK games during patch 11.16!) Tapping him down yet again with an early game nerf to clear the jungle champ pool for Worlds.

lines.raw: Base attack damage reduced to 68 from 70.

name: Lillia
rationale:
Base health regen decreased. Passive healing on large monsters increased. Q stack duration increased. E cooldown decreased.
Lillia's been very strong in top lane, limiting our ability to buff her jungling capabilities. Her early sustain will now be fairly conditional on hitting jungle monsters, making her a riskier pick in aggressive lanes and freeing up room for us to help her prance, dance, and—oops!—trip in the jungle.

lines.raw: Base health regeneration reduced to 2.5 from 7.5.
Health regeneration growth reduced to 0.55 from 0.75.
Base heal against monsters increased to 27 to 103.5 from 18 to 94.
Bonus movement speed duration increased to 6.5 seconds from 5.5.
Cooldown reduced to 16 seconds from 18.

lines.attribute: Fixed the tooltip so that it no longer states dealing bonus damage to monsters.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed the tooltip so that it no longer states dealing bonus damage to monsters.

name: Miss Fortune
rationale:
Number of R waves increased.
Miss Fortune has unfortunately been missing out on wins at all levels of play. Giving her ult some more bang to spice up the wombo combos. We've got a good feeling about this. ;)

lines.raw: Number of waves increased to 14 to 18 from 12 to 16.

name: Morgana
rationale:
E cooldown decreased.
Morgana has fallen as a support in both Average and Pro play. Giving her more access to her unique CC blocking shield should help, especially in matchups where she's historically excelled. (Looking at you, hard stun and knockup supports.)

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 24 to 16 seconds from 26 to 18.

lines.attribute: Base voice lines have been remastered to sound clearer, cleaner, and smoother.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Base voice lines have been remastered to sound clearer, cleaner, and smoother.

name: Qiyana
rationale:
Base attack speed increased. Health regen decreased. Q damage against monsters increased. E+Q combo targeting changed. E base damage decreased.
We removed Qiyana's ability to jungle back when she was a dominant mid/jungle flex pick in Pro. Her standings in mid have gone down since then, so we're cautiously optimistic about reintroducing her to the jungle. Our empress also has a staggeringly high-tier-biased winrate (sort of like Amumu, but the inverse). A likely reason for this skew is that her E+Q auto-aim combo can't be dodged at all, invalidating many would-be outplays which feels really bad. We're revising its targeting mechanisms to empower opponents who are quick enough to dare challenge her.

lines.raw: Base health regeneration reduced to 7.5 from 9.
Base attack speed increased to 0.688 from 0.625.
Attack speed ratio unchanged.

lines.ability: Q - Edge of Ixtal / Elemental Wrath
lines.raw: Damage against monsters increased to 125% from 100%.

lines.ability: Q - Edge of Ixtal / Elemental Wrath
lines.attribute: If cast during Audacity and the target uses a dash or blink or is no longer in vision during the dash, the ability will now aim at the target's last position prior to them starting the dash or blink or being in vision.
lines.raw: New Effect: If cast during Audacity and the target uses a dash or blink or is no longer in vision during the dash, the ability will now aim at the target's last position prior to them starting the dash or blink or being in vision.
Base damage reduced to 50 to 170 from 60 to 180.

name: Renekton
rationale:
Empowered W stun duration decreased; empowered W lockout now matches normal W behavior.
Renekton continues to live up to his name in Pro play, butchering his foes left and right. We're nerfing his crowd control specifically by changing the way his W works when empowered by Passive - Reign of Anger. This'll make it notably harder for him to lock down targets throughout the game, both in lane ganks and teamfights. To explain that weird self-lockout note below: Previously, Renekton was able to bypass his empowered W's additional lockout by attacking or moving at just the right time. We're making this decreased lockout time the baseline so the croc isn't CCing himself for almost as long as his target.

lines.raw: Empowered stun duration reduced to 1 second from 1.5.
Empowered self-lockout duration reduced to 0.52 seconds from 0.75.

name: Rumble
rationale:
Passive bonus attack speed decreased early; now scales with level. W cooldown decreased and no longer scales.
In 11.13, we simmered down Rumble's early game to temper his extreme jungle power in Pro play. This ended up being a huge damper to Rumble players all around, so we're rekindling his flame by buffing that back and nerfing his early jungle clear using a different approach. Now we're cookin'!

lines.raw: Bonus attack speed changed to 20 to 80% from 50% at all levels.
Cooldown reduced to 6 seconds at all ranks from 7 to 6.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where it did not apply life steal when cast during Wild Rush.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where it did not apply life steal when cast during Wild Rush.

lines.attribute: Block effect now properly takes priority over shield mitigations.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Block effect now properly takes priority over shield mitigations.

name: Singed
rationale:
Damage dealt with Q during R now applies Grievous Wounds.
As a damage-over-time champion in the top lane, Singed can struggle to make his damage stick against enemy healing. We're juicing up the mad chemist's signature concoction so he can counteract this when going for that kill with his ultimate... Slowly, but surely.

lines.attribute: Updated the tooltip to include its slow percentage.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Updated the tooltip to include its slow percentage.

lines.attribute: While active, Poison Trail now applies 40% Grievous Wounds for 1 second.
lines.raw: New Effect: While active, Poison Trail now applies 40% Grievous Wounds for 1 second.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where buffing an ally with the Melody aura did not grant her a Mana Charge stack on Tear of the Goddess.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where buffing an ally with the Melody aura did not grant her a Mana Charge stack on Tear of the Goddess.

lines.attribute: Fixed a bug where it would incorrectly grant a stack of Accelerando even if negated by a spell shield.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where it would incorrectly grant a stack of Accelerando even if negated by a spell shield.

name: Soraka
rationale:
R now clears Grievous Wounds before healing.
Like Dr. Mundo, Soraka's been particularly pained by Grievous Wounds over the past few seasons. While anti-healing items should be a valid counter to Soraka's sustain, it's starting to severely impede on her core gameplay. We're making every Soraka player's wish come true by giving her a limited tool to respond and make those clutch heals, but only on her ult (which has a pretty long cooldown).

lines.attribute: Updated the tooltip to state that it deals damage to enemy champions only.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Updated the tooltip to state that it deals damage to enemy champions only.

lines.attribute: Now removes Grievous Wounds from all targets before granting the heal.
lines.raw: New Effect: Now removes Grievous Wounds from all targets before granting the heal.

name: Taliyah
rationale:
Casting Q on Worked Ground now refunds its cooldown. Worked Ground radius and duration decreased.
Taliyah's found solid footing in the jungle but she's still on shaky ground in mid. Her kit has a number of rules that feel more punishing than empowering, so we're loosening up by reframing Worked Ground as an optional way to cast successive Qs rather than a severe movement tax on her higher-damage full Qs.

lines.attribute: Casting on Worked Ground now refunds 50% of its cooldown, but not below 1 second.
lines.raw: New Effect: Casting on Worked Ground now refunds 50% of its cooldown, but not below 1 second.
Worked Ground duration reduced to 25 seconds from 45.
Worked Ground size reduced to 300 units from 450.

name: Talon
rationale:
Q base damage decreased late. W now deals bonus damage vs monsters.
We're attempting to introduce some new assassin-y options into the jungle meta. Talon's got a clear advantage here with his high-mobility E—hardcore parkour!—so increasing his clear speed should make him a reasonable option in the role. Talon mid is also getting a little too powerful, so we're dulling his blades in late game a smidge.

lines.raw: Base damage reduced to 65 to 145 from 65 to 165.
Damage against monsters increased to 150% from 100%.

name: Thresh
rationale:
Base Move Speed decreased. E passive damage decreased early; bonus damage per Soul increased.
Thresh has arguably been the best support champ in Pro meta for much of the year despite multiple nerfs. We're taking a larger swing here at his ability to nullify popular melee support engages (think Leona, Nautilus, Rell) as well as his offensive threat to those same laners. Since this is a pretty big nerf, we're compensating some of the lost early damage with better Soul scaling, which is usually lower priority in Pro.

lines.raw: Base movement speed reduced to 330 from 335.
Minimum damage per soul increased to 1.5 from 1.
Maximum damage AD ratio reduced to 80 to 200% AD from 100 to 200% AD.
Maximum damage per soul increased to 1.5 from 1.

name: Trundle
rationale:
E slow decreased.
Trundle's become a potent jungle/support flex pick in professional play. We're tamping down the troll king's power in his secondary role a bit by nerfing his E, which supports typically max first and junglers usually max third.

lines.raw: Slow strength reduced to 30 to 46% from 32 to 60%.

lines.attribute: Crime City Nightmare Twisted Fate: New unique sound effect for basic attacks.
lines.raw: New unique sound effect for basic attacks.

lines.attribute: Crime City Nightmare Twisted Fate: Heavier sound effects for empowered basic attacks.
lines.raw: Heavier sound effects for empowered basic attacks.

name: Twitch
rationale:
R bonus AD increased.
Many of Twitch's skirmishes in higher level play involve sneaking around and blasting his enemies with his ult. We're ripening the damage only on his R to make his best-case surprise engagements more powerful without overbuffing his jungle or non-ultimate DPS.

lines.raw: Bonus attack damage increased to 40 to 70 from 30 to 60.

name: Urgot
rationale:
Q cooldown and mana cost reduced.
Urgot is pretty solid, but he struggles against ranged champions that often dominate the Pro top lane meta. This is a light buff that'll help him handle those situations more reliably.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 10 to 8 seconds from 12 to 8.
Mana cost reduced to 70 from 80.

name: Varus
rationale:
Base AD decreased. Passive bonus AS decreased early but increases with levels.
Varus has been bullying his lanes pretty hard, especially in Pro play. These changes should weaken his early game a bit on all fronts.

lines.raw: Base attack damage reduced to 59 from 61.

lines.attribute: Base bonus attack speed on non-champion kill
lines.raw: Base bonus attack speed on non-champion kill reduced to 10 to 20% from 20% at all levels.

lines.attribute: Can no longer access Living Forge to forge items while possessing him.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Can no longer access Living Forge to forge items while possessing him.

name: Yone
rationale:
W shielding per champion hit after the first increased.
Despite his reasonable power level in Average play, Yone falls behind at higher skill bands. Rather than directly buffing his 1v1 or assassination potential, we're enhancing one of Yone's more skill-based outputs on W to improve his skirmishing and teamfighting when piloted well.

lines.attribute: Bonus shield per subsequent champion hit
lines.raw: Bonus shield per subsequent champion hit increased to 50% from 25%.

name: Yuumi
rationale:
Passive cooldown decreased.
Yuumi can make for a catty bot lane when chosen as a niche pick. We're encouraging her to play more aggressively early so that she can be more influential in lane. This'll also give enemies more opportunities to pet play with engage the kitty early on. These dynamic changes should be less frustrating for both Yuumi players and opponents alike, but if her claws get a bit too sharp, we'll look to trim the less interactive parts of her kit like her late-game scaling and sustain while keeping her early game power feisty.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 14 to 6 seconds from 18 to 6.

name: Zed
rationale:
Passive deals bonus damage against monsters.
Zed's another assassin we're attempting to introduce into the jungle meta. Our buffs to Zed jungle earlier in the season didn't really land, so we're taking another stab at making him viable in the role by buffing his passive's damage vs monsters again.

lines.raw: Monster damage increased to 200% from 100%.

name: Zoe
rationale:
E cooldown decreased.
Zoe was putting way too many champions to sleep, so we increased her E cooldown back in 9.6. Now that she's no longer as much of a nightmare, we're reverting the nerf so she can contribute more throughout a fight. Prepare for trouble. And make it bubble.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 16 to 12 seconds from 20 to 14.

name: Ravenous Hydra
rationale: If an enemy champion stands next to the tower you're attacking, Ravenous Hydra's AoE passive triggers turret aggro, which is rather counterintuitive to split-pushing top laners who want to take down towers.

lines.attribute: Removed: Cleave no longer works against structures.: The tooltip now also mentions this.
lines.raw: The tooltip now also mentions this.

lines.attribute: Tooltip now mentions that Cleave does not work against structures.
lines.raw: Tooltip now mentions that Cleave does not work against structures.

name: Titanic Hydra
rationale: Repeat the above except say "Titanic" instead of "Ravenous". We put a titanic amount of effort into writing this paragraph.

lines.attribute: Cleave's cone damage no longer triggers against structures. On-hit damage still applies.
lines.raw: Removed: Cleave's cone damage no longer triggers against structures. On-hit damage still applies.

lines.attribute: The tooltip now also mentions this.
lines.raw: The tooltip now also mentions this.

name: Umbral Glaive
rationale: Umbral Glaive's stats and cost were bumped up last preseason to match it more closely with other lethality-focused Legendary items. However, this left it at a pretty weak state while also pricing it out of budget for supports like Senna and Pyke. We're shrinking the cost yet again and (hopefully!) bringing lethality supports back into Pro play.

lines.raw: Total cost reduced to 2400 gold from 2600 gold.
Combine cost reduced to 600 gold from 800 gold.
Lethality reduced to 10 from 12.

name: Predator
rationale: Increasing Predator's ganking power to push it up to Pro viability for junglers who gotta go fast—like former users Skarner, Hecarim, and Lillia.

lines.raw: Maximum bonus movement speed increased to 60% from 45%.

lines.attribute: Bonus movement speed ramp up time
lines.raw: Bonus movement speed ramp up time reduced to 1 second from 1.5.

name: Aatrox
rationale:
W cooldown decreased.
Aatrox's W cooldown was heavily nerfed in patch 9.9 in an effort to reduce his Pro domination. He's not running over the Pro scene anymore, so we're loosening his chains a bit.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 20 to 14 seconds from 26 to 14.

name: Akali
rationale:
Base health regen increased.
In a rare flip of events, Akali has room for some power at all levels of play. We're taking this opportunity to make her missteps a bit more forgiving in a way that doesn't win her more fights, but instead helps her subtly throughout her games.

lines.raw: Base health regeneration increased to 9 from 8.
Health regeneration growth increased to 0.9 from 0.5.

lines.attribute: If cast and the hook fails to attach to terrain while Avengerang missile was in flight, Avengerang can no longer be cast again immediately.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: If cast and the hook fails to attach to terrain while Avengerang missile was in flight, Avengerang can no longer be cast again immediately.

lines.attribute: Missile VFX no longer goes out of sync and appears further away than it actually is to the enemies' point of view when the caster enters vision.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Missile VFX no longer goes out of sync and appears further away than it actually is to the enemies' point of view when the caster enters vision.

lines.attribute: Now correctly blocks the damage dealt by Shock Blast if it was the first instance of champion damage against the barrier.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Now correctly blocks the damage dealt by Shock Blast if it was the first instance of champion damage against the barrier.

name: Cho'Gath
rationale:
Q cooldown decreased.
Despite being terrifyingly tanky, Cho'Gath is still weak across the board. We're increasing his CC and zoning capabilities so that he has more influence in fights.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 6 seconds from 7.

lines.attribute: Base voice lines have been remastered to sound clearer and more consistent.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Base voice lines have been remastered to sound clearer and more consistent.

name: Fizz
rationale:
Passive damage reduction against basic attacks removed. W damage reduced. E cooldown decreased late. R damage increased.
The 11.18 changes were an unintentional nerf to Fizz. We overestimated the Passive and W buffs and underestimated the R nerf. Rather than trying to fine tune those changes, we're reverting them entirely and doing a simpler buff instead. Go fish!

lines.attribute: Damage reduction against champion basic attacks is no longer increased to 8 (+ 2% AP).
lines.raw: Removed: Damage reduction against champion basic attacks is no longer increased to 8 (+ 2% AP).
On-hit base damage reduced to 10 to 30 from 20 to 40.
Cooldown reduced to 16 to 8 seconds from 16 to 10.
Guppy base damage increased to 150 to 350 from 150 to 300.
Chomper base damage increased to 225 to 425 from 200 to 350.
Gigalodon base damage increased to 300 to 500 from 250 to 400.
Guppy AP ratio increased to 80% AP from 70% AP.
Chomper AP ratio increased to 100% AP from 85% AP.
Gigalodon AP ratio increased to 120% AP from 100% AP.

name: Galio
rationale:
W cooldown now decreases with rank.
Galio's nerf back in 11.10 turned out to be a bit too effective on his Elite performance. We're bringing him back to life at that skill level by partially reverting those changes.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 18 to 16 seconds from 18 at all ranks.

name: Gragas
rationale:
W damage AP scaling increased.
Gragas didn't benefit much from the Predator changes last patch, so he's still pretty weak. We're helping his various AP builds pack more of a punch and speed up his mid-game clear. However, please remember to always drink responsibly.

lines.raw: Damage AP ratio increased to 70% AP from 60% AP.

name: Gwen
rationale:
Base health regen increased.
Gwen's E nerf in 11.15 was effective in snipping her overwhelming early lane power, especially in Pro. Now, similar to Akali's situation, there's room to weave in some more durability for Gwen players at all levels.

name: Kennen
rationale:
Q damage decreased.
Kennen's been on a dramatic rise in Pro priority since our changes in 11.15. We’re reducing his power by walking back on those changes slightly.

name: Mordekaiser
rationale:
E cooldown decreased early.
Mordekaiser's bummed that he’s been falling behind his peers. We don’t want the god of metal to be the butt of jokes, so we’re buffing him for skilled players by granting him more access to his most flexible spell.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 18 to 10 seconds from 22 to 10.

lines.raw: New Effect: Empowered attack's damage now triggers spell effects.

name: Poppy
rationale:
Passive cooldown decreased.
Poppy hasn't been looking too heroic lately, especially in top lane. We're enhancing her early lane power so that she can take greater advantage of favorable matchups, which should also make her more appealing as a Pro pick in specific situations.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 13 to 7 from 16 to 8.

name: Qiyana
rationale:
E+Q combo targeting on dashing targets adjusted. Q bonus damage against monsters increased.
Before 11.18, Qiyana's E+Q auto aim combo used to be undodgeable. We changed her E+Q targeting mechanism last patch so that enemies could escape by dashing or flashing away. However, that version of the combo generously treated every enemy dash as an attempt to dodge Qiyana's combo, and it turns out this isn't always the case. A dashing enemy might be headed towards the same direction or even the exact same location as Qiyana's E. So in scenarios where the dashing enemy ends up still within Qiyana's default attack range, she'll maintain her auto aim. Lastly, Qiyana jungle is not quite playable yet, so we're bumping that up to give her a fair shot.

lines.raw: Damage against monsters increased to 150% from 125%.

lines.attribute: Edge of Ixtal autonomously aiming at Audacity target now also requires the enemy champion to be within Qiyana's basic attack range (150 units) at the end of the dash.
lines.raw: Edge of Ixtal autonomously aiming at Audacity target now also requires the enemy champion to be within Qiyana's basic attack range (150 units) at the end of the dash.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Cooldown can no longer be sometimes bypassed after casting Terrashape.

name: Renekton
rationale:
Base health and health growth increased. W self-lockout duration decreased and empowered animation sped up.
We over swung on Renekton's nerf last patch. We still believe reducing the stun on his empowered W was a step in the right direction to mitigate his Pro dominance, so we're improving its look and feel. We're also giving him more chances to start fights and increasing his tankiness.

lines.raw: Base health increased to 590 from 575.
Health growth increased to 92 from 87.
Empowered self-lockout duration reduced to 0.375 seconds from 0.525.
Cast animation time reduced.

name: Ryze
rationale:
Q AP ratio reduced. E cooldown increased.
Ryze has risen above the other mid laners in most regions. We're nerfing his overall output to ensure he doesn't completely dominate at Worlds.

lines.raw: AP ratio reduced to 40% AP from 45% AP.
Cooldown increased to 3.5 to 2.5 from 3.25 to 2.25.

name: Sejuani
rationale:
Q cooldown decreased and damage increased.
Sejuani has been a bit of a boar lately. We’re slightly boosting her damage and giving her more access to her Q so she can stir up some more action!

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 18 to 12 seconds from 20 to 12.
Base damage increased to 90 to 290 from 80 to 280.

name: Seraphine
rationale:
R cooldown decreased.
Seraphine's been weak across the board, so we're giving her some more chances to make sick beats plays instead of just sitting backstage to scale.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 160 to 100 seconds from 180 to 120.

name: Sion
rationale:
W shield increased.
Sion isn't doing so hot right now, so we're carefully buffing his shield to help him lane more stably.

lines.raw: Shield strength increased to 60 to 160 from 50 to 150.

name: Sona
rationale:
Base armor reduced. Passive damage bug fixed. Q can no longer target hidden enemies. Power Chord E bug fixed.
Sona's songs have been a bit too powerful, especially in Skilled play. In addition to a few bugfixes, we're nerfing her base defenses a bit, all of which should add up to an appropriate nerf for the virtuoso.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Power Chord empowered attack slow is now properly considered a slow debuff; no longer bypasses effects that affect slows.

name: Soraka
rationale:
R healing decreased.
Soraka got a bit too powerful with her new ability to cleanse Grievous Wounds before applying her buffed ult's heal. We still think this strategy works to help her against heal reduction, so we're just tapping down the numbers.

rationale:
Base mana and mana regen increased.
Our 11.15 nerfs to Sylas's Q and W restrained him more than intended. We're offering him back some power by easing up on his mana constraints in lane, allowing him to be more proactive with his spells earlier in the game.

Darius hasn't been all that commanding lately. We're buffing his sidelane pushing and dueling powers while making his W more of a one-point wonder.

Elise keeps getting trampled underfoot by monsters and foes in the jungle, so we're boosting her carapace to help her survivability. (That's spider-speak for defense, by the way.)

rationale:
W cooldown reduced and no longer scales; healing against minions and monsters increased.
Hecarim used to stampede over Pro play with his full tank builds but has since become more of a fighter. We're helping him continue in this new direction with a chance to get a second W cast in fights, plus a buff to his sustain and clear.

Passive bonus AD ratio at max stacks reduced.

Passive bonus damage reduced.
Jarvan IV's been dominating the jungle meta with his exemplary ganks and super fast clear. We're partially reverting his 11.16 buffs—more specifically, the part that helped his dueling and clearing capabilities.

Passive shield decreased.
Shen's tipping the top lane tank meta out of equilibrium. We're reverting the 10.15 buff to his shield to restore some of the balance.

name: Singed
rationale:
E base damage and AP ratio decreased.
The mad chemist has gotten a little out of hand ever since we added a couple tricks to his name, like Grievous Wounds on his R+Q. Reducing the output on one of his less signature moves should keep him in smog check.

Q damage to monsters hit by subsequent stones reduced.
Taliyah is doing a bit too well in the jungle after her latest set of buffs. We're helping her stay grounded without eroding her rediscovered powers in mid.

rationale:
E bonus armor decreased.
Graves' defensive dueling power makes his laning a little too consistent in some early matchups. We're reducing his burliness to give his opponents a chance to outplay the outlaw.

Passive attack speed increased. E range increased. R cooldown decreased.
Jinx is craving some excitement, so we're boosting her passive to make her pop-off moments really pop and letting her wreak more havoc across the map with her ult. Flame Chompers' range is also getting a slight increase to work better with Fishbones' basic attacks. Everybody, panic!

name: Goredrinker
rationale: At its core, Goredrinker is supposed to be a sustain Mythic that lets fighters outlast their enemies with well-timed Thirsting Slashes. While wanting to sustain through a fight isn't unique to fighters, it's a big part of their class identity: They have the best tools to stay on the offensive at low health (ex. the dream Illaoi ult that lets her turn a 1v5). At the same time, this is a risky niche to fill: Two of our bigger rough patches since the item update have been damage and healing, and Goredrinker offers both. We've seen this risk play out over the course of the season, with Goredrinker becoming the dominant Mythic pick for fighters due to offering the best sustain without making sufficient tradeoffs on the damage front. As further evidence, assassins have been taking Goredrinker over their own Mythics. Assassins are designed to kill quickly, so they shouldn't be valuing an item that indexes so much into sustain and strength at low health. Between its 1.0 AD ratio and its heal, Goredrinker's active is just too valuable as another button in assassin combos that also lets them shrug off any damage they take while eviscerating their target. In order to move Goredrinker back into its sustain niche, we're removing its low-health bonus AD (to nerf damage for fighters) and weakening Thirsting Slash's AD scaling (to nerf damage for assassins). At the same time, we don't want Goredrinker to become a bad pick for fighters, so we're giving it omnivamp to make sure it still lives up to its identity as their sustain Mythic.

name: Lethal Tempo
rationale: The keystones available for marksmen felt a little flat. Hail of Blades offered a burst of instant attack speed, Lethal Tempo a delayed burst of attack speed, and Press the Attack a delayed burst of damage. Lethal Tempo stood out as the least popular of the bunch despite having a similar win rate. This meant it was either more niche, less satisfying, or both. We're clarifying Lethal Tempo's identity as the best ramping option for long term value and adding attack range to make it more unique.

At maximum stacks, gain 50 (melee) / 100 (ranged) bonus attack range and increase the attack speed cap to 10. Stacks decay by 1 every 0.5 seconds upon expiring.

name: Prototype: Omnistone
rationale: With the introduction of First Strike, it's also time we say goodbye to Prototype: Omnistone, a keystone that never really found a place in most players’ hearts. Its rules were too complex, and tinkering with it risked making it even harder to master. This left us in a tough spot where we couldn’t safely buff it because of its potential to warp gameplay in ways we weren't comfortable with.

name: Caitlyn
rationale:
Headshot resets partially restored.
Several attack "resets" on Caitlyn's Headshots were removed during her ASU. These resets were notoriously difficult to maneuver and were not part of Caitlyn's original design. (Technically, her Headshots executed as abilities rather than empowered basic attacks, which is what allowed the bugged reset functionality.) It wasn't sustainable—or healthy, even—to keep her passive as-is, so we're instead refactoring her Headshot resets in a way that looks smoother and is easier to pull off.

Ivern loves all of his forest friends equally, but when push comes to shove, freeing the Krugs isn't really worth the effort. Krugs give significantly less gold and experience than the other small jungle camps, even though it takes Ivern the same amount of time, mana, and health to free them. name: Kayle
rationale:
Passive wave distance now scales with bonus attack range.
After reaching level 11, if Kayle has enough stacks, her basic attacks launch waves of fire that travel an extra distance and damage enemies they pass through. The distance these waves travel used to be a flat number. Now, it will scale with her bonus attack range, which can be extended by other effects such as her passive at level 16 or Lethal Tempo.

name: Kled
rationale:
Kled & Skaarl's health calculations changed. E cooldown reduced; AD ratio increased.
Tank Kled has been optimal for a while because of the massive bonus HP he gets from Skaarl. We're adjusting how his health is calculated to make his playstyle healthier and more interesting. However, this will nerf some of his bruiser builds, so we're buffing his damage and cooldowns to compensate. We'll keep an eye on the cantankerous duo after this change to monitor AD Kled's viability.
