lines.attribute: Blue Sentinel & Red Brambleback: Attack SFX no longer sometimes fail to play.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Attack SFX no longer sometimes fail to play.

name: Ahri
rationale: Ahri is statistically fairly weak right now, so we’d like to give her an edge in aggressively diving into the enemy team, risking her life for the resets.

lines.raw: Base damage increased to 75 to 175 from 60 to 120.

lines.attribute: No longer shows debug text in the attack buff tooltip.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: No longer shows debug text in the attack buff tooltip.

lines.attribute: Joke VO is no longer prematurely interrupted.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Joke VO is no longer prematurely interrupted.

lines.attribute: Bolt damage now applies as spell damage instead of default damage.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Bolt damage now applies as spell damage instead of default damage.

lines.attribute: Now properly casts from wherever the caster is at the end of cast time.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Now properly casts from wherever the caster is at the end of cast time.

name: Brand
rationale: Brand is a little weak, especially in his more income-heavy roles. So we’re giving him a bit more power to let him run over games where he gets off to a good start by nuking his opposition.

lines.raw: Ablaze monster damage increased to 265% from 260%.
AP ratio increased to 70% AP from 60% AP.
Empowered AP ratio increased to 70*1.25% AP from 60*1.25% AP.
AP ratio per bounce increased to 30% AP from 25% AP.

name: Caitlyn
rationale: Caitlyn's been missing from pro play for quite some time now despite her reputation as a lane bully. As her ability casts are potent enough, we’re pushing up her basic attack power with the hope that she has a real shot at making it into some games this Worlds.

lines.raw: Base attack damage increased to 62 from 60.

name: Corki
rationale: Corki is becoming a little stale in pro play so we’re delivering a nerf to open up the bot lane metagame for Worlds this year. We’re hoping to pro-skew this nerf by removing some of his trivial wave pushing.

lines.raw: Base damage reduced to 60 to 240 from 70 to 250.
Bonus AD ratio reduced to 125% bonus AD from 130%.

name: Diana
rationale: Diana is a reasonably performant mid laner but overall weak as a jungler. So we’re buffing her bespoke monster mod in order to give her clear a bit more power.

lines.raw: Cleave monster damage increased to 300% from 260%.

name: Draven
rationale: Draven has a bit of room for buffs in regular play and is completely missing from pro. We're giving him a little power this patch to see if he can make it back into the spotlight.

lines.raw: Bonus attack speed increased to 30 to 50% from 20 to 40%.
Base damage increased to 200 to 400 from 175 to 375.

lines.attribute: Tooltip now correctly calculates the rockets' total base damage.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Tooltip now correctly calculates the rockets' total base damage.

name: Jax
rationale: We’d like to see Jax as a more meta-defining top laner at Worlds this year but acknowledge he’s already strong enough for regular players, so we’re making his strengths more windowed, something that highly skilled players and coordinated teams can readily harness.

lines.raw: Base health reduced to 650 from 665.
Bug Fix: Restored cast VO.
Primary bonus armor increased to 45 to 75 from 25 to 75.
Primary bonus magic resistance increased to 45*0.6 to 75*0.6 from 25*0.6 to 75*0.6.

name: Jinx
rationale: Jinx has been all but missing from pro play and we're hoping that with a little nudge to her early game she'll find her way back on stage.

lines.raw: Fishbones bonus attack range increased to 100 to 200 from 80 to 200.
Base damage increased to 90 to 290 from 70 to 270.

lines.attribute: If the player has shadows enabled, her shadow no longer lingers at her death position until she respawns.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: If the player has shadows enabled, her shadow no longer lingers at her death position until she respawns.

name: LeBlanc
rationale: With a hope of seeing some flighty assassin play in mid lane, we’re buffing LeBlanc ahead of Worlds by giving her better wave control and PVP burst, especially in protracted side lanes where she’s able to reliably get access to her target. We’re also wary of LeBlanc’s current status in support, so we’re backloading this power into those later-game side lane positions.

lines.attribute: Clone is no longer sometimes slightly bigger than LeBlanc.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Clone is no longer sometimes slightly bigger than LeBlanc.
AP ratio increased to 80% AP from 70% AP.
AP ratio increased to 80% AP from 75% AP.

name: Lee Sin
rationale: Lee Sin is a very performant jungler at almost all levels of play but is suspiciously absent from pro. Our goal with this patch is a series of power-neutral adjustments that should give him a sharp early game strategic niche without significantly changing his win rate.

lines.raw: Armor growth reduced to 4.5 from 4.9.
Base damage increased to 60 to 180 from 55 to 155.
Bonus AD ratio reduced to 95% bonus AD from 115%.
Minimum base damage increased to 60 to 180 from 55 to 155.
Maximum base damage increased to 60*2 to 180*2 from 55*2 to 155*2.
Minimum bonus AD ratio reduced to 95% bonus AD from 115%.
Maximum bonus AD ratio reduced to 95*2% bonus AD from 115*2%.

name: Lillia
rationale: Lillia is a little weak and we’d like to see some AP junglers at Worlds, so she’s the perfect candidate for a buff this patch. By playing up her ultimate, we’re hoping she’ll succeed more in highly skilled and coordinated environments.

lines.raw: Base damage increased to 150 to 250 from 100 to 200.
AP ratio increased to 45% AP from 40% AP.
Cooldown reduced to 140 to 100 seconds from 150 to 110.

name: Mel
rationale: Mel is statistically very weak and even though she sports a rather high ban rate, that doesn’t mean she has to be quite so underpowered for her player base. We’re playing up high-skill applications of her offensive output in order to bring her up in higher MMRs, where she performs much worse.

lines.raw: Projectile base damage increased to 8 to 33 from 8 to 25.
Projectile AP ratio increased to 3% AP from 1% AP.

lines.attribute: Tibbers, H-28Q Apex Turret and Daisy! now follow their summoner between realms.
lines.raw: New Effect: Tibbers, H-28Q Apex Turret and Daisy! now follow their summoner between realms.

lines.attribute: To alleviate performance issues, Cappa Juice hats above 10 will no longer display on her Packmates.
lines.raw: New Effect / Bug Fix: To alleviate performance issues, Cappa Juice hats above 10 will no longer display on her Packmates.

lines.attribute: Aura VFX now properly layers with impassable terrain.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Aura VFX now properly layers with impassable terrain.

lines.attribute: Attack splash VFX now properly layers with structures and units.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Attack splash VFX now properly layers with structures and units.

lines.attribute: Wave VFX now properly layers with structures and units.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Wave VFX now properly layers with structures and units.

name: Pantheon
rationale: Pantheon continues to dominate the pro jungle meta, and frankly he just doesn’t have a high skill gank pattern: Simply click on the enemy and they receive a stun. As a result, we’re swinging very hard to bring down some of his power.

lines.raw: Monster damage reduced to 75% from 90%.

lines.attribute: Minion and monster health ratio damage cap
lines.raw: Minion and monster health ratio damage cap reduced to 120 from 200.

name: Poppy
rationale: Poppy finally has a relatively equivalent win rate spread across her roles, but is overall a little too strong in all three. She’s also near the top jungle spot in pro play and we’d like to create more room for other junglers to get play.

lines.attribute: Minion and monster health ratio damage cap
lines.raw: Minion and monster health ratio damage cap reduced to 50 to 170 from 75 to 195.
Cooldown upon being cancelled increased to 30 seconds from 15.

lines.attribute: No longer displays a green decal under champions hit.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: No longer displays a green decal under champions hit.

name: Seraphine
rationale: Seraphine is a very popular support and occasional mid laner, but is unfortunately quite weak where a lot of her players are, which is in lower MMR. As Seraphine is the deathball mage-enchanter, we don’t want to get rid of that strength, but we also want her to be more self-reliant (mid lane), less reliant on her teammates knowing how her abilities work (low MMR), and more useful to her team when performing mage-like duties, such as helping take down epic monsters.

lines.raw: Health growth increased to 95 from 90.
Mana growth increased to 40 from 25.

lines.attribute: Bonus damage based on the target's missing health now applies against monsters.
lines.raw: New Effect: Bonus damage based on the target's missing health now applies against monsters.

lines.attribute: Heal no longer scales with number of nearby allies (including Seraphine).
lines.raw: Removed: Heal no longer scales with number of nearby allies (including Seraphine).
Heal changed to 8 to 16% missing health from 3 to 5%.
Previously 3*5 to 5*5% on 5 targets.

lines.attribute: Casting Death Surge no longer prevents the cast of effects that activate from ultimate ability casts until Sion has cast Unstoppable Onslaught twice without having cast Death Surge in the interim.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Casting Death Surge no longer prevents the cast of effects that activate from ultimate ability casts until Sion has cast Unstoppable Onslaught twice without having cast Death Surge in the interim.

name: Sivir
rationale: Sivir is a little OP in regular play and somewhat dominates the pro play sphere. While we’re happy to have a healthy share of hyper-carries, we’d like if Sivir had more competition in that archetype.

lines.raw: Bonus AD ratio reduced to 85% bonus AD from 100%.

lines.attribute: Indicator no longer causes various ability VFX that overlap with it to flicker.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Indicator no longer causes various ability VFX that overlap with it to flicker.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Casting Transcend One's Self no longer causes the icon for his Chain Lash to disappear from the player's HUD.

lines.attribute: Prestige T1 Sylas: Added Faker's signature to the border set in the Loading Screen.
lines.raw: Added Faker's signature to the border set in the Loading Screen.

name: Syndra
rationale: We’re delivering some power-neutral adjustments to Syndra, making her a stronger lane bully and teamfight carry mage while siphoning some power that should disproportionately impact non-pro players.

lines.raw: Health growth reduced to 100 from 104.
Armor growth reduced to 4 from 4.6.
Base damage increased to 80 to 220 from 75 to 215.
AP ratio increased to 65% AP from 60% AP.
Cooldown reduced to 15 seconds from 17.

lines.attribute: Feet no longer jitter during his Recall animation.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Feet no longer jitter during his Recall animation.

lines.attribute: Mist Walkers spawned as Yorick exited the Death Realm no longer remain alive indefinitely in the Death Realm.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Mist Walkers spawned as Yorick exited the Death Realm no longer remain alive indefinitely in the Death Realm.

lines.attribute: Tooltip now notes the maximum single-target damage from all parts of the ability instead of noting the ability can deal damage at least three times (300%) when two separate enemies are slammed while at least one enemy is between them.
lines.raw: Tooltip now notes the maximum single-target damage from all parts of the ability instead of noting the ability can deal damage at least three times (300%) when two separate enemies are slammed while at least one enemy is between them.

lines.attribute: Restored yoyo SFX during walking animations.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Restored yoyo SFX during walking animations.

name: Celestial Opposition
rationale: We’re fixing a long-standing issue with Celestial Opposition that gave it very weird optimizations. Essentially, players could send a clone forward and it would result in a nearly guaranteed slow-bomb on a short cooldown. While it’s fine that clones often mimic items, getting slowed by thin air just isn’t a good experience. So now the champion (or clone) must be alive in order for Celestial Opposition’s slow to trigger. This means that, for example, attacking Neeko W won’t result in you getting crowd controlled.

lines.attribute: Blessed buff is now properly removed on death. Previously, the user could receive damage (prior to dying) then have the shockwave trigger at the end of the linger period after dying, which was accompanied by no visual or sound effects.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Blessed buff is now properly removed on death. Previously, the user could receive damage (prior to dying) then have the shockwave trigger at the end of the linger period after dying, which was accompanied by no visual or sound effects.

lines.attribute: Immolate description in the tooltip now notes the minion and monster damage modifiers separately.
lines.raw: Immolate description in the tooltip now notes the minion and monster damage modifiers separately.

name: Redemption
rationale: Redemption has found its place as a near unanimous first item for tank supports in pro play. We’re looking to pull back on Redemption’s power to allow items like Locket and Knight’s Vow to compete.

lines.raw: Heal reduced to 150 to 350 from 200 to 400.

name: Unsealed Spellbook
rationale: Unsealed Spellbook’s recent buff took it from being entirely forgotten to the only keystone anyone not named Neeko even uses in pro play. As a result, we’re splitting the difference with the hope that it’s still a viable keystone rune without completely dominating all choice.

lines.raw: Starting cooldown increased to 270 seconds from 240.
Minimum cooldown increased to 270-(25*6) from 240-(25*6).

lines.attribute: Initial cooldown unchanged at 360 seconds. Cooldown reduction per unique swap unchanged at 25 seconds.
lines.raw: Initial cooldown unchanged at 360 seconds. Cooldown reduction per unique swap unchanged at 25 seconds.

lines.attribute: Teleport / Unleashed Teleport: No longer sometimes places the caster at the far side of a terrain if the target destination is near terrain, due to incorrectly assuming there is no available space.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: No longer sometimes places the caster at the far side of a terrain if the target destination is near terrain, due to incorrectly assuming there is no available space.

lines.attribute: Minimap icon for the camp being live no longer sometimes duplicates.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Minimap icon for the camp being live no longer sometimes duplicates.

name: Anivia
rationale: Anivia's been struggling to find success in the mid lane as of late. Her low mobility is one of her weaknesses, so we're lowering her Q's cooldown slightly as a way for her to keep her enemies at bay while also giving her a bit more damage on her E to help her out.

lines.raw: Cooldown reduced to 11 to 7 seconds from 12 to 8.
Base damage increased to 55 to 155 from 50 to 150.
Empowered base damage increased to 55*2 to 155*2 from 50*2 to 150*2.

name: Azir
rationale: Azir's a bit too powerful in higher levels of play at the moment, but he's in pretty good shape for regular play. So we're looking to shift his power around and reduce those pro-specific strengths. To do this, we're digging into his early laning phase and giving him less passive guaranteed wave control and compensating him with better late-game scaling and more rewards for taking big risks.

lines.raw: Recharge timer increased to 12 to 6 seconds from 10 to 6.
AP ratio changed to 30 to 70% AP from 40 to 60% AP.
Soldier subsequent target damage modifier changed to 20 / 28 to 100% from 25 to 100%.
Base damage increased to 70 to 230 from 60 to 220.
Damage AP ratio increased to 60% AP from 40% AP.

name: Briar
rationale: Despite her lack of self-control, Briar's been tearing it up as one of the highest performing junglers at lower ranks for a bit now. We're looking to tap down her power to bleed out enemies with her passive at max stacks, as effective kiting (and thus lower stack counts) are more common at higher ranks.

lines.raw: Maximum number of stacks reduced to 5 from 7.

name: Camille
rationale: In her current state, Camille's laning phase is very hit or miss: Either she can comfortably beat her opponent with her passive, or she can't really engage with the lane and loses. While she appears powerful in the hands of most players we don't think this shape is healthy for her as a whole, so we're giving her W some additional power that will give her some more strength to play around early while balancing that with reduced base stats, which shouldn't feel particularly noticeable.

lines.raw: Armor growth reduced to 4.5 from 5.
Base damage increased to 60 to 160 from 50 to 150.
Cooldown reduced to 15 to 11 seconds from 17 to 11.

name: Fizz
rationale: Fizz is a little weak right now (some might say he's floundering) and is incredibly reliant on snowballing, as his base damages are appropriate in the early game but generally don't scale well without gold. We're looking to make some power-positive adjustments to make him less reliant on snowballing while still asking him to build primarily AP assassin items. As a whole, these changes should be positive for his up-front W burst damage, make his ultimate a bit weaker, and open up a few new item choices.

lines.attribute: Passive base damage over time per tick
lines.raw: Passive base damage over time per tick increased to 30/6 to 90/6 from 20/6 to 60/6.
Total base damage increased to 30 to 90 from 20 to 60.
Passive AP ratio per tick reduced to 25/6% AP from 30/6% AP.
Total AP ratio reduced to 25% AP from 30% AP.

lines.attribute: Removed: Passive damage over time no longer applies against structures.: Active damage is still applied, and at 50% effectiveness.
lines.raw: Active damage is still applied, and at 50% effectiveness.
Active base damage increased to 50 to 150 from 50 to 130.
Active on-hit base damage increased to 20 to 40 from 10 to 30.
Active on-hit AP ratio reduced to 30% AP from 35% AP.

lines.attribute: Damage text for the passive (damage-over-time) effect now has a cumulative display.
lines.raw: Damage text for the passive (damage-over-time) effect now has a cumulative display.
Guppy base damage increased to 180 to 420 from 150 to 350.
Guppy AP ratio reduced to 60% AP from 80% AP.
Chomper base damage increased to 180*1.25 to 420*1.25 from 225 to 425.
Chomper AP ratio reduced to 60*1.25% AP from 100% AP.
Gigalodon base damage changed to 180*1.5 to 420*1.5 from 300 to 500.
Gigalodon AP ratio reduced to 60*1.5% AP from 120% AP.

name: Graves
rationale: Graves is a fairly popular jungler that's performing decently right now, but his builds have devolved into one-shot lethality. We don't believe this to be a good state for him because his playstyle becomes one-shot or be one-shot which isn't fun for anyone. We think it'd be better for him to have a sustained combat pattern where skillful Graves players can utilize their Grit, so we're nudging his builds and playstyle around to make him less reliant on bonus AD. Overall this should net out in a small buff once this change has had some time to settle and players adapt.

lines.raw: Initial base damage increased to 50 to 150 from 45 to 125.
Initial AD ratio reduced to 65% bonus AD from 80%.
Explosion base damage changed to 80 to 260 from 85 to 225.
Explosion AD ratio changed to 55 to 115% bonus AD from 40 to 140% bonus AD.

lines.attribute: If casting Zap! immediately after triggering Get Excited!, the former is no longer missing VFX.
lines.raw: If casting Zap! immediately after triggering Get Excited!, the former is no longer missing VFX.

name: Katarina
rationale: Despite Katarina feeling oppressive in the mid-game, she's been having a hard time actually converting her snowballs into wins. This is true even in the hands of her most dedicated mains. So, we're going to play up some of her resilience in lane so that she can find more success battling her lane opponent.

lines.raw: Base armor increased to 32 from 28.

lines.attribute: If a target is next to terrain and the blade connects with them, Leona no longer illegally loses turret aggro immediately, and regardless of her position at the travel's start, during the travel itself or at the travel's end.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: If a target is next to terrain and the blade connects with them, Leona no longer illegally loses turret aggro immediately, and regardless of her position at the travel's start, during the travel itself or at the travel's end.

name: Malphite
rationale: Malphite's a solid top laner and a consistent rock for his teams, but even so he is often a bit heavy for his teams. We're giving him a little help this patch by increasing his base armor just a bit to solidify his early game.

lines.raw: Base armor increased to 40 from 37.
Base damage increased to 80 to 240 from 70 to 230.
Undocumented: Damage modifier changed to 75 to 225% from 0 to 225%.[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hYsLSyp_M_4][https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WdqAjlbcvC0]

name: Orianna
rationale: At higher skill levels Orianna's early wave clear is far too safe and her optimized builds make her too tanky for her to be exposed to any real risks, so we're looking to re-introduce some risk to her overall kit. We want to incentivize Orianna to build more damage and less tank, so we're weakening her early wave clear power spikes so she has to pick up more AP to clear waves, something most players are already doing and thus shouldn't be impacted much by.

lines.raw: Base damage reduced to 70 to 230 from 70 to 270.
AP ratio increased to 80% AP from 70% AP.

name: Pantheon
rationale: Our nerfs last patch to Pantheon hit him a bit too hard, so we're walking them back a little bit. We still want there to be a strong clear speed tradeoff for a jungler with such reliable ganks, but it doesn't have to be quite so bad.

lines.raw: Monster damage increased to 80% from 75%.

lines.attribute: Minion and monster health ratio damage cap
lines.raw: Minion and monster health ratio damage cap increased to 150 from 120.

lines.attribute: Incoming heal indicator in the health bar no longer incorrectly multiplies the health value that the target would receive by the number of nearby allies including Seraphine.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Incoming heal indicator in the health bar no longer incorrectly multiplies the health value that the target would receive by the number of nearby allies including Seraphine.

lines.raw: [Note: This had no gameplay effect. The heal has not scaled with number of nearby allies since patch 25.19.]

lines.raw: Undocumented: Death Surge now once again prevents the cast of effects that activate from ultimate ability casts until Sion has cast Unstoppable Onslaught twice without having cast Death Surge in the interim.

lines.attribute: VFX no longer flicker. This applies to all skins.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: VFX no longer flicker. This applies to all skins.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: No longer accidentally duplicates her staff upon Soraka dropping to the ground, remaining for the duration of her death.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Model no longer slides into view from below the map during the respawn sequence.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: No longer incorrectly gains Death Surge instead of Unstoppable Onslaught if cast on Sion during his Glory in Death zombie state.

lines.attribute: No longer grants Tahm Kench the effects of Cloud Dragon Soul upon using the ability on any target to acquire them (i.e. even on targets who are out of range) instead of upon the ability being cast.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: No longer grants Tahm Kench the effects of Cloud Dragon Soul upon using the ability on any target to acquire them (i.e. even on targets who are out of range) instead of upon the ability being cast.

name: Veigar
rationale: Veigar's been coming up a bit short of success as of late, so to help our resident miniature king we're upping his W's AP ratio so he can take more advantage of his infinite AP scaling to pop enemies he catches with a well placed Event Horizon.

lines.raw: AP ratio increased to 70 to 110% AP from 60 to 100% AP.

name: Volibear
rationale: Volibear's been one of the strongest junglers in solo queue for a while now, so in this patch we're looking to bring his (ability) power down a notch. His ability to synergize with cooldown reduction has allowed him to sustain through most situations while still dealing a respectable amount of DPS. We're okay with his sustain, but to bring his DPS down just a tad we're hitting his AP ratios which should weaken some of his most popular builds while leaving his AD builds untouched.

lines.raw: Lightning AP ratio reduced to 45% AP from 50% AP.
Damage AP ratio reduced to 70% AP from 80% AP.

name: Warwick
rationale: Warwick is particularly oppressive in lower skill brackets of play, so we're looking to make his claws and teeth just a little less lethal. As he's often able to simply build tank items later in the game, we're nudging him toward keeping up with damage purchases by reducing his guaranteed late game damage output.

lines.raw: Attack damage growth reduced to 2.5 from 2.75.

name: Wukong
rationale: Wukong has been performing quite well at the highest levels of play despite not being particularly strong at lower skill levels. We're looking to bring his ceiling down and floor up a bit by moving some power away from his pro skewed abilities and distributing it throughout the rest of his kit.

name: Bard
rationale: We're pretty happy with Bard's current balance state but would like to open up some more options for him, namely in building AP items like Shurelya's, making him better at supporting his team when playing AP-heavy.

name: Diana
rationale: Diana's last buff to her jungle clears overshot a bit, so we're walking it back slightly to keep her in line.

lines.raw: Cleave monster damage reduced to 280% from 300%.

name: Dr. Mundo
rationale: Dr. Mundo is a scaling juggernaut who has to wade through a fairly weak early game in order to scale into the ability to go wherever he pleases. And we're happy he's able to go where he pleases, but he's bursting whomever he pleases a bit too easily. We're looking for some power neutral adjustments that take away some late-game burst and give back late-game durability in its stead.

lines.raw: Armor growth increased to 4.5 from 3.7.
Active minimum health ratio reduced to 5% bonus health from 7%.
Active maximum health ratio reduced to 5*1.4% bonus health from 7*1.4%.

name: Ezreal
rationale: Ezreal has been a low performer lately especially at lower ranks. We're looking to add a little bit of general power to help him keep up as games go late.

lines.raw: Attack damage growth increased to 3.25 from 2.75.

name: Graves
rationale: We'd like to nudge Graves back toward having a strong sustained fight pattern and that means letting him rely on Grit and playing to stack it up. As he's getting this MR from Quickdraw, he can once again have the base magic resistance of a ranged champion. So, if you can catch Graves before he's able to stack up, he's more burstable than before, but if he's able to play the fight out the way he wants, he'll grow to be the sustained monster we all know and hate love.

lines.raw: Base magic resistance reduced to 30 from 32.
Magic resistance growth reduced to 1.3 from 2.05.

lines.attribute: True Grit stacks now also grant bonus magic resistance equal to 50% of the bonus armor gained.
lines.raw: New Effect: True Grit stacks now also grant bonus magic resistance equal to 50% of the bonus armor gained.

name: Gwen
rationale: Back in 25.06 we sought to give Gwen more power over her laning phase while still being that scaling AP skirmisher. However, those changes have left her in a less popular state that has alienated Gwen players from the version of her that they enjoyed. So we're going back to almost the exact same champion from 25.05, with two differences: Her armor growth is a little lower, and her jungle levers are weaker. These two changes weren't reverted because she was a little too strong in top and significantly too strong in the jungle back before the changes. Enjoy your Gwensday tomorrow!

On-hit AP ratio reduced to 20% AP from 25% AP.

lines.raw: Undocumented / Bug Fix: Recall cast time no longer illegally cancels the evolution animation, instantly granting the effect.

name: Kalista
rationale: Kalista has been underperforming for quite a while now and we'd like to carve out some mid-game strength for her. We're hoping to achieve that by increasing her attack damage growth, which directly feeds into her attacks as well as her Q and E damage.

lines.raw: Attack damage growth increased to 4.75 from 4.25.

name: Kog'Maw
rationale: Kog'Maw is one of the winningest bot laners in the game and has also lost his old identity as a scaler. We're delivering a targeted nerf toward his early trading in order to re-balance him and retain some of that scaling potential.

lines.raw: Bonus attack speed reduced to 5 to 25% from 10 to 30%.

name: Morgana
rationale: Morgana has taken off as a highly powerful mid laner across all ranks of play. We're super happy that she's found a new audience here but she's also meaningfully overpowered. In order to open up some more weaknesses, we're looking to bring down her guaranteed durability, making her rely more on Black Shield and Soul Siphon.

lines.raw: Armor growth reduced to 4.2 from 5.
Undocumented: Damage modifier changed to 0 to 225% from 75 to 225%.

name: Qiyana
rationale: Qiyana has been one of the clear winners from the recent changes to Profane Hydra and Axiom Arc. She's been taking over in both mid lane and jungle especially in elite play. We're hitting her with some nerfs that'll take her down a notch in both roles.

lines.raw: Health growth reduced to 121 from 124.

lines.ability: Q - Elemental Wrath / Edge of Ixtal
lines.raw: Bonus AD ratio reduced to 85% bonus AD from 90%.

name: Quinn
rationale: Quinn has been one of the winningest top laners for a while now and with us nerfing both Doran's Shield and Second Wind this patch, we're confident that Quinn is due for some nerfs of her own lest she completely overtake top lane. We hope that these nerfs will open up her build options away from simply high AD lethality burst, allowing her the space to play out a more sustained auto-attacking pattern.

lines.raw: Bonus AD ratio reduced to 80 to 100% bonus AD from 80 to 120%.

AD ratio changed to 35% bonus AD from 70% total AD.

lines.raw: Adjusted splash artwork for Winged Hussar Xin Zhao.

name: Yone
rationale: Yone's been a low performer for quite a while now, and the upcoming changes to Doran's Shield and Second Wind will likely leave him in a pretty sad state. We'd like to pre-emptively give him some early game power to make up for it.

lines.raw: Base attack damage increased to 62 from 60.

lines.attribute: Buffering Mortal Steel or Soul Unbound while casting Spirit Cleave no longer causes them to be cast in Yone's facing direction.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Buffering Mortal Steel or Soul Unbound while casting Spirit Cleave no longer causes them to be cast in Yone's facing direction.

name: Yunara
rationale:
We're here to buff Yunara today. As she's still relatively new, over two thirds of her games are played by inexperienced players, substantially dragging down her win rate. But even after accounting for that fact, she's still weaker than the average bot laner. We want to achieve two goals here: First, we want to improve the value of ability ranks in W so that players who invest in spell damage are rewarded for their skill points. Second, we want to make her more consistently mobile, bringing up Kanmei's Steps average movement speed so that players don't have to hold it just to juke a key skillshot and instead can take more proactive and aggressive fights.
The change here to her ultimate is a very slight nerf that aligns both W abilities to use bonus attack damage while keeping her total appetite for Long Swords about the same.

name: Catalyst of Aeons
rationale: Catalyst needs to be competitive with Lost Chapter in giving tankier AP champions enough mana to play out their laning phases. It does not, however, need to invalidate burst damage so strongly. So we're delivering a small health nerf until it's turned into Rod of Ages.

lines.raw: Health reduced to 300 from 350.

name: Doran's Blade
rationale: We're moving Doran's Blade back to its 14.1 version with omnivamp because the item is meant to serve more than just attackers, but instead a wide range of AD champions, such as those who rely on abilities do deal their damage.

lines.raw: Life steal reduced to 0% from 3%.

lines.raw: New Unique Passive - Life Draining: Heal for 2.5% of damage dealt, reduced to 33.3% effectiveness for area of effect and pet damage spells.

name: Doran's Ring
rationale: The current tuning of some starter items and Second Wind can make it feel pointless to attempt to harass during lane phase, resulting in stale gameplay especially in mid lane where players don't play for kills often enough. With these changes, we're attempting to nudge back towards poke being more valuable in the lane phase.

lines.raw: Removed Unique Passive - Restoration: Restore 1.25 mana every second. If you cannot gain mana, heal 0.55 health instead.

rationale: See Doran's Ring.

name: Second Wind

name: Akshan
rationale: Akshan was one of the clear winners from the recent changes to early game sustain, so this patch we’re back to balance things out by tapping down his early game threat and vulnerability.

lines.raw: Base health reduced to 610 from 630.
Cooldown increased to 9 to 5 seconds from 8 to 5.

name: Aurelion Sol
rationale: While Aurelion Sol can still be a menace in the late game (deliberately so), we don’t think his early game needs to be quite as painful as it currently is so we’re giving him better early trades and generally improving his ability to dodge skill shots and navigate fights. His W is based on his underlying move speed, so this move speed buff helps his flying, too.

lines.raw: Movement speed increased to 340 from 335.
Burst base damage increased to 60 to 100 from 55 to 95.
Base speed increased to 340 from 335.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: VFX now properly features team colors.

name: Blitzcrank
rationale: Blitzcrank has been underperforming so we want to add some more pep to this steam golem’s step with some better sustained disruption and damage to get him rolling again.

name: LeBlanc
rationale: LeBlanc’s last set of changes made her more viable in the highest levels of play, but have also led to her being a bit overwhelming for the rest of us at home. We’re delivering some base stat nerfs that should make her weaker for most players without impacting her viability in high level play too much.

lines.raw: Health growth reduced to 108 from 111.
Armor growth reduced to 4.2 from 4.7.
Undocumented: Damage modifier changed to 30 to 225% from 0 to 225%.

lines.raw: Undocumented: Enemies no longer turn around when hit by Vault.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Airborne disable no longer ends abruptly on targets upon their collision with terrain during the displacement.

name: Skarner
rationale: Skarner is one of a few champions who’s a little weak but has a deceptively low win rate due to being quite hard to play. Still, he’s a champion who has room for buffs, so we’d like to do just that. We’re aware of his recent history with pro play, so we’re pairing these buffs with some nerfs that we hope will disproportionately affect low-ping, pro players. Our overall goal is a stronger Skarner who can sustain this new level of power for months to come. We’re nerfing Impale’s cast time to increase his counter-play for skilled opponents. As Skarner is meant to occasionally be a juggernaut, we’re increasing the viability of AD juggernaut items, specifically Sterak’s Gage, by increasing his total base AD and his overall AD scaling. And finally, to make him more approachable, we’re removing an awkward optimization around Q’s uptime with compensation that should feel similar for most players.

lines.raw: Attack damage growth increased to 4 from 3.
Bonus AD ratio increased to 90% bonus AD from 80%.
Cooldown reduced to 8 to 4 seconds from 13 to 7.

lines.raw: New Effect: Shattered Earth's cooldown now restarts with each attack hit or upon Upheaval's cast.

lines.raw: New Effect: Damage now also scales with 120% bonus AD.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Haste no longer triggers both perspectives' SFX (self and others) for the player.

name: Talon
rationale: Talon is running (front-flipping) the jungle right now, especially with the newly-buffed Axiom Arc. By comparison, he’s pretty fair in mid, so we’re just looking to give him some jungle-specific nerfs without hurting his viability mid.

lines.raw: Monster damage reduced to 100% from 110%.

name: Volibear
rationale: As the dust has settled from Volibear’s recent changes, his AD and AP builds are much closer in power and we believe jungle Volibear to be appropriately strong. That said, top lane Volibear is currently quite weak. To help him out we’re delivering some changes that’re intended to keep jungle Voli at about the same power level but substantially buff up top lane.

lines.raw: Base attack damage increased to 62 from 60.
Base armor increased to 35 from 31.
Bonus movement speed reduced to 12 to 26% from 12 to 28%.

name: Yone
rationale: We buffed Yone last patch but due to his tendency to build Doran’s Shield and Second Wind, he didn’t end up as powerful as we would have liked. Since we are happy with the results of reducing his sustain in the last patch, we’re re-adding more early agency through his ability to hit back at his opposition.

lines.raw: Base damage increased to 25 to 125 from 20 to 120.
Health regeneration health ratio reduced to 1.5% maximum health from 2%.

lines.raw: Undocumented: Now can only be seen by the blue side Support in the red side Support's inventory without gaining sight of the user.

name: Cash Back
rationale: Cash Back stonks are low despite the fact that virtually every champion buys items and wants more of them. We’re looking to empower this rune to make it a more competitive choice in its row.

lines.raw: Gold refund increased to 8% from 6%.

name: Guardian
rationale: We recently adjusted Guardian to make it more attractive to enchanters and now we’d like to revisit the rune to push up its desirability across all classes, both tanks and otherwise. We don’t want an early surge of health to make it impossible to all-in squishy champions in lane, so we’re mostly backloading this buff by increasing its level and AP scaling.

lines.raw: Base shield increased to 45 to 180 from 45 to 150.
Shield AP ratio increased 25% AP from 15% AP.

name: Hail of Blades
rationale: Hail of Blades has its share of hard-bound users who we tune against the rune, but it would also be nice if it had a set of champions who wanted to occasionally run it. The combat pattern of melee Hail of Blades is pretty compelling, so we’d like to buff it for melee champions in order to give it more of a fighting chance.

lines.attribute: Bonus attack speed for melee champions
lines.raw: Bonus attack speed for melee champions increased to 160% from 140%.

lines.attribute: Bonus attack speed for ranged champions unchanged.
lines.raw: Bonus attack speed for ranged champions unchanged.

name: Legend: Bloodline
rationale: Bloodline's current tuning has left it in a pretty underwhelming state. Given that life steal is so highly sought-after, its pick rate has remained quite steady regardless. Still, we're looking to return some power and satisfaction to the rune when it's picked up.

lines.raw: Life steal per stack increased to 0.4% from 0.35%.
Maximum life steal increased to 6% from 5.25%.

name: Nimbus Cloak
rationale: As part of our goal to open up more choices in minor rune slots we're tuning up Nimbus Cloak this patch to be more appealing, especially when using longer cooldowns.

lines.raw: Bonus movement speed increased to 15 / 35 / 45% from 14 / 28 / 40%.

name: Phase Rush
rationale: It’s important that Phase Rush has some slow resist on it in order to feel like it actually does something when faced with slows. However, it's sometimes so strong that it can feel like there’s nothing you can do to pin them down. We’re softening the slow resist on Phase Rush a little bit in order to make it not quite so good at letting its users get away.

lines.raw: Slow resistance reduced to 50% from 75%.

name: Triple Tonic
rationale: Triple Tonic has been dwarfed by the ever-popular Biscuit Delivery for some time now, and while we’re shipping a small nerf to Biscuits this patch, we’re also looking to give this rune a stronger identity through its short windows of power, giving potentially a better early-game Recall and then an all-in opportunity at level 6.

lines.raw: Elixir of Avarice gold increased to 60 gold from 40 gold.

lines.raw: Elixir of Force adaptive force increased to 30*0.6 bonus Attack Damage or 30 Ability Power (Adaptive) from 20*0.6 bonus Attack Damage or 20 Ability Power (Adaptive).

lines.attribute: Summoner's Rift: Map updated with a winter theme.
lines.raw: Map updated with a winter theme.

name: Aatrox
rationale: Here's a fun story: Aatrox's VGU was slated for the jungle for part of his early development before being shipped as a top laner. He's a very interesting champion with fun mechanics to play around, so we're alleviating some max-HP caps and adding some jungle juice to see how he performs in this new role.

lines.raw: Monster damage cap increased to 100 to 320 from 100 at all levels.

lines.attribute: Now deals 40 bonus physical damage to monsters, affected by the subsequent cast and Sweetspot damage modifiers.
lines.raw: New Effect: Now deals 40 bonus physical damage to monsters, affected by the subsequent cast and Sweetspot damage modifiers.

name: Ahri
rationale: Our latest buff to Ahri didn't get her quite as high up as we'd hoped, so we're back to deliver some more damage. We're juicing up her W when used to pick off an individual target to reward her for landing autos, E, or generally just properly isolating her opponents.

lines.raw: Subsequent damage increased to 40% from 30%.

name: Ambessa
rationale: Ambessa's jungle play rate never really took off but it's always been right behind top lane in terms of actual power. We're giving it a light nudge that should make her balanced in this alternate role and especially help unoptimized players who can't always get sweet spots to land on large jungle monsters.

Lacerate can no longer be buffered during an attack windup if Ambessa only has one stack of Medarda Maxim.]
Bonus monster damage increased to 150 from 125.
Bonus monster damage increased to 150 from 125.

name: Ashe
rationale: We're delivering a suite of ADC changes in this patch in order to shake up the end-of-season solo queue meta. A few of the most commonly picked are being nerfed and some of the least common are being buffed. We'd also like to move in a direction of making non-caster ADCs more attack speed-reliant, which you should notice in many of the ADC changes later on in this patch. Ashe has been a top performer in terms of both pick and win rate for most of this season, so we're tapping her down to create a little more equity in ADC pick rates. We're maintaining Ashe's appetite for attack speed by giving her a little bit less from Q.

lines.raw: Bonus attack speed reduced to 20 to 60% from 25 to 75%.

name: Caitlyn
rationale: Like Ashe above, Caitlyn has also been eating up a lot of ADC pick rate. We think she should maintain her identity as a long-range lane bully, but she's also bursting champions too hard with late game Headshots, so we're bringing down the top-end damage a bit.

lines.raw: AD ratio reduced to 60 to 100% AD from 60 to 120% AD.
Non-champion AD ratio reduced to 110% AD at all levels from 110 to 120% AD.

lines.attribute: Debuff can no longer stack with itself once per cast instance of Miasma, when a target walks into a cloud from a previous cast instance of Miasma.
lines.raw: Bug Fix: Debuff can no longer stack with itself once per cast instance of Miasma, when a target walks into a cloud from a previous cast instance of Miasma.

name: Cho'Gath
rationale: While he's no stranger to being played in all sorts of alternate roles, Cho'Gath has a naturally fitting jungle kit and we'd like to make that work well. We're adjusting his E damage vs. monsters to no longer care about their max HP and instead just deliver a solid punch to get through his camps. This should be an unequivocal buff to early monster damage.

lines.attribute: Monster damage: 20 to 100 (+ 30% AP) (+ 2.5 to 3.9% (+ 0.5% per Feast stack) of target's maximum health). The damage based on the target's health ratio is capped at 200 against monsters.
lines.raw: Old: 20 to 100 (+ 30% AP) (+ 2.5 to 3.9% (+ 0.5% per Feast stack) of target's maximum health). The damage based on the target's health ratio is capped at 200 against monsters.

name: Dr. Mundo
rationale: Dr. Mundo has once again risen up the ranks in popularity due to some very skilled players playing him very publicly. This time, in the jungle! We think Dr. Mundo is appropriately balanced in both roles at the present, but will continue to monitor how he's performing in the coming weeks. All that said, we're shipping a very impactful bug fix in this patch, which will increase his win rate, so we're also preemptively nerfing him a bit. We're happy with his recent reduction in burst damage, which this bug fix furthers, but want to maintain his overall sustained threat, so we're re-buffing his functional attack damage.

name: Fizz
rationale: While Fizz wins an appropriate number of games in mid lane, he's incredibly feast-or-famine and often relies on simply leaving his lane to go kill other champions, so we'd like to make him more robust in playing out his laning phase. In order to do that, we're improving his early resilience so that he can take more trades and compensate elsewhere to make him a little less ult-reliant. We're also taking a swing at enabling jungle Fizz. We think this new role is a bit of a stretch and may not pan out in the end, but we're swinging hard to get his first jungle clear into something comfortable and seeing if players will enjoy him here.

name: Hwei
rationale: Hwei's a well-performing mid laner who has low-quality gameplay when he can simply throw out Q-E and clear waves with little effort. We'd like to weaken his access to non-committal wave clear by nerfing that output. As the intended rank 5 magnitude would mark an over-nerf, we're partially compensating him with an AP ratio buff. These changes will still result in a net reduction in power and should open up more room for laning phase interactivity.

name: Jayce
rationale: We think Jayce jungle is a bit of a longshot but there's a chance he's got a real player base in this new role, so we're delivering some buffs to make his first clear more comfortable and watching to see how many players are interested.

rationale: Jhin looks quite weak at the present, so we're giving him some damage buffs and found another place to include the number 4 in his tooltips, which is the only buff he really needs, right?

rationale: As with the other ADC nerfs above, Jinx wins a large portion of her games and risks crowding out other champions if left untouched amidst the other nerfs in this patch. We want to preserve her identity as a late-game auto attack monster, so we're nerfing some of Jinx's spell damage.

name: Kai'Sa
rationale: Kai'Sa has been the most picked solo queue ADC in most ranks for months on end, so we're delivering a small nerf to create more variety in the role. The primary nerf is to her base armor, where a bit less early safety should make her feel more assailable.

name: Malphite
rationale: Malphite has a natural jungle kit with a decent gank paradigm, and repeatable damage for killing monsters. He just doesn't deal enough right now to comfortably clear, so we're juicing both his early game clear (hint hint start W!) and late-game as well, since he often builds full tank and needs his damage to keep up with growth monster health.

name: Mel
rationale: We're glad that Mel is a viable mid laner (shoutout League's GOAT for raising awareness!). However, she's also proven to be one of League's most frustrating champions, which we're looking to alleviate. Her passive buffs that required her to take on more risk were successful in our eyes, so we're headed back to that. To continue to expose her to more risk, we're weakening Solar Snare's lockdown and self-peel potential. We know she's still got such sharp interactions that she'll still sport one of League's highest ban rates, but we hope this adjustment will be roughly power-neutral and frustration-reducing.

rationale: Miss Fortune isn't winning as often as she should for how straightforward she is to play, and unlike many of the other ADCs in this patch, she is indeed a caster, so we're looking to amp up her ability to take over teamfights with her ultimate.

name: Ornn
rationale: While Ornn is a totally viable top laner, we think he could also shine in the tank jungle roster, so we're buffing some of his monster damage caps. We're also adding some tooltip clarity, as some of his numbers weren't exposed to players.

lines.raw: Brittle monster damage cap increased to 260 to 500 from 250 at all levels.
Total monster damage cap increased to 260 to 500 from 155 to 255.

name: Rek'Sai
rationale: Rek'Sai top has been an enjoyable spectator experience but a fairly miserable one to play against and she's significantly overpowered for those who know what they're doing. We don't want to remove this role from viability but we'd like to reduce just now immovable she is through her lane sustain. Her jungle will take a small hit from this nerf, but she can sustain a small nerf there, as well.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Leap from a bush no longer fails to grant stacks of Conqueror and Lethal Tempo.

name: Riven
rationale: Riven's native mobility, strong dueling, and interesting risk profile of having to burn damage in order to close the gap could make for a really compelling jungle champion. She's also monstrously hard to play, but even accounting for that, she appears to be a pretty abysmal jungler at her current tuning. We're substantially buffing her first clear to see if players will find a fun, dynamic, high-skill fighter compelling in this new role.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Resolved a VFX distortion issue.

name: Sion
rationale: Sion is pretty playable in the jungle but is slightly weak and deserving of a small nudge for players who want to yell “COWARDS!” as they barrel up and down the river. We're just delivering a light touch to see how many players want to try their hand at Si-ungle.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Death Surge no longer incorrectly triggers effects that activate from ultimate ability casts upon expiring (regardless of the slot used).
Monster damage increased to 165% from 150%.

name: Skarner
rationale: Last patch's Skarner changes unfortunately landed him weaker than we had hoped and anticipated. We're now here to deliver direct buffs in order to give him the power he deserves. We were overly cautious on how much attack damage to give him, so we're back for more, and his Q isn't doing quite enough now that he can't quickly get two cycles off, so we're buffing its uptime and throughput.

lines.raw: Attack damage growth increased to 5 from 4.

Target health ratio increased to 9% of target's maximum health from 8%.

name: Swain
rationale: Swain is quite weak in his most-played role of support. We're giving him a little more power in his E as well as lowering its mana cost to let Swain support have more room to work with without a mana item, since he typically doesn't buy one there.

lines.raw: Base damage increased to 90 to 250 from 80 to 240.

name: Tristana
rationale: Tristana is a little underrepresented and could do with a small buff and we'd like to ensure she has good late-game attack power, so we're bumping her AD growth.

lines.raw: Attack damage growth increased to 2.9 from 2.5.

name: Vladimir
rationale: We're continuing to identify ranged top laners who undeservedly gained laning dominance from our recent lane sustain changes, and Vladimir is next on that list of overperforming ranged tops. We're looking to make his matchups more interactive by giving more room for typically-physical melee champions to strike back during Vlad's moments of downtime. Also, the number 607 makes it uncomfortably easy to type 6-7 and we just can't have that.

lines.raw: Base health reduced to 600 from 607.
Base armor reduced to 24 from 27.

name: Volibear
rationale: Volibear's last patch succeeded in addressing his jungle-vs-top gap but left him a little weaker than we wanted across both roles. We're here to deliver him some more power to our favorite Zilean-hating demigod. We chose attack damage here to ensure that as a moderate-mobility melee champion, his attacks are appropriately threatening

lines.raw: Base attack damage increased to 65 from 62.

name: Xayah
rationale: While Rakan's been making waves, Xayah's been sitting on the sidelines for quite some time. We're looking to bring up her feather damage to help her cut through her opponents.

That said, we're still happy with where Top Mundo ended up, but Jungle Mundo is now a little over the line, so we're here to deliver a jungle-specific nerf to bring his two primary roles closer to parity.

name: Kayn
rationale: Shadow Assassin Kayn is a bit too good at taking down his targets at the moment so we're here this patch to give them a fighting chance. We don't want Rhaast to be caught in the crossfire of these nerfs so we're taking aim at some of Blue Kayn's assassin-specific damage that often comes in the form of W poke from the fog of war.

name: Kha'Zix
rationale: Kha'Zix is one of the strongest junglers at the moment and is in need of a nerf. We don't want to hurt his ability to assassinate targets, so instead we're going to slow down his jungle clear a touch by reducing his early AoE.

lines.raw: Base damage reduced to 75 to 195 from 85 to 205.

name: Master Yi
rationale: Master Yi is another powerful champion who's been dominating the jungle as of late. To level the playing field we're bringing down his durability and damage a bit split between the early and late game as we're currently happy with his overall combat and game pacing.

lines.raw: Base health reduced to 640 from 655.
Attack damage growth reduced to 2.5 from 2.8.

name: Mel
rationale: While not mathematically overpowered, Mel has solidified herself as the most frustrating champion to face in League, which is a deeper problem than just numbers. In the short term we're delivering a direct nerf that will still allow dedicated mains to win an appropriate number of games, but will make her suboptimal for inexperienced players. As for our changes themselves, we're going after how inescapable her E can feel to play against. In the longer term, we have some larger work planned for early next year with more significant changes aimed at returning her to a more appropriate power level while also making her feel more fair to play against for her opponents.

name: Nasus
rationale: Nasus has been an underdog for some time now so we're looking to throw him a bone with some changes that will make him a bit more durable in lane and powering up his Q for more effective stacking (because who hasn't missed a cannon minion by 5 health before).

name: Nidalee
rationale: Nidalee has risen up the ranks as an extremely high-powered jungler, largely due to a bug where her Q deals more damage than it should at most ranges. We’ve fixed this bug and will keep an eye on her to see how she lands.

rationale: Much like her fellow Freljordian tank, Sejuani is one of the weaker champions in the game right now, so we're here to deliver a shot in the arm with some cooldown buffs. While we're here, we're also taking a pass on making Top Sejuani and AP Sejuani more viable as well because who doesn't love a good AP Sejuani?

name: Viktor
rationale: Viktor's in need of a little more power right now, and we'd like to do that by leaning into his strengths as a mid-range battlemage. To do this we're increasing the shield on his Q so that he can stick it out better when going in to look for trades against opponents.

name: Zaahen
rationale: These changes went out as a micropatch during 25.23, but we wanted to capture them here for posterity and offer some thoughts on how we think Zaahen's release went. For 25.23, overall Zaahen released a bit too strong. His damage was a bit high and had room to go down while still feeling satisfying, so we decided to target that over other parts of his kit. We're being cautious here, so we're taking a little more time to see how he settles before we make additional changes, but we'll be keeping our eyes peeled and will make additional changes as needed. Now we’re at 25.24 and Zaahen is still a bit strong, particularly in higher ranks, so we’ve got some skill skewed changes here which should bring him down a bit. We also want to compensate his jungle a bit as we expect it to lose some power as a result of these changes, so we’re upping his Q’s monster damage mod.

name: Zed
rationale: One bar we want to hold for high-quality jungle gameplay is around exactly how quickly a champion can clear their own jungle and then reasonably invade their opponents. In Zed's case, he can clear his jungle to hit level 4 and invade you, or instead, Recall, buy two Long Swords, and then fight you for Rift Scuttler. Of course someone has to have the fastest clear in the game (that crown will move to Ivern most likely), but what they do with that speed is important, and the way Zed manifests his jungle strengths crosses the line. So this patch, we're slowing his early jungle clear speed by a few seconds, which we expect will make him too weak for many players. While we like the variety he brings to the game and jungle, we don't believe it can come at the cost of overall game health.

name: Akshan
rationale: Akshan's abilities currently scale crit in three different ways and we're making that more consistent here. His passive auto, being functionally a true basic attack, will crit for 100% value. Meanwhile, the crit scaling on E and R are going down as compensation. We're also doing some discretionary adjustments to allow Q-max and E-max to perform at similar levels of power by adjusting their rank-up incentives.

lines.attribute: Second shot now critically strikes at 100% effectiveness instead of 30%.
lines.raw: Second shot now critically strikes at 100% effectiveness instead of 30%.

name: Aphelios
rationale: Aphelios has a lot of intricacies and some of his abilities try to behave exactly like basic attacks. With that in mind, we're converting Severum's active to total attack damage in line with similar abilities and generally lowering the bonus AD ratios of several abilities that already scale well due to firing off basic attacks that can crit as part of their cast.

name: Ashe
rationale: Ashe is already quite attack-reliant and pretty balanced but considering she buys about 1.5 crit items per game, we're lowering her late game a little to make room for the increased damage coming her way.

lines.raw: Attack speed growth reduced to 3% from 3.33%.

Critical strike chance ratio increased to 0 to 100% from 0 to 75%.

lines.attribute: Bonus critical damage ratio unchanged at 100%.

name: Caitlyn
rationale: Caitlyn's top-end Headshot damage has gotten out of hand and with the value of critical strikes going up it's about to get even stronger, so we're taking a heavy swing to Headshot's top end. We're also making her R scale with Infinity Edge, as it already scales with critical strike chance, but we're reducing its damage to make room for her stronger basic attacks.

lines.raw: Critical strike chance ratio increased to 100% critical strike chance from 85%.

lines.attribute: Critical strike chance ratio formula now modifies critical damage instead of the total damage.
lines.raw: Critical strike chance ratio formula now modifies critical damage instead of the total damage.

lines.raw: New Effect: Damage now also scales with 0 to 30% bonus critical damage.

name: Cassiopeia
rationale: While Cassiopeia's no boots passive is very thematic, the addition of more boot based systems over the years (like role quest rewards) has made it feel like a punishment at times instead of a boon. We think it's important for Cassio to have the opportunity to engage with these new systems so we're reworking the passive into a new movement based effect. (We also wanted to do Soobin a solid.)

lines.raw: Movement speed increased to 335 from 328.

lines.raw: New Effect: Now increases the effectiveness of all movement speed bonuses by 6 to 40%.

name: Corki
rationale: Corki isn't particularly strong at the moment, so while this is a nerf on paper, we expect Corki will be overall stronger at the start of the season. This nerf is aimed at weakening his ability to crush a minion wave right before a Recall.

lines.raw: Base damage per tick reduced to 30 to 90 from 40 to 100.

name: Draven
rationale: Draven is very auto-attack focused and averages about two crit items per game, so he's also in need of some compensation. Considering he's gaining direct auto-attack DPS, we're trying to compensate him directly on the same axis.

lines.raw: Attack damage growth reduced to 3 from 3.6.
Bonus attack speed reduced to 20 to 40% from 30 to 50%.

name: Elise
rationale: Elise is in a silly spot where ability power quickly fails to scale her damage against monsters after the mid game. We're delivering a change that will be a slight buff on average but is primarily meant to let her damage scale up with AP like it would for anyone else.

name: Gangplank
rationale: Gangplank is one of two champions (alongside Smolder) who we think is going to gain extra power due to Essence Reaver once again building from Sheen. We expect him to perform much, much better with his increased critical strike damage, so we're pulling out many of the unique crit scalars that have been added over the years and delivering an extra hit to his E on top.

name: Garen
rationale: Critical strike chance on Garen is pretty good since both his basic attacks and Judgment are improved by it. We want to continue to make space for non-crit Garen builds, so we're compensating the global critical strike damage increase and updating the calculation to properly discount bonus crit damage.

name: Graves
rationale: The functional result of these Graves changes should be almost nothing. He'll deal about 1% more damage with his basic attacks when critically striking.

name: Jax
rationale: Now that the top lane quest can raise champion levels to 20, we're looking for any champions who intermittently scale their passives and giving them another breakpoint if they deserve one. Jax is one such champion who's gaining a bit more attack speed at level 19.

rationale: Jhin won't behave any differently next season as we want to avoid letting his guaranteed crit fourth shot do too much damage.

lines.raw: Total critical damage penalty increased to 25% from 14%.

name: Jinx
rationale: We like the overall shape of how Jinx functions and generally just want to preserve the value of her minigun's high attack speed, so we're making sure her two stances are more distinguished from one another and generally lowering a bit of spell damage to keep her attack-focused.

name: Kindred
rationale: Kindred's E mechanics are rather confusing and they build several critical strike items already. So we're updating the E to be much easier to understand and reducing the numbers. We're also modernizing the E's monster cap to allow for more damage when building AD and ranking up the ability.

name: Lucian
rationale: Lucian's builds are pretty sensible and as a spell-focused ADC, but we want to make sure his spell scaling is good. We're updating R to fire even more bullets with crit damage, which will make crit scale his ult just as well as it scales basic attacks. Considering he's already got extremely strong AD scaling and we want to make sure that Navori Flickerblades feels good, we're bringing down some of his Q's AD scaling.

name: Rengar
rationale: Rengar is getting a heavy re-script. This is mostly intended to maintain current functionality and feel, while addressing bugs and tech debt. The list of bug fixes is too long to add here so it'll be added to the bugs section. Alongside the crit changes, we're looking to make Rengar's Q work more intuitively by letting the underlying attack itself roll for critical strikes, and if so, deal bonus damage based on his total AD. This removes an optimization around rushing Infinity Edge to enhance the old forced-crit mechanic and also makes him not immediately lose 30% of his damage if his opponents build Randuin's Omen. We'll keep an eye on lethality-vs-crit Rengar and how it performs next season as we suspect Essence Reaver will be a big deal on him.

name: Tryndamere
rationale: Tryndamere is getting some real gameplay updates with this patch and some very real nerfs due to how much critical strike chance he normally has. To weaken how incredible his early game all-ins can be with 200% crit damage, we're nerfing his early bonus AD from Q and nerfing his early E as well. However, he's also getting some new tools. First, his Q now gives full value at 10% remaining health, meaning he can get the full bonus attack damage during his ultimate and it no longer has a disincentive for ranking up. Second, his W will now slow enemies any time they are running away from Tryndamere, regardless of where they were looking when he cast it. We expect this substantial increase in reliability is a big buff, so we've preemptively nerfed the slow itself. Though the slow duration is going down, the AD reduction is still the full four seconds regardless of facing.

name: Armored Advance
rationale: This year, we're introducing a major new concept to Summoner's Rift: Role Quests. Building off the item-based quests that junglers and support players have had for years, we're adding new lane-phase defining quests for the other three positions and updating the existing quests for support and jungle. You'll be automatically assigned the position quest corresponding to the role you've queued up as—if you want to trade positions, you'll need to do that during champion select. And the game will now reward playing out your lane matchup, at least for the first few minutes every game. This change will also help us better balance and tackle the pro play meta around lane swaps going forward, so no more LANE SWAP DETECTED pop ups. Every position will receive quest rewards for successfully completing their role quest. For top, mid, and bot lane players, these will be entirely new advantages. For support and jungle players, your existing rewards will be updated, and you'll be receiving some new rewards as well.

name: Spellslinger's Shoes
rationale: This year, we're introducing a major new concept to Summoner's Rift: Role Quests. Building off the item-based quests that junglers and support players have had for years, we're adding new lane-phase defining quests for the other three positions and updating the existing quests for support and jungle. You'll be automatically assigned the position quest corresponding to the role you've queued up as—if you want to trade positions, you'll need to do that during champion select. And the game will now reward playing out your lane matchup, at least for the first few minutes every game. This change will also help us better balance and tackle the pro play meta around lane swaps going forward, so no more LANE SWAP DETECTED pop ups. Every position will receive quest rewards for successfully completing their role quest. For top, mid, and bot lane players, these will be entirely new advantages. For support and jungle players, your existing rewards will be updated, and you'll be receiving some new rewards as well.

name: Baron Nashor
rationale: Baron Nashor is receiving a similar treatment to Elder Dragon, reducing its overall gold reward and ensuring the experience reward is impactful to drive those exciting moments where clutch objective steals lead into a teamfight comeback. We're preserving its buff power as a meaningful game-ender, though. We've also done a tuning pass on Baron's various abilities to ensure they're not weaker than his regular attacks so he lives up to his raid boss aura. His shred is also being empowered to consistently weaken all enemies around him, making the fight more lethal than before when an enemy team comes to contest. You thought pro teams were done throwing the game at 20 minute objective fights? Think again! Ultimately, Baron will be more durable than before and slightly more threatening, as his abilities will more accurately scale across game time and the increased shred will make the attacking team more prone to being more vulnerable to contests.

name: Voidgrubs
rationale: Void Grubs have generally been an epic monster camp that's more about getting yourself ahead and rewarding the whole team for running over to assist in the takedown. With this season's increased focus on pushing turrets, we think the buff already rewards that playstyle strongly, but we want to reduce the pressure on having whole teams roam up for Grubs. We also want to make it easier for laners to run over to take a single Void Grub and then leave back to their lane. To accomplish these goals, we're concentrating the gold reward purely on the killer of each monster and re-tuning the rewards to be more in line with our goals for camps like these. We're also reducing the camp's damage in order to make them less scary for non-junglers to engage with. As with most other epic monsters, their durability is increasing as well. As a point of clarification, the changes to Voidmites only affect the monster camp version and have no impact on the reward mites summoned from taking down the camp.

name: Aatrox
rationale: Aatrox has struggled to find a place on the Rift in the new season with split pushing on the rise and fewer chances to flex his team fighting strengths. We're giving him some additional power this patch, primarily in the jungle, where his growing audience has been kneecapped, as well as in the top lane where he could use more ways to benefit from experience. We hope this satiates Aatrox players, especially those with Endless Hunger.

name: Ashe
rationale: Ashe is underperforming in the new season so we’re here to bring her back up near her former power level. We like that she has a strong affinity for buying attack speed, so we’re just making those purchases multiply a little bit harder.

lines.raw: Attack damage growth increased to 3.5 from 3.

name: Gwen
rationale: Gwen jungle has skyrocketed in both pickrate and winrate. While we're excited to see her loving the new season and snipping from dusk til dawn, we need to make sure she's not turning all opponents (especially jungle camps) into paper.

lines.raw: Base monster damage cap reduced to 3 from 5.
Monster damage cap AP ratio reduced to 5% AP from 10% AP.

name: Jayce
rationale: Jayce jungle (AKA Jungle Jayce) has become extremely popular and is also much too strong. One of those two things is awesome and the other isn’t. We’d like to retain JJ as a viable option in the jungle, but without him dominating the competition. So we’re delivering a light nerf that’s intended to bring him more in line with other junglers.

lines.ability: Q - To the Skies / Shock Blast

lines.ability: Q - To the Skies / Shock Blast

name: Lillia
rationale: Lillia has been in a dream since the changes to Rift. Unfortunately we need to wake her up as it’s become a nightmare for her opponents. We want her to maintain her spot as our premier in-and-out skirmisher in the jungle, but without her prancing out of control. We are looking to nerf her ability to stay topped up as well as bring down some of her late game damage.

lines.raw: Monster heal AP ratio reduced to 9% AP from 15% AP.
AP ratio reduced to 30% AP from 35% AP.

name: Malphite
rationale: Malphite’s been a frontrunner on the Rift for a while, both in top and in the jungle. We’re actually very happy that he’s found a real audience in the jungle! That said, he’s still overperforming, so we need to bring him down now while still leaving him with two roles to play. To do that, we’re reducing some of his trading and clearing damage while retaining his high durability to physical damage and strong engage power. We’re also hitting jungle a little more as it’s meant to be slightly weaker than his top lane, as opposed to slightly stronger, which is currently the case.

name: Master Yi
rationale: Master Yi has been struggling as a result of the changes in the new season. We’re looking to return some of his power so that he can keep up with other junglers and better live up to his full hyper carry potential.

name: Nunu
rationale: Nunu & Willump are devouring the competition in the new season, so we’re here to bring them back to a fairer level of power. To do that, we’re reducing a mix of the PvP and PvE power out in their kits to give opponents a fighting chance.

name: Sivir
rationale: Sivir has become an extremely dominant ADC pick, regardless of whether or not she buys Essence Reaver, so it’s time to bring her down a notch. Since she has very strong wave control and great damage scaling, we’re looking to bring down her top end a little.

lines.raw: Armor growth reduced to 4 from 4.45.
Attack speed growth reduced to 1.6% from 2%.

name: Smolder
rationale: As expected Smolder has become much more powerful with the new Essence Reaver and increased minion counts. Since we’ve tuned our systems to our liking for now, it’s time to take stock of individual champions, Smolder being one. We want to make sure Smolder’s strong late-game damage has durability tradeoffs, even when buying the occasional HP item.

lines.raw: Armor growth reduced to 4 from 4.7.

name: Taliyah
rationale: Taliyah’s been missing from the jungle as of late and the gameplay changes for the new season didn’t help her, quite the opposite actually. To that end we want to get her rocking and rolling in the jungle again so we’re buffing up her mid game clear speed to help her out.

lines.raw: Bonus monster damage increased to 20 to 40 from 20 at all ranks.
Monster damage increased to 225% from 190%.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed a bug that caused the blind to not cause Rengar Ferocity empowered attacks to be consumed on use.

name: Varus
rationale: Varus isn’t doing very well in the new season so we’re here to lift up his two primary builds, on-hit and AD caster.

name: Viego
rationale: Viego is performing worse this season due to direct adjustments and overall game-wide changes. As a result he needs some power added back in, both compensating some crit scaling that he lost and generally just making him a better fighter.

lines.raw: Attack speed growth increased to 2.75% from 2.25%.

name: Zed
rationale: Zed’s recent jungle changes didn't affect him as strongly as we had anticipated, and players have noticed, resulting in a resurgence of pick and ban rate. We’d like to slow his clear and lower his potency, this time with more accuracy now that we have a better understanding of how to tune him in the jungle.

lines.raw: Monster damage reduced to 120% from 180%.

name: Bandlepipes
rationale: The pipes are sounding good on the rift but they're crowding out other support options due to their low price point. While we’re excited for their newfound popularity, we don’t want them to completely steal the spotlight.

lines.raw: Total cost increased to 2300 gold from 2000 gold.

name: Fiendhunter Bolts
rationale: Fiendhunter Bolts is doing what it's supposed to do, but it's not quite well enough to get picked over its competition. We’re buffing up a little bit all around on the Bolts to help it hold up better against the other Zeal items.

lines.raw: Attack speed increased to 45% from 40%.
Critical strike damage scaling increased to 80% from 75%.
Bonus true damage increased to 15% from 10%.

name: Hexoptics C44
rationale: Hexoptics has found a place in some situational builds for longer range champions, but is a bit too niche and a little weaker than needed for it to function for most of the marksman roster, so we’re giving it a general appreciable AD buff and easing the range requirement.

name: Ahri
rationale: As the new season has shaken out, Ahri is performing worse than last year and worse than she ought to. Now that she's back on high burst builds, we're reverting a nerf from her “Rod of Ages every game” phase of her K-pop career. Some artists just fall off, you know?

name: Bel'Veth
rationale: Bel'Veth is one of several AD junglers who suffered in the new season and we're here to buff her back up. We're aiming to bring up her late game in ways that synergize with squishy high attack speed builds by giving her a better payout for that attack speed and enough health to not need to buy as much of it.

lines.raw: Bug Fix: Fixed an issue where it would prevent the support item from properly executing minions.

name: Braum
rationale: Braum has easily become a top tier support with the start of the new season. New items like Bandlepipes have been instrumental in helping him and his allies stick onto enemies and take them down. Given that Braum is still looking quite strong even after the nerf to Bandlepiepes, we'll be looking to revert the health buffs we gave him at the end of last year and bring down some of his overall fighting power.

lines.raw: Base health reduced to 610 from 630.
Base damage reduced to 75 to 255 from 75 to 275.

name: Briar
rationale: Briar lost some of her luster in the new season and as someone with ample counter-play, she deserves to win more games than she currently does. We want to make sure her lifesteal-focused durability can manifest by giving her enough health and resists to make that healing efficient and while we're here, we're also throwing top lane Briar a bone by letting her trade more efficiently as well.
